title: BOJ. Two Circles (7869)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Geometry, Two Circles, 두 원
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/7869Intersection areaLet the circle centers be $C_1=(x_1,y_1)$ and $C_2=(x_2,y_2)$, their radii be $r_1,r_2$, and the distance between centers be$d=\sqrt{(x_1-x_2)^2+(y_1-y_2)^2}$. The intersection area depends on how the circles meet: If $d\ge r_1+r_2$, they are disjoint or externally tangent, so the intersection area is $0$. If $d\le r_1-r_2 $, one circle lies inside the other or they are internally tangent. The intersection is the smaller disk, with area $\pi\min(r_1,r_2)^2$. This also handles coincident centers ($d=0$), including equal circles, without dividing by $d$. Otherwise, the circles partially overlap and their boundaries intersect at two points.For partial overlap, draw radii to either intersection point. In the triangle formed by the two centers and that point, the cosine law gives the half-angles at the centers:\[\theta_1=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{d^2+r_1^2-r_2^2}{2dr_1}\right),\qquad\theta_2=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{d^2+r_2^2-r_1^2}{2dr_2}\right).\]Each circle contributes a sector with central angle $2\theta_i$. Subtracting the isosceles triangle inside that sector leaves a circular segment of area$r_i^2\theta_i-\frac12r_i^2\sin(2\theta_i)$. Adding the two segments gives the lens area:\[A=r_1^2\theta_1+r_2^2\theta_2-\frac12r_1^2\sin(2\theta_1)-\frac12r_2^2\sin(2\theta_2).\]Floating-point rounding can move a cosine-law value slightly outside its mathematical range, so clamp each acos argument to [-1, 1]. The containment and disjointness cases are tested first; consequently the partial-overlap formulas never divide by zero and tangencies are handled by the boundary cases.C++17 implementationThe algorithm uses constant time and constant extra space, $O(1)$ for both.#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;cmath&gt;#include &lt;iomanip&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;int main() { std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false); std::cin.tie(nullptr); double x1, y1, r1, x2, y2, r2; std::cin &gt;&gt; x1 &gt;&gt; y1 &gt;&gt; r1 &gt;&gt; x2 &gt;&gt; y2 &gt;&gt; r2; const double dx = x1 - x2; const double dy = y1 - y2; const double d = std::hypot(dx, dy); const double pi = std::acos(-1.0); double area; if (d &gt;= r1 + r2) { area = 0.0; } else if (d &lt;= std::abs(r1 - r2)) { const double radius = std::min(r1, r2); area = pi * radius * radius; } else { const double d2 = d * d; const double r1_2 = r1 * r1; const double r2_2 = r2 * r2; const double cos1 = std::clamp((d2 + r1_2 - r2_2) / (2.0 * d * r1), -1.0, 1.0); const double cos2 = std::clamp((d2 + r2_2 - r1_2) / (2.0 * d * r2), -1.0, 1.0); const double theta1 = std::acos(cos1); const double theta2 = std::acos(cos2); area = r1_2 * theta1 + r2_2 * theta2 - 0.5 * r1_2 * std::sin(2.0 * theta1) - 0.5 * r2_2 * std::sin(2.0 * theta2); } std::cout &lt;&lt; std::fixed &lt;&lt; std::setprecision(3) &lt;&lt; area &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}

title: BOJ 1069 - Going Home
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Geometry, Going Home
snippet: Problem linkLet $D_0=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ be the distance from the starting point to the target. Walking directly takes $D_0$ time. A jump always covers exactly $D$ distance, takes time $T$, and may be made in any direction; walking can cover any remaining distance.Write $q=\lfloor D_0/D\rfloor$ and $r=D_0-qD$, so $0\le r&lt;D$. The natural candidates are: Walk all the way: $D_0$. Make $q$ jumps toward the target, then walk the remaining $r$: $qT+r$. Make $q+1$ jumps in the target direction and walk back the overshoot $D-r$: $(q+1)T+D-r$. Reach the target using $q+1$ jumps: $(q+1)T$. For $q\ge1$, make $q-1$ jumps along the target direction, then use two jumps whose resultant displacement is $D+r$. Any resultant length from $0$ to $2D$ is possible with two length-$D$ jumps, and $D+r&lt;2D$. For $q=0$, two jumps can directly have resultant length $D_0&lt;D$, so the same time applies. These candidates cover the optimum. With $n\le q$ jumps, the remaining distance cannot be less than $D_0-nD$, so that strategy costs at least $nT+D_0-nD$, a linear function of $n$ whose minimum on this range occurs at $n=0$ or $n=q$. With at least $q+1$ jumps, the jump cost alone is at least $(q+1)T$, and that cost is achievable as described above. This also handles $q=0$; for one jump, the best remaining distance is $ D-D_0 =D-r$, and two jumps can reach the target. Thus the minimum of the listed candidates is valid, including when $D_0&lt;D$ or $r=0$. C++17 implementationhypot computes the Euclidean distance robustly. The running time and extra space are both $O(1)$.#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;cmath&gt;#include &lt;iomanip&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;int main() { std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false); std::cin.tie(nullptr); double x, y, jumpDistance, jumpTime; std::cin &gt;&gt; x &gt;&gt; y &gt;&gt; jumpDistance &gt;&gt; jumpTime; const double distance = std::hypot(x, y); const auto q = static_cast&lt;long long&gt;(std::floor(distance / jumpDistance)); const double remainder = distance - q * jumpDistance; double answer = distance; if (q == 0) { answer = std::min({answer, jumpTime + jumpDistance - distance, 2.0 * jumpTime}); } else { answer = std::min({answer, q * jumpTime + remainder, (q + 1) * jumpTime + jumpDistance - remainder, (q + 1) * jumpTime}); } std::cout &lt;&lt; std::fixed &lt;&lt; std::setprecision(10) &lt;&lt; answer &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}

title: BOJ. Crossing Lines (17386)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Outer Product, CCW, Geometry, Crossing Lines, 선분 교차 1
snippet: ProblemOrientation and segment intersectionFor points A, B, and C, define the signed orientationcross(A, B, C) = (B.x - A.x)(C.y - A.y) - (B.y - A.y)(C.x - A.x)A positive value means C is to the counterclockwise side of directed line AB; a negative value means clockwise; zero means the points are collinear.The input gives two segments AB and CD. The problem guarantees that no three of the four endpoints are collinear. Therefore the segments cannot touch at an endpoint or lie on a common line: any intersection must be a proper crossing through the interior of both segments. The segments cross exactly when A and B lie on opposite sides of line CD, and C and D lie on opposite sides of line AB. In orientation values, both pairs must have opposite signs.Checking both segments is important: opposite sides of only one infinite line do not by themselves prove that the finite segments intersect. The collinearity guarantee also means none of the four orientation values is zero, so strict sign comparisons are sufficient. Do not multiply the two cross products to compare signs, since that product can overflow even when each cross product fits in 64 bits.The coordinate limits are -1,000,000 &lt;= x, y &lt;= 1,000,000. Coordinate differences are at most 2,000,000, so a cross product has magnitude at most 8 × 10^12, which fits in a signed 64-bit integer. The algorithm uses O(1) time and O(1) extra space.C++17 implementation#include &lt;iostream&gt;using namespace std;struct Point { long long x, y;};long long cross(const Point&amp; a, const Point&amp; b, const Point&amp; c) { return (b.x - a.x) * (c.y - a.y) - (b.y - a.y) * (c.x - a.x);}bool oppositeSigns(long long a, long long b) { return (a &lt; 0 &amp;&amp; b &gt; 0) || (a &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; b &lt; 0);}int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); Point a, b, c, d; cin &gt;&gt; a.x &gt;&gt; a.y &gt;&gt; b.x &gt;&gt; b.y &gt;&gt; c.x &gt;&gt; c.y &gt;&gt; d.x &gt;&gt; d.y; const long long abC = cross(a, b, c); const long long abD = cross(a, b, d); const long long cdA = cross(c, d, a); const long long cdB = cross(c, d, b); cout &lt;&lt; (oppositeSigns(abC, abD) &amp;&amp; oppositeSigns(cdA, cdB));}

title: BOJ. Crossing Lines 2 (17387)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Outer Product, CCW, Geometry, Crossing Lines 2, 선분 교차 2
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/17387Idea: orientation tests and closed-segment boundsFor three points $P$, $Q$, and $R$, the sign of the cross product $(Q-P) \times (R-P)$ tells which side of the directed line $PQ$ contains $R$. A positive result means counterclockwise, a negative result clockwise, and zero means collinear.Let the segments be $AB$ and $CD$. If $C$ and $D$ lie on strictly opposite sides of line $AB$, and $A$ and $B$ lie on strictly opposite sides of line $CD$, the segments cross properly. “Strictly opposite” matters: a zero orientation is not a proper crossing and must be handled as a boundary case.For each zero orientation, check whether the collinear point lies inside the other segment’s closed bounding box: its x-coordinate and y-coordinate must each be between the corresponding endpoint coordinates, inclusively. This test is essential for collinear segments: lying on the same infinite line alone does not mean the finite segments overlap. The inclusive bounds accept endpoint contact and overlap, and reject separated collinear segments. Checking all four endpoint-on-segment cases also covers degenerate segments consisting of a single point.With coordinates in $[-10^9, 10^9]$, coordinate differences have magnitude at most $2 \cdot 10^9$. Each product in the cross product is at most $4 \cdot 10^{18}$ in magnitude, and their difference is at most $8 \cdot 10^{18}$, which fits in signed 64-bit integer range. The code stores coordinates and cross products as long long.Boundary checks: A proper crossing returns 1. Segments meeting at one endpoint return 1. Collinear segments with a shared endpoint or positive-length overlap return 1. Collinear segments with a gap return 0, even though all four points are collinear. A point segment on another segment returns 1; a point outside it returns 0.C++17#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;using namespace std;struct Point { long long x; long long y;};long long cross(const Point&amp; a, const Point&amp; b, const Point&amp; c) { return (b.x - a.x) * (c.y - a.y) - (b.y - a.y) * (c.x - a.x);}int orientation(const Point&amp; a, const Point&amp; b, const Point&amp; c) { const long long value = cross(a, b, c); if (value &gt; 0) return 1; if (value &lt; 0) return -1; return 0;}bool onSegment(const Point&amp; a, const Point&amp; b, const Point&amp; p) { return min(a.x, b.x) &lt;= p.x &amp;&amp; p.x &lt;= max(a.x, b.x) &amp;&amp; min(a.y, b.y) &lt;= p.y &amp;&amp; p.y &lt;= max(a.y, b.y);}bool intersects(const Point&amp; a, const Point&amp; b, const Point&amp; c, const Point&amp; d) { const int abC = orientation(a, b, c); const int abD = orientation(a, b, d); const int cdA = orientation(c, d, a); const int cdB = orientation(c, d, b); if (abC * abD &lt; 0 &amp;&amp; cdA * cdB &lt; 0) return true; if (abC == 0 &amp;&amp; onSegment(a, b, c)) return true; if (abD == 0 &amp;&amp; onSegment(a, b, d)) return true; if (cdA == 0 &amp;&amp; onSegment(c, d, a)) return true; if (cdB == 0 &amp;&amp; onSegment(c, d, b)) return true; return false;}int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); Point a, b, c, d; cin &gt;&gt; a.x &gt;&gt; a.y &gt;&gt; b.x &gt;&gt; b.y &gt;&gt; c.x &gt;&gt; c.y &gt;&gt; d.x &gt;&gt; d.y; cout &lt;&lt; (intersects(a, b, c, d) ? 1 : 0) &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}

title: BOJ. The Area Of The Polygon (2166)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Network Flow, CCW, Cross Product, The Area Of The Polygon, 다각형의 면적
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2166#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;#include &lt;stack&gt;#include &lt;cmath&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define FASTIO ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0)#define command_param int argc, char *argv[]#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define ll long long#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 2002;const int INF = 987654321;int n;vector&lt;pair&lt;int,int&gt;&gt; points;ll calc_size(pair&lt;int,int&gt; v1, pair&lt;int,int&gt; v2) { return (ll)v1.first * v2.second - (ll)v1.second * v2.first;}int main() { FASTIO; cin &gt;&gt; n; for0(i, n) { int x, y; cin &gt;&gt; x &gt;&gt; y; points.push_back(make_pair(x, y)); } double size = 0; for1(i, n - 1) { size += calc_size( { points[i].first - points[0].first, points[i].second - points[0].second }, { points[i+1].first - points[0].first, points[i+1].second - points[0].second } ); } cout &lt;&lt; fixed; cout.precision(1); cout &lt;&lt; (abs(size)/2); return 0;}

title: BOJ. Passionate Gang-Ho 4 (11378)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Network Flow, Edmonds Karf, Passionate Gang-Ho 4, 열혈강호 4
snippet: Problem linkModelThere are N workers and M jobs. Each worker has a list of jobs they are qualified to do. A worker may receive one job normally and at most one additional job. Across all workers, the number of additional assignments is at most K. Each job can be assigned to at most one worker. Maximize the total number of assigned jobs.Maximum-flow constructionCreate a source, one vertex per worker, a bonus vertex, one vertex per job, and a sink. Add these edges: source → each worker, capacity 1 (the worker’s normal assignment) source → bonus vertex, capacity K (the global additional-assignment limit) bonus vertex → each worker, capacity 1 (at most one additional assignment for that worker) each worker → every eligible job, capacity 1 each job → sink, capacity 1 (a job is assigned at most once)A worker can receive at most one unit through each of the two incoming routes, so at most two units total, and at most one of those units can be bonus flow. The bonus vertex can send at most K units in total. Thus a flow yields a valid assignment: each worker has at most two jobs, the total number beyond one per worker is at most the bonus flow and therefore at most K, and each job is used at most once. Conversely, for any valid assignment, route each worker’s first job through the direct source-to-worker edge and, if present, the second through the bonus vertex. This respects all capacities. Integral maximum flow therefore has the same value as the maximum feasible number of assignments.Algorithm and complexityDinic’s algorithm repeatedly builds a level graph with BFS and sends blocking flow along its level-respecting edges. When no source-to-sink path remains in the residual graph, the flow is maximum. Let A be the number of worker-job eligibility edges. This network has V = N + M + 3 vertices and E = A + 2N + M + 1 forward edges. The general time bound for Dinic is O(V^2 E) and its space use is O(V + E). The problem limits are N, M ≤ 1,000 and K ≤ N; no tighter worst-case bound specific to this network is assumed here.C++17 implementation#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;struct Dinic { struct Edge { int to; int rev; int cap; }; vector&lt;vector&lt;Edge&gt;&gt; graph; vector&lt;int&gt; level; vector&lt;int&gt; nextEdge; explicit Dinic(int n) : graph(n), level(n), nextEdge(n) {} void addEdge(int from, int to, int cap) { Edge forward{to, static_cast&lt;int&gt;(graph[to].size()), cap}; Edge reverse{from, static_cast&lt;int&gt;(graph[from].size()), 0}; graph[from].push_back(forward); graph[to].push_back(reverse); } bool buildLevels(int source, int sink) { fill(level.begin(), level.end(), -1); queue&lt;int&gt; q; level[source] = 0; q.push(source); while (!q.empty()) { int current = q.front(); q.pop(); for (const Edge&amp; edge : graph[current]) { if (edge.cap &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; level[edge.to] == -1) { level[edge.to] = level[current] + 1; q.push(edge.to); } } } return level[sink] != -1; } int sendFlow(int current, int sink, int pushed) { if (current == sink || pushed == 0) return pushed; for (int&amp; i = nextEdge[current]; i &lt; static_cast&lt;int&gt;(graph[current].size()); ++i) { Edge&amp; edge = graph[current][i]; if (edge.cap == 0 || level[edge.to] != level[current] + 1) continue; int sent = sendFlow(edge.to, sink, min(pushed, edge.cap)); if (sent == 0) continue; edge.cap -= sent; graph[edge.to][edge.rev].cap += sent; return sent; } return 0; } int maxFlow(int source, int sink) { int total = 0; while (buildLevels(source, sink)) { fill(nextEdge.begin(), nextEdge.end(), 0); while (int sent = sendFlow(source, sink, 1'000'000'000)) { total += sent; } } return total; }};int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int n, m, k; cin &gt;&gt; n &gt;&gt; m &gt;&gt; k; const int source = 0; const int bonus = n + 1; const int firstJob = n + 2; const int sink = n + m + 2; Dinic dinic(sink + 1); for (int worker = 1; worker &lt;= n; ++worker) { dinic.addEdge(source, worker, 1); } dinic.addEdge(source, bonus, k); for (int worker = 1; worker &lt;= n; ++worker) { dinic.addEdge(bonus, worker, 1); } for (int worker = 1; worker &lt;= n; ++worker) { int count; cin &gt;&gt; count; while (count--) { int job; cin &gt;&gt; job; dinic.addEdge(worker, firstJob + job - 1, 1); } } for (int job = 0; job &lt; m; ++job) { dinic.addEdge(firstJob + job, sink, 1); } cout &lt;&lt; dinic.maxFlow(source, sink) &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}

title: BOJ. Maximum Flow (6086)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Network Flow, Edmonds Karp, Maximum Flow, 최대 유량
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/6086#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;#include &lt;stack&gt;#include &lt;cmath&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define FASTIO ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0)#define command_param int argc, char *argv[]#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define ll long long#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 5e5 + 1;const int INF = 987654321;int n;int capacity[52][52];int flow[52][52];vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; adj;int convert(char ch) { return ch &gt; 'Z' ? ch - 'a' + 26 : ch - 'A';}int solve() { queue&lt;int&gt; q; int flow_max = 0; while(1) { q = {}; q.push(0); int prev[52]; fill(prev, prev + 52, -1); while(!q.empty()) { int cur = q.front(); q.pop(); if(cur == 25) break; for(int next : adj[cur]) { if(prev[next] == -1 &amp;&amp; capacity[cur][next] - flow[cur][next]) { q.push(next); prev[next] = cur; } } } if(prev[25] == -1) break; int min_flow = INF; for(int s = 25; s != 0; s = prev[s]) { min_flow = min(min_flow, capacity[prev[s]][s] - flow[prev[s]][s]); } for(int s = 25; s != 0; s= prev[s]) { flow[prev[s]][s] += min_flow; flow[s][prev[s]] -= min_flow; } flow_max += min_flow; } return flow_max;}int main() { FASTIO; cin &gt;&gt; n; adj.resize(52); for0(i, n) { char from, to; int c; cin &gt;&gt; from &gt;&gt; to &gt;&gt; c; int cfrom = convert(from), cto = convert(to); capacity[cfrom][cto] += c; capacity[cto][cfrom] += c; adj[cfrom].push_back(cto); adj[cto].push_back(cfrom); } cout &lt;&lt; solve(); return 0;}

title: BOJ. Passionate Gang-Ho 2 (11376)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Network Flow, Bipartite Matching, Passionate Gang-Ho 2, 열혈강호2
snippet: ProblemModelThere are N workers and M jobs. Each worker lists the jobs they can do. Assign each job to at most one worker, and assign at most two jobs to each worker; maximize the number of assigned jobs.Make a bipartite graph with two matching slots for each worker. Connect both slots to exactly the jobs that worker can do. A matching uses each slot and each job at most once, so a worker receives at most two jobs and no job is assigned twice. Conversely, any valid assignment can place a worker’s two (or fewer) assigned jobs into their two slots. Thus the maximum matching size is exactly the desired answer.Augmenting pathsProcess every slot with a standard augmenting-path search. For one search, mark jobs rather than slots. When a candidate job is already matched, recursively try to move its current slot to another eligible job. If that succeeds, give the candidate job to the current slot. A job is visited at most once in a search, which prevents cycles; successful reassignment preserves the matching invariant. By the augmenting-path theorem, processing all left-side slots this way produces a maximum matching.There are 2N slots and E worker-job eligibility edges (counted once per worker). One DFS takes O(E) time, so the total time is O(N E). The graph and matching arrays use O(N + M + E) space.C++17#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int n, m; cin &gt;&gt; n &gt;&gt; m; vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; jobs(n); for (int worker = 0; worker &lt; n; ++worker) { int count; cin &gt;&gt; count; jobs[worker].resize(count); for (int&amp; job : jobs[worker]) { cin &gt;&gt; job; --job; } } // matchedSlot[job] is the slot currently assigned to this job. vector&lt;int&gt; matchedSlot(m, -1); vector&lt;char&gt; visitedJob(m); auto augment = [&amp;](auto&amp;&amp; self, int slot) -&gt; bool { for (int job : jobs[slot / 2]) { if (visitedJob[job]) continue; visitedJob[job] = true; if (matchedSlot[job] == -1 || self(self, matchedSlot[job])) { matchedSlot[job] = slot; return true; } } return false; }; int assigned = 0; for (int slot = 0; slot &lt; 2 * n; ++slot) { fill(visitedJob.begin(), visitedJob.end(), false); if (augment(augment, slot)) ++assigned; } cout &lt;&lt; assigned &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}The recursion only changes ownership along an augmenting path, so each successful search increases the matching by exactly one while keeping every job and slot unique.

title: BOJ. Passionate Gang-Ho (11375)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Network Flow, Bipartite Matching, Passionate Gang-Ho, 열혈강호
snippet: BOJ 11375: Passionate Gang-HoApproach: bipartite matchingTreat each worker as a vertex on the left and each job as a vertex on the right. Draw an edge from a worker to every job they can do. A valid assignment is a matching: no worker and no job can appear in more than one selected edge. The answer is the maximum matching cardinality.Process workers one at a time and search for an augmenting path with depth-first search. For the current worker, try each eligible job that has not yet been visited in this search. If the job is free, assign it. If it is already assigned, recursively try to move its current worker to another eligible job. When that succeeds, the current worker can take the job. This reassignment is what lets a later search improve an earlier choice instead of leaving a usable job blocked.The visited array is indexed by jobs and is reset before each starting worker. Mark a job as visited before following its current assignment; this prevents cycles and ensures each job is considered at most once in that search. A successful search increases the matching size by exactly one, while a failed search leaves it unchanged.The input gives the number of workers N and jobs M, followed by one line per worker: the number of jobs they can do and those job IDs (numbered from 1). Print the maximum number of workers that can be assigned. Each worker and job can be used at most once.With this DFS implementation, each search takes O(E) time in the worst case, where E is the number of eligibility edges. Running one search for each worker takes O(N E) time; the graph and matching use O(N + M + E) memory.C++17#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; eligibleJobs;vector&lt;int&gt; assignedWorker;vector&lt;bool&gt; visitedJob;bool findAssignment(int worker) { for (int job : eligibleJobs[worker]) { if (visitedJob[job]) continue; visitedJob[job] = true; if (assignedWorker[job] == -1 || findAssignment(assignedWorker[job])) { assignedWorker[job] = worker; return true; } } return false;}int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int workerCount, jobCount; cin &gt;&gt; workerCount &gt;&gt; jobCount; eligibleJobs.resize(workerCount); assignedWorker.assign(jobCount, -1); for (int worker = 0; worker &lt; workerCount; ++worker) { int count; cin &gt;&gt; count; eligibleJobs[worker].resize(count); for (int&amp; job : eligibleJobs[worker]) { cin &gt;&gt; job; --job; } } int matchingSize = 0; for (int worker = 0; worker &lt; workerCount; ++worker) { visitedJob.assign(jobCount, false); if (findAssignment(worker)) ++matchingSize; } cout &lt;&lt; matchingSize &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/16163#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;#include &lt;stack&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define ll long long#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 5e5 + 1;const int INF = 987654321;string s;ll ans = 0;void solve() { int l_odd = 0, r_odd = -1; int l_even = 0, r_even = -1; vector&lt;int&gt; odd(s.size(), 1); vector&lt;int&gt; even(s.size(), 0); for(int i = 0; i &lt; s.size(); i++) { if(i &lt;= r_odd) odd[i] = min(r_odd - i + 1, odd[l_odd+r_odd-i]); if(i &lt;= r_even) even[i] = min(r_even - i, even[l_even+r_even - i - 1]); while(i-odd[i]&gt;=0 &amp;&amp; i+odd[i]&lt;s.size() &amp;&amp; s[i-odd[i]] == s[i+odd[i]]) odd[i]++; while(i-even[i]&gt;=0 &amp;&amp; i+even[i]+1&lt;s.size() &amp;&amp; s[i-even[i]] == s[i+even[i]+1]) even[i]++; if(i + odd[i] - 1 &gt; r_odd) { r_odd = i + odd[i] - 1; l_odd = i - odd[i] + 1; } if(i + even[i] &gt; r_even) { r_even = i + even[i]; l_even = i + 1 - even[i]; } ans += (odd[i] + even[i]); }}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; s; solve(); cout &lt;&lt; ans; return 0;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1854#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;#include &lt;stack&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define ll long long#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 5e5 + 1;const int INF = 987654321;int n, m, k;vector&lt;map&lt;int, int&gt;&gt; time;int update_cnt[1000];int dijk[1000];struct cmp { bool operator()(pair&lt;int, int&gt; p1, pair&lt;int, int&gt; p2) { return p1.first &gt; p2.first; }};int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n &gt;&gt; m &gt;&gt; k; time.resize(n); for0(i, m) { int a, b, c; cin &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b &gt;&gt; c; a--, b--; time[a][b] = c; } priority_queue&lt;pair&lt;int, int&gt;, vector&lt;pair&lt;int,int&gt;&gt;, cmp&gt; pq; dijk[0] = 0; pq.push({ 0, 0 }); while(!pq.empty()) { pair&lt;int,int&gt; p = pq.top(); pq.pop(); int v = p.first, idx = p.second; if(update_cnt[idx] &gt;= k) continue; update_cnt[idx]++; dijk[idx] = v; for(auto map_p: time[idx]) { int dest = map_p.first, edge_val = map_p.second; if(update_cnt[dest] &gt;= k) continue; pq.push({ v + edge_val, dest }); } } for0(i, n) { if(update_cnt[i] &lt; k) cout &lt;&lt; -1 &lt;&lt; endl; else cout &lt;&lt; dijk[i] &lt;&lt; endl; } return 0;}

title: Tree Investment
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Implementation, Tree Investment, 나무 재테크
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/16235Each year runs in a fixed order: spring, summer, autumn, then winter. In spring, trees in each cell are processed from youngest to oldest. A tree consumes food equal to its age and then grows by one. If the cell cannot feed a tree, that tree and every older tree still waiting in that cell die; processing stops there. In summer, each dead tree returns floor(age / 2) food to its cell. Autumn trees whose age is a multiple of five produce one age-one tree in each of the eight neighboring cells that are inside the farm. Finally, winter adds the scheduled food to every cell.Each cell stores tree ages in a sorted vector, youngest first. Spring scans from the front. As soon as food is insufficient, the current tree and all unprocessed (older) trees are dead; sum their food return from the back and shrink the vector to keep only survivors. This avoids erasing from the middle while preserving the correct death rule. Autumn offspring are counted in a separate grid so that newborns do not reproduce in the same autumn. They are inserted at the front, preserving age order for next spring.There are at most N * N cells and K &lt;= 1000 years (N &lt;= 10). Let T_y be the number of living trees entering year y. Each year visits O(N^2) cells and processes each tree a constant number of times, including at most eight neighbor checks per reproducing tree. Newborns are collected per cell and inserted into each sorted vector in one batch; because each reproducing tree creates at most eight newborns, total insertion work is also bounded by the number of trees processed that year. The running time is O(N^2*K + sum_y T_y) and storage is O(N^2 + T_max). Tree counts can grow rapidly, so complexity cannot be bounded by N, M, and K alone without accounting for population size.C++17#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int n, m, years; cin &gt;&gt; n &gt;&gt; m &gt;&gt; years; vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; winterFood(n, vector&lt;int&gt;(n)); for (auto&amp; row : winterFood) { for (int&amp; food : row) cin &gt;&gt; food; } vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; food(n, vector&lt;int&gt;(n, 5)); vector&lt;vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt;&gt; trees(n, vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt;(n)); for (int i = 0; i &lt; m; ++i) { int row, column, age; cin &gt;&gt; row &gt;&gt; column &gt;&gt; age; trees[--row][--column].push_back(age); } for (auto&amp; row : trees) { for (auto&amp; cell : row) sort(cell.begin(), cell.end()); } constexpr int dr[8] = {-1, -1, -1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1}; constexpr int dc[8] = {-1, 0, 1, -1, 1, -1, 0, 1}; vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; deadFood(n, vector&lt;int&gt;(n)); for (int year = 0; year &lt; years; ++year) { for (int r = 0; r &lt; n; ++r) { for (int c = 0; c &lt; n; ++c) { auto&amp; cell = trees[r][c]; int alive = 0; deadFood[r][c] = 0; while (alive &lt; static_cast&lt;int&gt;(cell.size()) &amp;&amp; food[r][c] &gt;= cell[alive]) { food[r][c] -= cell[alive]; ++cell[alive]; ++alive; } for (int i = static_cast&lt;int&gt;(cell.size()) - 1; i &gt;= alive; --i) { deadFood[r][c] += cell[i] / 2; } cell.resize(alive); } } for (int r = 0; r &lt; n; ++r) { for (int c = 0; c &lt; n; ++c) food[r][c] += deadFood[r][c]; } vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; offspring(n, vector&lt;int&gt;(n)); for (int r = 0; r &lt; n; ++r) { for (int c = 0; c &lt; n; ++c) { for (int age : trees[r][c]) { if (age % 5 != 0) continue; for (int d = 0; d &lt; 8; ++d) { const int nr = r + dr[d]; const int nc = c + dc[d]; if (0 &lt;= nr &amp;&amp; nr &lt; n &amp;&amp; 0 &lt;= nc &amp;&amp; nc &lt; n) { ++offspring[nr][nc]; } } } } } for (int r = 0; r &lt; n; ++r) { for (int c = 0; c &lt; n; ++c) { trees[r][c].insert(trees[r][c].begin(), offspring[r][c], 1); food[r][c] += winterFood[r][c]; } } } int answer = 0; for (const auto&amp; row : trees) { for (const auto&amp; cell : row) answer += cell.size(); } cout &lt;&lt; answer &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/7453#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define ll long long#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 5e5 + 1;int n;vector&lt;int&gt; a, b, c, d;int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n; a.resize(n); b.resize(n); c.resize(n); d.resize(n); for0(i, n) cin &gt;&gt; a[i] &gt;&gt; b[i] &gt;&gt; c[i] &gt;&gt; d[i]; sort(a.begin(), a.end()); sort(b.begin(), b.end()); sort(c.begin(), c.end()); sort(d.begin(), d.end()); vector&lt;int&gt; ab, cd; for0(i, n) { for0(j, n) { ab.push_back(a[i] + b[j]); cd.push_back(c[i] + d[j]); } } sort(ab.begin(), ab.end()); sort(cd.begin(), cd.end()); int ab_idx = 0, cd_idx = cd.size() - 1; ll cnt = 0; while(ab_idx &lt; ab.size() &amp;&amp; cd_idx &gt;= 0) { int ab_val = ab[ab_idx], cd_val = cd[cd_idx]; int sum = ab_val + cd_val; if(sum == 0) { int abcnt = 1, cdcnt = 1; while(ab_idx + 1 &lt; ab.size() &amp;&amp; ab[ab_idx + 1] == ab_val) { abcnt++; ab_idx++; } while(cd_idx - 1 &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; cd[cd_idx - 1] == cd_val) { cdcnt++; cd_idx--; } cnt+=(ll)abcnt * cdcnt; ab_idx++; cd_idx--; } else if(sum &gt; 0) cd_idx--; else ab_idx++; } cout &lt;&lt; cnt; return 0;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/11000#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define ll long long#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 5e5 + 1;int n;bool cmp(pair&lt;int, bool&gt; pl, pair&lt;int, bool&gt; pr) { if(pl.first == pr.first) return pl.second == pr.second ? false : (!pl.second || pr.second); return pl.first &lt; pr.first;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n; vector&lt;pair&lt;int, bool&gt;&gt; schedule; for0(i, n) { int s, t; cin &gt;&gt; s &gt;&gt; t; schedule.push_back({ s, true }); schedule.push_back({ t, false }); } sort(schedule.begin(), schedule.end(), cmp); int cnt = 0, max_val = 0; for(auto e: schedule) { if(e.second) cnt++; else cnt--; max_val = max(max_val , cnt); } cout &lt;&lt; max_val; return 0;}

title: LeetCode. 1028. Recover a Tree From Preorder Traversal
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, C++, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Divide And Conquer, Recover a Tree From Preorder Traversal
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/recover-a-tree-from-preorder-traversal/#include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;/** * Definition for a binary tree node. * struct TreeNode { * int val; * TreeNode *left; * TreeNode *right; * TreeNode() : val(0), left(nullptr), right(nullptr) {} * TreeNode(int x) : val(x), left(nullptr), right(nullptr) {} * TreeNode(int x, TreeNode *left, TreeNode *right) : val(x), left(left), right(right) {} * }; */class Solution {public: vector&lt;pair&lt;int,int&gt;&gt; nodes; TreeNode* div_con(int l, int r) { if(l == r) return new TreeNode(nodes[l].first); else if(l+1 == r) { TreeNode *child_node = new TreeNode(nodes[r].first); return new TreeNode(nodes[l].first, child_node, nullptr); } int top_depth = nodes[l].second; vector&lt;int&gt; next_nodes; for(int i = l+1; i &lt;= r; i++) { if(nodes[i].second == top_depth + 1) next_nodes.push_back(i); } if(next_nodes.size() == 1) { return new TreeNode(nodes[l].first, div_con(next_nodes[0], r), nullptr); } else if(next_nodes.size() == 2) { return new TreeNode(nodes[l].first,div_con(next_nodes[0], next_nodes[1] - 1), div_con(next_nodes[1], r)); } return new TreeNode(nodes[l].first); } TreeNode* recoverFromPreorder(string s) { int i = 0, depth = 0, tot = 0; string str; while(i &lt; s.size()) { depth = 0; str = ""; while(s[i]=='-') { depth++; i++; } while(i &lt; s.size() &amp;&amp; s[i]!='-') str+=s[i++]; int node_val = stoi(str); nodes.push_back({ node_val, depth }); TreeNode* node = new TreeNode(node_val); tot++; } return div_con(0, tot - 1); }};

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2517#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 5e5 + 1;int n;int seg[MAX &lt;&lt; 1];vector&lt;int&gt; abilities;void insert(int ability) { for(ability+=MAX; ability &gt; 0; ability&gt;&gt;=1) seg[ability]++;}int query(int ability) { int rank = 0; for(int l = MAX, r = MAX + ability; l &lt; r; l&gt;&gt;=1, r&gt;&gt;=1) { if(l &amp; 1) rank += seg[l++]; if(r &amp; 1) rank += seg[--r]; } return rank;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); // freopen("input.txt", "r", stdin); cin &gt;&gt; n; int cur_rank = 1; for0(i, n) { int ability; cin &gt;&gt; ability; abilities.push_back(ability); } vector&lt;int&gt; cp = abilities; sort(cp.begin(), cp.end(), greater&lt;int&gt;()); for0(i, n) { int rank = lower_bound(cp.begin(), cp.end(), abilities[i], greater&lt;int&gt;()) - cp.begin(); cout &lt;&lt; min(query(rank), i) + 1 &lt;&lt; endl; insert(rank); } return 0;}

title: BOJ. Candy Box (2243)

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2243#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "const int MAX = 1e6 + 1;const int log = 20;const NUM = 1e6;int n;int seg[1 &lt;&lt; log+1];void update(int v, int amount, int idx, int l, int r) { if(r &lt; v || v &lt; l) return; int mid = l+r&gt;&gt;1; seg[idx]+=amount; if(l == r) return; update(v, amount, idx&lt;&lt;1, l, mid); update(v, amount, idx&lt;&lt;1|1, mid + 1, r);}int pull(int rank) { int seg_idx = 1, l = 1, r = NUM; while(l != r) { int left_cnt = seg[seg_idx&lt;&lt;1]; if(left_cnt &gt;= rank) { seg_idx&lt;&lt;=1; r = l+r&gt;&gt;1; } else { rank -= left_cnt; seg_idx = seg_idx&lt;&lt;1|1; int mid = l+r&gt;&gt;1; l = mid + 1; } } update(l, -1, 1, 1, NUM); return l;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); // freopen("input.txt", "r", stdin); cin &gt;&gt; n; while(n--) { int a, b; cin &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b; if(a == 1) { cout &lt;&lt; pull(b) &lt;&lt; endl; } else { int c; cin &gt;&gt; c; update(b, c, 1, 1, NUM); } } return 0;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/9934#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;cstring&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"#define nulls '\0'#define dkdk " "int k;// vector&lt;int&gt; ans;vector&lt;int&gt; record;void conquer(vector&lt;int&gt; *ans, int left, int right, int idx) { if(left == right) { (*ans)[idx-1] = record[left - 1]; return; } int mid = (left + right) &gt;&gt; 1; (*ans)[idx-1] = record[mid - 1]; conquer(ans, left, mid - 1, 2*idx); conquer(ans, mid + 1, right, 2*idx+1);}void solve(vector&lt;int&gt; *ans) { ans-&gt;resize((1 &lt;&lt; k) - 1); conquer(ans, 1, (1 &lt;&lt; k) - 1, 1);}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); // freopen("input.txt", "r", stdin); cin &gt;&gt; k; int i = (1 &lt;&lt; k) - 1; while(i--) { int in; cin &gt;&gt; in; record.push_back(in); } i = 0; vector&lt;int&gt; ans; solve(&amp;ans); int stair = 1; int idx = 0; for(int stair = 1; stair &lt;= k; stair++) { for0(i, 1 &lt;&lt; (stair-1)) cout &lt;&lt; ans[idx++] &lt;&lt; dkdk; cout &lt;&lt; endl; } return 0;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/16437#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"typedef long long ll;const int INF = 987654321;const int MAX = 123456;const int log = 17;int n;ll sheep[MAX];int deg[MAX];vector&lt;int&gt; bridge;int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n; bridge.resize(n); for0(i, n-1) { char t; int a, p; cin &gt;&gt; t &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; p; p--; deg[p]++; sheep[i+1] = t == 'S' ? a : -a; bridge[i+1] = p; } queue&lt;int&gt; q; for0(i, n) if(deg[i] == 0) q.push(i); while(!q.empty()) { int cur = q.front(); q.pop(); if(cur == 0) continue; int next = bridge[cur]; if(sheep[cur] &gt; 0) sheep[next] += sheep[cur]; if(--deg[next] == 0) q.push(next); } cout &lt;&lt; sheep[0]; return 0;}

title: BOJ. Distance Between Vertices (1761)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, LCA, Lowest Common Ancestor, Distance Between Vertices, 정점들의 거리
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1761#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"typedef long long ll;const int INF = 987654321;const int MAX = 4e4 + 1;const int log = 17;int n, m;vector&lt;vector&lt;pair&lt;int, int&gt;&gt;&gt; edges;int dis[MAX][log];int parent[MAX][log];int depth[MAX];void get_root_dfs(int idx) { for(pair&lt;int,int&gt; p: edges[idx]) { if(parent[idx][0] == p.first) continue; parent[p.first][0] = idx; depth[p.first] = depth[idx] + 1; dis[p.first][0] = p.second; get_root_dfs(p.first); }}void calc_sparse() { for1(i, log) { for1(j, n + 1) { parent[j][i] = parent[parent[j][i - 1]][i - 1]; dis[j][i] = dis[j][i-1] + dis[parent[j][i-1]][i-1]; } }}int get_lca(int a, int b) { if(depth[a] &lt; depth[b]) swap(a, b); for(int i = log - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { if(depth[a] - depth[b] &gt;= 1 &lt;&lt; i) { a = parent[a][i]; } } if(a == b) return a; for(int i = log - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { if(parent[a][i] != parent[b][i]) { a = parent[a][i]; b = parent[b][i]; } } return parent[a][0];}int get_dis(int child, int anc) { int distance = 0; for(int i = log - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { if(depth[child] - depth[anc] &gt;= 1 &lt;&lt; i) { distance += dis[child][i]; child = parent[child][i]; } } return distance;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n; edges.resize(n + 1); for0(i, n-1) { int a, b, dis; cin&gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b &gt;&gt; dis; edges[a].push_back(make_pair(b, dis)); edges[b].push_back(make_pair(a, dis)); } get_root_dfs(1); calc_sparse(); cin &gt;&gt; m; for0(i, m) { int a, b; cin &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b; int lca = get_lca(a, b); cout &lt;&lt; get_dis(a, lca) + get_dis(b, lca) &lt;&lt; endl; } return 0;}

title: BOJ 1240 — Distance Between Nodes
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Tree, Graph, DFS
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1240 — Distance Between Nodes · 한국어 · 日本語The input is a tree, so there is exactly one path between any two vertices. Therefore, the shortest-path distance is simply the sum of the edge weights along that unique path; no general shortest-path algorithm is needed.For each query, traverse from its starting vertex with an explicit stack. Each stack entry carries the current vertex, its parent, and the distance accumulated from the start. Skip the parent edge so the traversal does not go back across an already-used edge. When the target is reached, print its accumulated distance and stop that query’s traversal. This is iterative, so even a chain-shaped tree does not consume the call stack.Input vertex labels are 1-based and can be used directly with arrays sized N + 1. The given edge weights are at most 10,000, and N &lt;= 1,000, so any path contains at most 999 edges and has length at most 9,990,000. A 64-bit integer safely stores the accumulated distance. The graph and traversal stack use O(N) memory; processing all M queries takes O(NM) time in the worst case.C++17#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;tuple&gt;#include &lt;utility&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int n, m; cin &gt;&gt; n &gt;&gt; m; vector&lt;vector&lt;pair&lt;int, int&gt;&gt;&gt; graph(n + 1); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; ++i) { int a, b, weight; cin &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b &gt;&gt; weight; graph[a].push_back({b, weight}); graph[b].push_back({a, weight}); } while (m--) { int start, target; cin &gt;&gt; start &gt;&gt; target; vector&lt;tuple&lt;int, int, long long&gt;&gt; pending; pending.emplace_back(start, 0, 0); while (!pending.empty()) { auto [node, parent, distance] = pending.back(); pending.pop_back(); if (node == target) { cout &lt;&lt; distance &lt;&lt; '\n'; break; } for (auto [next, weight] : graph[node]) { if (next != parent) { pending.emplace_back(next, node, distance + weight); } } } }}

title: BOJ. Cheese (2636)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, BFS, Implementation, Cheese, 치즈
snippet: ProblemApproachAt the start of each hour, flood-fill the empty cells reachable from the paddedoutside border. Any cheese cell adjacent to this exterior air melts during thathour. Collect all such cells first, then remove them together; cheese exposedonly after this removal must wait until the next hour.Keep the total cheese count before each melting round. When a round removes thelast cheese, that saved count is the number immediately before the finalmelting hour. An initially empty board needs no rounds, so the answer is 0hours and 0 cheese.C++17#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;utility&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int rows, cols; cin &gt;&gt; rows &gt;&gt; cols; // The extra empty border guarantees a safe exterior-air starting cell. vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; cheese(rows + 2, vector&lt;int&gt;(cols + 2, 0)); int remaining = 0; for (int r = 1; r &lt;= rows; ++r) { for (int c = 1; c &lt;= cols; ++c) { cin &gt;&gt; cheese[r][c]; remaining += cheese[r][c]; } } int hours = 0; int beforeLastMelt = 0; const int dr[] = {-1, 1, 0, 0}; const int dc[] = {0, 0, -1, 1}; while (remaining &gt; 0) { beforeLastMelt = remaining; vector&lt;vector&lt;char&gt;&gt; visited(rows + 2, vector&lt;char&gt;(cols + 2, false)); vector&lt;vector&lt;char&gt;&gt; melts(rows + 2, vector&lt;char&gt;(cols + 2, false)); queue&lt;pair&lt;int, int&gt;&gt; air; vector&lt;pair&lt;int, int&gt;&gt; toMelt; air.push({0, 0}); visited[0][0] = true; while (!air.empty()) { auto [r, c] = air.front(); air.pop(); for (int d = 0; d &lt; 4; ++d) { int nr = r + dr[d]; int nc = c + dc[d]; if (nr &lt; 0 || nr &gt;= rows + 2 || nc &lt; 0 || nc &gt;= cols + 2) { continue; } if (cheese[nr][nc]) { if (!melts[nr][nc]) { melts[nr][nc] = true; toMelt.push_back({nr, nc}); } } else if (!visited[nr][nc]) { visited[nr][nc] = true; air.push({nr, nc}); } } } // Apply this hour's melt only after the exterior-air search is complete. for (auto [r, c] : toMelt) { cheese[r][c] = 0; } remaining -= static_cast&lt;int&gt;(toMelt.size()); ++hours; } cout &lt;&lt; hours &lt;&lt; '\n' &lt;&lt; beforeLastMelt &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}For H melting rounds on an R × C board, each round visits O(R·C) cells,so the running time is O(H·R·C). The board, visit/melt markers, and workqueues use O(R·C) space.

title: BOJ. Is This Tree? (6416)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Tree, Is This Tree, 트리인가
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/6416#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"typedef long long ll;const int INF = 987654321;const int MAX = 123456;const int log = 17;int n;map&lt;int, int&gt; deg;map&lt;int, vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; edges;set&lt;int&gt; v;bool bfs(int root) { queue&lt;int&gt; q; q.push(root); set&lt;int&gt; visit_set; bool is_tree = true; int v_cnt = 0; while(!q.empty()) { int cur = q.front(); q.pop(); if(visit_set.count(cur)) { is_tree = false; break; } visit_set.insert(cur); v_cnt++; for(int child: edges[cur]) q.push(child); } return is_tree ? v_cnt == v.size() : false;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); bool end = false; int case_idx = 1; while(true) { deg.clear(); edges.clear(); v.clear(); while(true) { int a, b; cin &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b; if(!a &amp;&amp; !b) break; if(a == -1 &amp;&amp; b == -1) { end = true; break; } v.insert(a); v.insert(b); edges[a].push_back(b); deg[b]++; } if(end) break; if(!v.size()) { cout &lt;&lt; "Case " &lt;&lt; case_idx++ &lt;&lt; " is a tree." &lt;&lt; endl; continue; } int zero_deg_cnt = 0, root = 0; for(int vertex: v) if(deg[vertex] == 0) { zero_deg_cnt++; root = vertex; } if(zero_deg_cnt != 1) cout &lt;&lt; "Case " &lt;&lt; case_idx++ &lt;&lt; " is not a tree." &lt;&lt; endl; else { if(bfs(root)) cout &lt;&lt; "Case " &lt;&lt; case_idx++ &lt;&lt; " is a tree." &lt;&lt; endl; else cout &lt;&lt; "Case " &lt;&lt; case_idx++ &lt;&lt; " is not a tree." &lt;&lt; endl; } } return 0;}

title: BOJ. Factory (7578)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Segment Tree, Non-Recursive Segement Tree, Factory, 공장
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/7578#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"typedef long long ll;const int INF = 987654321;const int MAX = 100;const int N = 5e5;int n;vector&lt;int&gt; seg(2*N);vector&lt;int&gt; idx_vec;void insert(int val) { int idx = N + val; seg[idx]++; while(idx &gt; 1) { idx &gt;&gt;= 1; seg[idx] = seg[idx &lt;&lt; 1] + seg[idx &lt;&lt; 1 | 1]; }}int get(int val) { int ans = 0; for(int l = N + val, r = 2 * N; l &lt; r; l&gt;&gt;=1, r&gt;&gt;=1) { if(l &amp; 1) ans+=seg[l++]; if(r &amp; 1) ans+=seg[--r]; } return ans;}void solve() { ll ans = 0; for(int e: idx_vec) { ans += get(e); insert(e); } cout &lt;&lt; ans;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n; idx_vec.resize(n); map&lt;int, int&gt; number_idx; for0(i, n) { int in; cin &gt;&gt; in; number_idx[in] = i; } for0(i, n) { int in; cin &gt;&gt; in; idx_vec[number_idx[in]] = i; } solve();}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/15685#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"typedef long long ll;const int INF = 987654321;const int MAX = 100;int n, m, ans = 0;vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; sub;vector&lt;int&gt; sum;bool mm[101][101];int cx, cy;int dx[4] = { 1, 0, -1, 0 };int dy[4] = { 0, -1, 0, 1 };vector&lt;int&gt; directions;void draw(int generation) { fori(i, generation) { int start_idx = directions.size(); for(int i = start_idx - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { int dir = directions[i]; if(++dir == 4) dir = 0; cx += dx[dir], cy += dy[dir]; if(0 &lt;= cx &amp;&amp; 0 &lt;= cy &amp;&amp; cx &lt;= 100 &amp;&amp; cy &lt;= 100) mm[cx][cy] = true; directions.push_back(dir); } }}int count() { int ans = 0; for0(i, 100) { for0(j, 100) { if(mm[i][j] &amp;&amp; mm[i+1][j] &amp;&amp; mm[i][j+1] &amp;&amp; mm[i+1][j+1]) ans++; } } return ans;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n; for0(i, n) { int d, g; cin &gt;&gt; cx &gt;&gt; cy &gt;&gt; d &gt;&gt; g; directions.clear(); mm[cx][cy] = true; cx += dx[d], cy += dy[d]; mm[cx][cy] = true; directions.push_back(d); draw(g); } cout &lt;&lt; count() &lt;&lt; endl;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/14267#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"typedef long long ll;const int INF = 987654321;const int MAX = 100;int n, m, ans = 0;vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; sub;vector&lt;int&gt; sum;void propagate(int idx, int inc) { sum[idx] += inc; for(int sub_idx : sub[idx]) { propagate(sub_idx, sum[idx]); }}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n &gt;&gt; m; sub.resize(n); sum.resize(n); fill(sum.begin(), sum.end(), 0); for0(i, n) { int super; cin &gt;&gt; super; if(super == -1) continue; super--; sub[super].push_back(i); } for0(i, m) { int emp, compli; cin &gt;&gt; emp &gt;&gt; compli; sum[--emp] += compli; } propagate(0, 0); for(int v : sum) cout &lt;&lt; v &lt;&lt; " "; return 0;}

snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/13325#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;#include &lt;map&gt;#include &lt;set&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;// #include &lt;bits/stdc++.h&gt;using namespace std;#define for0(i, n) for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)#define for1(i, n) for(int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++)#define fori(s, e) for(int i = s; i &lt; e; i++)#define endl "\n"typedef long long ll;const int INF = 987654321;const int MAX = 100;int n, m, ans = 0;vector&lt;int&gt; edges;int dfs(int idx) { if(idx &lt;&lt; 1 &gt;= (1 &lt;&lt; n+1)) return 0; int dfs_left = dfs(idx &lt;&lt; 1), dfs_right = dfs(idx &lt;&lt; 1 | 1); int max_val = max(dfs_left + edges[idx &lt;&lt; 1], dfs_right + edges[idx &lt;&lt; 1 | 1]); edges[idx &lt;&lt; 1] += max_val - (dfs_left + edges[idx &lt;&lt; 1]); edges[idx &lt;&lt; 1 | 1] += max_val - (dfs_right + edges[idx &lt;&lt; 1 | 1]); return max_val;}int main() { ios_base::sync_with_stdio(0); cin.tie(0); cout.tie(0); cin &gt;&gt; n; edges.push_back(0); edges.push_back(0); for0(i, (1 &lt;&lt; n+1) - 2) { int in; cin &gt;&gt; in; edges.push_back(in); } dfs(1); long sum = 0l; for0(i, 1 &lt;&lt; n+1) sum+=edges[i]; cout &lt;&lt; sum; return 0;}

title: BOJ. Slope (14890)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Implementation, Slope, 경사로
snippet: Problem: BOJ 14890 — Slope · 한국어 · 日本語A runway can be built on a row or column when every height change between neighboring cells is exactly 0 or 1, and each height difference of 1 can be covered by a length-L ramp. A ramp occupies L cells on the lower side of the height change. Those cells must all have the same height, stay within the line, and not have been used by another ramp.Validate one line from left to right while tracking which cells already hold a ramp. Equal neighboring heights need no action. For an upward step, the lower side is the L cells immediately before the step; for a downward step, it is the L cells beginning at the next cell. Check bounds, equal heights across that segment, and overlap before marking the cells as used. This explicit occupancy check prevents consecutive descents from reusing the same cells. A height difference greater than 1, an unavailable segment, or any overlap makes the line invalid. Run this validator on every row and every column.Each segment can hold a ramp only once. The two sides of a ramp transition must have equal height, while adjacent height differences greater than 1 are always invalid. With N &lt;= 100, checking up to L cells for each of N transitions in each of 2N lines takes O(N^2 * L) time. The height grid uses O(N^2) space, and the line plus ramp-occupancy scratch uses O(N) space.C++17#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;bool canBuildRunway(const vector&lt;int&gt;&amp; line, int length) { const int n = static_cast&lt;int&gt;(line.size()); vector&lt;bool&gt; used(n, false); for (int i = 0; i + 1 &lt; n; ++i) { const int difference = line[i + 1] - line[i]; if (difference == 0) continue; if (difference &lt; -1 || difference &gt; 1) return false; const int start = difference == 1 ? i - length + 1 : i + 1; const int end = difference == 1 ? i : i + length; if (start &lt; 0 || end &gt;= n) return false; const int lowerHeight = difference == 1 ? line[i] : line[i + 1]; for (int cell = start; cell &lt;= end; ++cell) { if (line[cell] != lowerHeight || used[cell]) return false; } for (int cell = start; cell &lt;= end; ++cell) { used[cell] = true; } } return true;}int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int n, length; cin &gt;&gt; n &gt;&gt; length; vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; height(n, vector&lt;int&gt;(n)); for (auto&amp; row : height) { for (int&amp; cell : row) cin &gt;&gt; cell; } int answer = 0; vector&lt;int&gt; line(n); for (int row = 0; row &lt; n; ++row) { if (canBuildRunway(height[row], length)) ++answer; } for (int column = 0; column &lt; n; ++column) { for (int row = 0; row &lt; n; ++row) { line[row] = height[row][column]; } if (canBuildRunway(line, length)) ++answer; } cout &lt;&lt; answer &lt;&lt; '\n'; return 0;}

title: BOJ. LCA (11437)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Tree, Lowest Common Ancestor, LCA
snippet: Problem: BOJ 11437 — Lowest Common Ancestor · 한국어 · 日本語Root the tree at node 1. An iterative breadth-first traversal records each node’s depth and its immediate parent; the root’s parent is 0, a sentinel whose ancestors are also 0. Because the input is a tree, each non-root node is reached from exactly one parent. Using a queue instead of recursive DFS keeps traversal safe even when the tree is a chain of 50,000 nodes.Let ancestor[v][j] be the node reached by moving 2^j edges upward from v. The immediate-parent traversal fills level 0; then ancestor[v][j] = ancestor[ancestor[v][j - 1]][j - 1] builds each higher level. The sentinel makes this recurrence valid at the root as well.For a query, first lift the deeper node by the depth difference so both nodes are at the same level. If they are now equal, that node is the LCA. Otherwise, inspect jump levels from largest to smallest, moving both nodes upward whenever their ancestors at that level differ. They then sit immediately below their lowest common ancestor, so their immediate parent is the answer.Preprocessing takes O(N log N) time and memory; each query takes O(log N) time.C++17#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;queue&gt;#include &lt;utility&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int n; cin &gt;&gt; n; vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; graph(n + 1); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; ++i) { int a, b; cin &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b; graph[a].push_back(b); graph[b].push_back(a); } constexpr int LOG = 17; // 2^16 &gt;= 50,000 vector&lt;int&gt; depth(n + 1, -1); vector&lt;vector&lt;int&gt;&gt; ancestor(LOG, vector&lt;int&gt;(n + 1, 0)); queue&lt;int&gt; pending; depth[1] = 0; pending.push(1); while (!pending.empty()) { int node = pending.front(); pending.pop(); for (int next : graph[node]) { if (next == ancestor[0][node]) { continue; } ancestor[0][next] = node; depth[next] = depth[node] + 1; pending.push(next); } } for (int level = 1; level &lt; LOG; ++level) { for (int node = 1; node &lt;= n; ++node) { ancestor[level][node] = ancestor[level - 1][ancestor[level - 1][node]]; } } auto lca = [&amp;](int a, int b) { if (depth[a] &lt; depth[b]) { swap(a, b); } int difference = depth[a] - depth[b]; for (int level = 0; level &lt; LOG; ++level) { if (difference &amp; (1 &lt;&lt; level)) { a = ancestor[level][a]; } } if (a == b) { return a; } for (int level = LOG - 1; level &gt;= 0; --level) { if (ancestor[level][a] != ancestor[level][b]) { a = ancestor[level][a]; b = ancestor[level][b]; } } return ancestor[0][a]; }; int queries; cin &gt;&gt; queries; while (queries--) { int a, b; cin &gt;&gt; a &gt;&gt; b; cout &lt;&lt; lca(a, b) &lt;&lt; '\n'; }}

title: BOJ. Phone Number List (5052)
tags: C++, Algorithm, BOJ, Sort, Phone Number List, 전화번호 목록
snippet: Problem: BOJ 5052 — Phone Number List · 한국어 · 日本語Sort all phone numbers in lexicographic order, then inspect each adjacent pair. If one number is a prefix of another, the shorter number sorts immediately before the longer one: at the first position after the shorter number ends, the longer one still has a digit, which makes it sort later. Thus any prefix conflict appears in an adjacent pair. Equal strings also count as a prefix conflict, and the prefix comparison below correctly detects them.The list is rebuilt for every test case, so no number or conflict state carries over between cases. The sort takes O(N log N * L) time when comparing strings of maximum length L; the adjacent scan takes O(NL). Storing the numbers takes O(NL) space.C++17#include &lt;algorithm&gt;#include &lt;iostream&gt;#include &lt;string&gt;#include &lt;vector&gt;using namespace std;int main() { ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); int test_cases; cin &gt;&gt; test_cases; while (test_cases--) { int n; cin &gt;&gt; n; vector&lt;string&gt; numbers(n); for (string&amp; number : numbers) { cin &gt;&gt; number; } sort(numbers.begin(), numbers.end()); bool consistent = true; for (int i = 0; i + 1 &lt; n; ++i) { if (numbers[i + 1].compare(0, numbers[i].size(), numbers[i]) == 0) { consistent = false; break; } } cout &lt;&lt; (consistent ? "YES" : "NO") &lt;&lt; '\n'; }}
