title: Codeforces Round 771 (Div. 2) A. Reverse
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Codeforces Round, Div 2, Codeforces, Reverse
snippet: Problem: Codeforces 1638A — Reverse · 한국어 · 日本語The array is a permutation of 1..n. We may choose one segment and reverse it; the goal is to make the permutation lexicographically smallest.Scan from left to right to find the first index i where p[i] != i + 1. Every earlier position already contains its smallest possible value, so it must stay fixed. The value i + 1 occurs somewhere to the right; let its position be j. Reversing [i, j] moves i + 1 to the first mismatching position while leaving the already-correct prefix unchanged. This is the lexicographically smallest possible result.If no mismatch exists, the permutation is already sorted, so reversing a length-one segment leaves it unchanged. Finding the mismatch and the target value takes O(n) time, and the input permutation uses O(n) space per test case.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int ptr; private int len; private int read() throws IOException { if (ptr == len) { len = in.read(buffer); ptr = 0; if (len == -1) return -1; } return buffer[ptr++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner fs = new FastScanner(); int tests = fs.nextInt(); StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); while (tests-- &gt; 0) { int n = fs.nextInt(); int[] permutation = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { permutation[i] = fs.nextInt(); } int left = 0; while (left &lt; n &amp;&amp; permutation[left] == left + 1) { left++; } if (left &lt; n) { int right = left; while (permutation[right] != left + 1) { right++; } while (left &lt; right) { int value = permutation[left]; permutation[left++] = permutation[right]; permutation[right--] = value; } } for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { if (i &gt; 0) answer.append(' '); answer.append(permutation[i]); } answer.append('\n'); } System.out.print(answer); }}

title: BOJ. 2-SAT - 4 (11281)
tags: Java, Algorithm, BOJ, SCC, Graph, Strongly Connected Component, 2-SAT - 4
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/11281Iterative Kosaraju for 2-SATEach input clause (a ∨ b) is equivalent to the implications ¬a → b and ¬b → a. Represent every signed literal as a vertex: positive literal x uses index x - 1, and negative literal ¬x uses index N + x - 1. Its negation is the vertex index ^ N. Store every implication in both the graph and its reverse graph.A formula is unsatisfiable exactly when some variable and its negation belong to the same strongly connected component: each literal then implies the other, forcing both truth values at once. Otherwise, process strongly connected components with Kosaraju’s algorithm. The first pass records finishing order in the original graph; the second pass visits vertices in reverse finishing order in the reversed graph. Both passes below use explicit stacks, so even a long implication chain cannot overflow the Java call stack.The component IDs are assigned in the order the second pass discovers components. With this traversal order, every edge between distinct components goes from a smaller ID to a larger ID in the original implication graph. Therefore, set variable x to true exactly when component(x) &gt; component(¬x). This is the reverse-topological assignment rule for this particular numbering; reversing the pass order or numbering convention would require reversing the comparison too.The first pass uses a per-vertex next-edge index to simulate recursive DFS and append a vertex only after all outgoing edges have been explored. The second pass marks each vertex when it is pushed, preventing duplicate stack entries. Each vertex and implication is examined a constant number of times, so the time and space complexities are both O(N + M).import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int pointer; private int length; private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = in.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[pointer++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } } private static int literalIndex(int literal, int n) { return literal &gt; 0 ? literal - 1 : n - literal - 1; } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int m = input.nextInt(); int vertexCount = 2 * n; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[vertexCount]; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] reverseGraph = new ArrayList[vertexCount]; for (int vertex = 0; vertex &lt; vertexCount; vertex++) { graph[vertex] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); reverseGraph[vertex] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int clause = 0; clause &lt; m; clause++) { int a = input.nextInt(); int b = input.nextInt(); int notA = literalIndex(-a, n); int indexA = literalIndex(a, n); int notB = literalIndex(-b, n); int indexB = literalIndex(b, n); graph[notA].add(indexB); reverseGraph[indexB].add(notA); graph[notB].add(indexA); reverseGraph[indexA].add(notB); } boolean[] visited = new boolean[vertexCount]; int[] nextEdge = new int[vertexCount]; int[] stack = new int[vertexCount]; int[] order = new int[vertexCount]; int orderSize = 0; for (int start = 0; start &lt; vertexCount; start++) { if (visited[start]) { continue; } int top = 0; stack[top++] = start; visited[start] = true; while (top &gt; 0) { int vertex = stack[top - 1]; if (nextEdge[vertex] &lt; graph[vertex].size()) { int next = graph[vertex].get(nextEdge[vertex]++); if (!visited[next]) { visited[next] = true; stack[top++] = next; } } else { order[orderSize++] = vertex; top--; } } } int[] component = new int[vertexCount]; int componentCount = 0; for (int index = orderSize - 1; index &gt;= 0; index--) { int start = order[index]; if (component[start] != 0) { continue; } int top = 0; stack[top++] = start; component[start] = ++componentCount; while (top &gt; 0) { int vertex = stack[--top]; for (int next : reverseGraph[vertex]) { if (component[next] == 0) { component[next] = componentCount; stack[top++] = next; } } } } for (int variable = 0; variable &lt; n; variable++) { if (component[variable] == component[variable + n]) { System.out.println(0); return; } } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder("1\n"); for (int variable = 0; variable &lt; n; variable++) { output.append(component[variable] &gt; component[variable + n] ? '1' : '0'); if (variable + 1 &lt; n) { output.append(' '); } } output.append('\n'); System.out.print(output); }}

title: AtCoder. Regular Contest 135 C XOR to All
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, XOR, Regular Contest
snippet: [Link] https://AtCoder.jp/contests/arc135/tasks/arc135_cIdeaFor each index i, compute sum_j (A[i] XOR A[j]), then take the maximum over all i. Consider one bit position b at a time. If bit b of A[i] is zero, its XOR has that bit set exactly for the count[b] array elements whose bit is one. If its bit is one, the XOR has that bit set for the other N - count[b] elements. Thus the contribution of this bit is 2^b times the corresponding count, and summing these contributions over all bit positions gives the requested sum for i.The values are at most 10^8, so 30 bit positions (0 through 29) cover every value. The input values and bit counts are stored once, then each value is evaluated across all 30 bits. The running answer is a long; use 1L &lt;&lt; b so the bit weight and its product are computed as long, not overflowing as int. Initializing the maximum to zero handles arrays containing zero as well as cases where every candidate sum is zero. The time complexity is O(N * B) for B = 30; auxiliary space is O(B) beyond the stored input array.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { private static final int BITS = 30; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine()); String[] tokens = input.readLine().split(" "); int[] values = new int[n]; int[] bitCount = new int[BITS]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { values[i] = Integer.parseInt(tokens[i]); for (int bit = 0; bit &lt; BITS; bit++) { if ((values[i] &amp; (1 &lt;&lt; bit)) != 0) { bitCount[bit]++; } } } long answer = 0; for (int value : values) { long sum = 0; for (int bit = 0; bit &lt; BITS; bit++) { int ones = (value &amp; (1 &lt;&lt; bit)) == 0 ? bitCount[bit] : n - bitCount[bit]; sum += (1L &lt;&lt; bit) * ones; } answer = Math.max(answer, sum); } System.out.println(answer); }}

title: AtCoder. Regular Contest 135 B Sum of Three Terms
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, XOR, Regular Contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ARC 135 B — Sum of Three Terms · 한국어 · 日本語We are given an array A of length N. We must determine whether there is a nonnegative integer array B of length N + 2 such thatA[i] = B[i] + B[i + 1] + B[i + 2]for every 0 &lt;= i &lt; N. If one exists, print Yes and any such array; otherwise print No.Subtract two consecutive equations:A[i + 1] - A[i] = B[i + 3] - B[i].Thus, for each residue modulo 3, the values of B form an independent chain: once its first value is chosen, every later value in that chain is determined by the differences of A. For residue r, define prefix[r] as the cumulative sum of these differences along the chain, including the initial sum 0. Then every value in that chain is B[r] + prefix[r]. It is nonnegative exactly when B[r] is at least -minPrefix[r].Choose the smallest possible starting values for residues 0 and 1: B[0] = -minPrefix[0] and B[1] = -minPrefix[1]. The first equation requires B[0] + B[1] + B[2] = A[0], so it forces B[2] = A[0] - B[0] - B[1]. If B[2] &lt; -minPrefix[2], no solution is possible: the minimum required starting values for all three chains already sum to more than A[0]. Otherwise all chains are nonnegative, and the recurrence constructs a valid B.This reasoning also covers N = 1: there are no differences, all three minimum prefixes are zero, and any nonnegative split of A[0] works. In particular, when A[0] is zero the constructed values are all zero.The algorithm processes each adjacent pair of A once, so its time complexity is O(N). It stores A and the constructed array, using O(N) space. long is used for differences, prefix sums, and constructed values.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); long[] a = new long[n]; StringTokenizer tokens = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { a[i] = Long.parseLong(tokens.nextToken()); } long[] prefix = new long[3]; long[] minPrefix = new long[3]; for (int i = 0; i + 1 &lt; n; i++) { int residue = i % 3; prefix[residue] += a[i + 1] - a[i]; minPrefix[residue] = Math.min(minPrefix[residue], prefix[residue]); } long[] b = new long[n + 2]; b[0] = -minPrefix[0]; b[1] = -minPrefix[1]; b[2] = a[0] - b[0] - b[1]; if (b[2] &lt; -minPrefix[2]) { System.out.println("No"); return; } for (int i = 0; i + 3 &lt; n + 2; i++) { b[i + 3] = b[i] + a[i + 1] - a[i]; } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder("Yes\n"); for (int i = 0; i &lt; b.length; i++) { if (i &gt; 0) { output.append(' '); } output.append(b[i]); } System.out.println(output); }}

title: AtCoder. Regular Contest 135 A Floor, Ceil Decomposition
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, Regular Contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ARC 135 A — Floor, Ceil Decomposition[English] · 한국어 · 日本語For a positive integer x, define f(x) = x when x &lt;= 4. Otherwise, split x into floor(x / 2) and ceil(x / 2), and define f(x) as the product of their values modulo 998244353:f(x) = f(floor(x / 2)) * f(ceil(x / 2)) mod 998244353.The split makes both arguments smaller, so the recurrence eventually reaches the base cases. Memoized recursion avoids recomputing the same arguments. At each recursion depth, the values are only the rounded halves of the original input, so there are at most two distinct values per depth. Thus there are O(log x) distinct states, recursion depth is O(log x), and the memo table uses O(log x) space.Reduce each recursive result modulo 998244353 before multiplying. Since each factor is less than the modulus, their product is less than 998244353², which fits in a signed Java long. Computing the upper half as x / 2 + x % 2 also avoids overflowing x + 1.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.HashMap;import java.util.Map;public class Main { private static final long MOD = 998244353L; private static final Map&lt;Long, Long&gt; memo = new HashMap&lt;&gt;(); public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); long x = Long.parseLong(input.readLine().trim()); System.out.println(value(x)); } private static long value(long x) { if (x &lt;= 4) { return x; } Long cached = memo.get(x); if (cached != null) { return cached; } long lower = x / 2; long upper = lower + x % 2; long result = value(lower) * value(upper) % MOD; memo.put(x, result); return result; }}

title: Codeforces Global Round 19 B. MEX and Array
tags: Java, Algorithm, Codeforces, Codeforces Global Round, MEX and Array, Math
snippet: Problem: Codeforces 1637B — MEX and Array · 한국어 · 日本語For an array, a partition splits it into contiguous non-empty segments. Its cost is the number of segments plus the sum of the MEX of each segment, and the array’s value is the maximum such cost. We must sum the values of every non-empty subsegment of the given array.The official constraints are 1 &lt;= t &lt;= 30, 1 &lt;= n &lt;= 100, and 0 &lt;= a[i] &lt;= 10^9; the sum of n over all test cases is at most 100. In particular, values may be zero or much larger than n.Value of one subsegmentFor a subsegment of length m containing z zeroes, its value is exactly m + z.To see the upper bound, consider any one segment of a partition, with length L, containing q zeroes. If its MEX is x, then it contains every integer from 0 to x - 1. Thus it has at least x elements, and when x &gt; 0 it contains at least one zero. In either case, 1 + x &lt;= L + q. Summing this inequality over all partition segments bounds the cost by the total length plus the total number of zeroes, namely m + z.This bound is attainable by partitioning into single-element segments: a nonzero element has MEX 0 and contributes 1, while a zero has MEX 1 and contributes 2. The resulting cost is m + z, proving the claim.Sum over all subsegmentsThere are (n - k + 1) subsegments of length k, so summing their lengths givessum(k * (n - k + 1), k = 1..n) = n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) / 6.Each zero at zero-based index i belongs to exactly (i + 1) * (n - i) subsegments: choose the subsegment’s left endpoint from the i + 1 positions up to i, and its right endpoint from the n - i positions starting at i. Therefore the full answer isn * (n + 1) * (n + 2) / 6 + sum((i + 1) * (n - i)) over all indices where a[i] == 0.So the formula in the original implementation is correct for the official statement. The answer is accumulated in long; at n &lt;= 100 it is well within range. The algorithm takes O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space per test case.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int ptr; private int len; private int read() throws IOException { if (ptr == len) { len = in.read(buffer); ptr = 0; if (len == -1) return -1; } return buffer[ptr++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner fs = new FastScanner(); int tests = fs.nextInt(); StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); while (tests-- &gt; 0) { int n = fs.nextInt(); long valueSum = (long) n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) / 6; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { if (fs.nextInt() == 0) { valueSum += (long) (i + 1) * (n - i); } } answer.append(valueSum).append('\n'); } System.out.print(answer); }}

title: BOJ. Idol (3648)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, SCC, Strongly Connected Component, Idol, 아이돌, Review, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 3648 — Idol · 한국어 · 日本語For each test case, Karl must satisfy all clauses and variable 1 must be true. A clause (a OR b) is represented by the implications ¬a → b and ¬b → a. The required truth of variable 1 is the unit clause (1 OR 1), which adds ¬1 → 1 just like any other clause.The input contains signed literals. For n variables, the 2n graph vertices are indexed from 0 to 2n - 1: positive literal i maps to i - 1, and negative literal -i maps to n + i - 1. Negation swaps the two halves of this index range. Each implication is stored in both the graph and its reverse graph.Kosaraju’s algorithm finds strongly connected components using two iterative DFS passes. In the first pass, the stack stores both the current vertex and the index of its next outgoing edge; a vertex is appended to finishing order only after all its edges have been processed. This simulates recursive DFS without using the call stack, so a long implication chain cannot overflow it. The second pass visits the reverse graph in decreasing finishing order and assigns component IDs. The formula is satisfiable exactly when no variable and its negation share a component.Each case has 2n vertices and 2m + 2 implication edges, including the two edges for (1 OR 1). The algorithm takes O(n + m) time and space per case. Cases are read until EOF, and each answer is printed as lowercase yes or no.Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int length; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); if (c == -1) { return Integer.MIN_VALUE; } int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } } private static int literalIndex(int literal, int n) { int variable = Math.abs(literal) - 1; return literal &gt; 0 ? variable : variable + n; } private static int negation(int vertex, int n) { return vertex &lt; n ? vertex + n : vertex - n; } @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") private static boolean satisfiable(int n, int m, FastScanner input) throws IOException { int vertices = 2 * n; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[vertices]; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] reverse = new ArrayList[vertices]; for (int v = 0; v &lt; vertices; v++) { graph[v] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); reverse[v] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int i = 0; i &lt;= m; i++) { int a; int b; if (i == m) { a = literalIndex(1, n); b = a; } else { a = literalIndex(input.nextInt(), n); b = literalIndex(input.nextInt(), n); } int notA = negation(a, n); int notB = negation(b, n); graph[notA].add(b); reverse[b].add(notA); graph[notB].add(a); reverse[a].add(notB); } boolean[] visited = new boolean[vertices]; int[] order = new int[vertices]; int orderSize = 0; int[] stackVertex = new int[vertices]; int[] stackNext = new int[vertices]; for (int start = 0; start &lt; vertices; start++) { if (visited[start]) { continue; } int top = 0; stackVertex[top] = start; stackNext[top] = 0; visited[start] = true; while (top &gt;= 0) { int v = stackVertex[top]; if (stackNext[top] &lt; graph[v].size()) { int next = graph[v].get(stackNext[top]++); if (!visited[next]) { visited[next] = true; stackVertex[++top] = next; stackNext[top] = 0; } } else { order[orderSize++] = v; top--; } } } int[] component = new int[vertices]; int componentId = 0; int[] stack = new int[vertices]; for (int i = orderSize - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { int start = order[i]; if (component[start] != 0) { continue; } componentId++; int top = 0; stack[top++] = start; component[start] = componentId; while (top &gt; 0) { int v = stack[--top]; for (int next : reverse[v]) { if (component[next] == 0) { component[next] = componentId; stack[top++] = next; } } } } for (int variable = 0; variable &lt; n; variable++) { if (component[variable] == component[variable + n]) { return false; } } return true; } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); while (true) { int n = input.nextInt(); if (n == Integer.MIN_VALUE) { break; } int m = input.nextInt(); output.append(satisfiable(n, m, input) ? "yes" : "no").append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); }}

title: Codeforces Global Round 19 C. Andrew and Stones
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Codeforces Global Round, Codeforces, Andrew and Stones
snippet: Problem: Codeforces 1637C — Andrew and Stones · 한국어 · 日本語In one operation, choose indices i &lt; j &lt; k such that pile j has at least two stones, remove two stones from pile j, and add one stone to each of piles i and k. The goal is to leave stones only in the first and last piles.Minimum operationsEach operation is centered on exactly one interior pile and removes two stones from it. If a pile starts with a[i] stones and receives r stones from other operations, then emptying it requires 2 * moves[i] = a[i] + r. Thus moves[i] &gt;= ceil(a[i] / 2), and the total number of operations is at least the sum of these ceilings.For n &gt; 3, the lower bound is attainable unless every interior pile initially contains exactly one stone. When at least one interior pile has two or more stones, use it to start a sequence of operations and exploit the freedom to choose non-adjacent outer indices: route one incoming stone to each odd remainder that needs parity correction, while sending any other recipient to an endpoint. It is never necessary to add a stone to the same odd pile more than once. This lets each pile be centered exactly ceil(a[i] / 2) times. If every interior pile is one, no operation is possible initially, so the goal cannot be reached.For n = 3, the only triple is (1, 2, 3). The middle pile loses two stones each time, so its parity never changes. An odd middle value can never reach zero; an even value requires exactly a[1] / 2 operations.The official constraints are 3 &lt;= n &lt;= 100000 and 1 &lt;= a[i] &lt;= 10^9, with the sum of n over all test cases at most 100000. For n &gt; 3, let sum be the sum of the interior values and oddCount the number of odd interior values. Since ceil(x / 2) = (x + (x mod 2)) / 2, the answer is (sum + oddCount) / 2. The sum is accumulated in a long; it is at most (n - 2) * 10^9 &lt;= 10^14, safely within long.Examples: n = 3, middle 4 gives 2; middle 3 gives -1. For n = 4, interior piles [1, 1] give -1; [1, 2] give 2. For n = 5, interior piles [1, 2, 3] give 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.The algorithm scans each test case once: O(n) time and O(n) space for the input array. The problem guarantees n &gt;= 3; smaller values are outside the input domain.import java.util.*;import java.io.*;public class Main { static BufferedReader br; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int test = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); for (int t = 0; t &lt; test; t++) { int n = Integer.parseInt(br.readLine()); int[] a = Arrays.stream(br.readLine().split(" ")) .mapToInt(Integer::parseInt) .toArray(); if (n == 3) { answer.append((a[1] &amp; 1) == 1 ? -1 : a[1] / 2); } else { boolean allOne = true; int oddCount = 0; long sum = 0; for (int i = 1; i &lt; n - 1; i++) { if (a[i] != 1) allOne = false; if ((a[i] &amp; 1) == 1) oddCount++; sum += a[i]; } answer.append(allOne ? -1 : (sum + oddCount) / 2); } answer.append('\n'); } System.out.print(answer); }}

title: Codeforces Global Round 19 A. Sorting Parts
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Codeforces Global Round, Codeforces, Sorting Parts
snippet: Problem: Codeforces 1637A — Sorting Parts · 한국어 · 日本語For each test case, choose a split k with 1 &lt;= k &lt; n. Sort the prefix a[1..k] and the suffix a[k+1..n] independently. The question is whether there is a valid split for which the resulting whole array is not non-decreasing. This is not a choice of one arbitrary segment: both sides of the split are sorted.If the original array is non-decreasing, then sorting either part leaves its values in their existing order, and the boundary between the parts is also ordered. Every split therefore produces a sorted array, so print NO.If the array is not non-decreasing, it has an adjacent inversion a[i] &gt; a[i + 1]. Choose k = i, so the inversion lies exactly across the split. After sorting the prefix, its last value is the prefix maximum, which is at least a[i]; after sorting the suffix, its first value is the suffix minimum, which is at most a[i + 1]. Thus the boundary still has left value greater than right value, and the resulting array is unsorted. Print YES. This works even if there is only one inversion or values repeat; only a strict &gt; is an inversion.The constraints have n &gt;= 2, so a valid split always exists. For a length-one array, if considered outside those constraints, there is no valid split and the answer is NO. (The code also returns NO because there is no adjacent pair.)The scan checks each adjacent pair once, taking O(n) time. The input array uses O(n) space; aside from that array, the decision uses O(1) extra space. The program reads the test-case count, then each n and its array, and appends one uppercase YES or NO line per test case.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int testCases = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int test = 0; test &lt; testCases; test++) { int n = input.nextInt(); int[] a = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) a[i] = input.nextInt(); boolean hasInversion = false; for (int i = 0; i + 1 &lt; n; i++) { if (a[i] &gt; a[i + 1]) { hasInversion = true; break; } } output.append(hasInversion ? "YES\n" : "NO\n"); } System.out.print(output); } static class FastScanner { private final BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); private StringTokenizer tokenizer; int nextInt() throws IOException { while (tokenizer == null || !tokenizer.hasMoreTokens()) { tokenizer = new StringTokenizer(reader.readLine()); } return Integer.parseInt(tokenizer.nextToken()); } }}

title: LeetCode. 100. Same Tree
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Same Tree
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/same-tree//** * Definition for a binary tree node. * public class TreeNode { * int val; * TreeNode left; * TreeNode right; * TreeNode() {} * TreeNode(int val) { this.val = val; } * TreeNode(int val, TreeNode left, TreeNode right) { * this.val = val; * this.left = left; * this.right = right; * } * } */class Solution { public boolean isSameTree(TreeNode p, TreeNode q) { return dfs(p, q); } boolean dfs(TreeNode p, TreeNode q) { if(p == null &amp;&amp; q == null) return true; if(p == null || q == null) return false; if(p.val != q.val) return false; if(!dfs(p.left, q.left)) return false; if(!dfs(p.right, q.right)) return false; return true; }}

title: BOJ. 2-SAT - 3 (11280)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Strongly Connected Component, Kosaraju's algorithm, SCC, 2-SAT - 3, Review, Important, difficult
snippet: Problem: BOJ 11280 — 2-SAT - 3 · 한국어 · 日本語Each clause (a OR b) becomes two implications: ¬a → b and ¬b → a. The input literals are signed integers. Encode the positive literal for variable i (i) as vertex i - 1, and the negative literal (-i) as vertex N + i - 1. Thus, the negation of a vertex v is v + N when v &lt; N, and v - N otherwise. Store every implication in both the forward graph and its reverse.Find strongly connected components (SCCs) with iterative Kosaraju. The first pass uses an explicit stack that also stores each vertex’s next edge position, producing DFS finishing order without recursion. Processing the vertices in reverse finishing order on the reverse graph assigns component IDs. If a variable and its negation belong to the same SCC, each implies the other, forcing both to be true; the formula is contradictory. Otherwise it is satisfiable. Unit clauses need no special handling: (x OR x), for example, adds the implication ¬x → x.There are 2N vertices and 2M implication edges. Both graph passes take O(N + M) time and space. Print only 1 if the formula is satisfiable, or 0 otherwise.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { private static int literalIndex(int literal, int n) { return literal &gt; 0 ? literal - 1 : n - literal - 1; } private static int negation(int vertex, int n) { return vertex &lt; n ? vertex + n : vertex - n; } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); StringTokenizer first = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int n = Integer.parseInt(first.nextToken()); int m = Integer.parseInt(first.nextToken()); int vertices = 2 * n; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[vertices]; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] reverse = new ArrayList[vertices]; for (int v = 0; v &lt; vertices; v++) { graph[v] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); reverse[v] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int i = 0; i &lt; m; i++) { StringTokenizer clause = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int a = literalIndex(Integer.parseInt(clause.nextToken()), n); int b = literalIndex(Integer.parseInt(clause.nextToken()), n); int notA = negation(a, n); int notB = negation(b, n); graph[notA].add(b); reverse[b].add(notA); graph[notB].add(a); reverse[a].add(notB); } boolean[] visited = new boolean[vertices]; int[] order = new int[vertices]; int orderSize = 0; int[] stackVertex = new int[vertices]; int[] stackNext = new int[vertices]; for (int start = 0; start &lt; vertices; start++) { if (visited[start]) { continue; } int top = 0; stackVertex[top] = start; stackNext[top] = 0; visited[start] = true; while (top &gt;= 0) { int v = stackVertex[top]; if (stackNext[top] &lt; graph[v].size()) { int next = graph[v].get(stackNext[top]++); if (!visited[next]) { visited[next] = true; stackVertex[++top] = next; stackNext[top] = 0; } } else { order[orderSize++] = v; top--; } } } int[] component = new int[vertices]; int componentId = 0; int[] stack = new int[vertices]; for (int i = orderSize - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { int start = order[i]; if (component[start] != 0) { continue; } componentId++; int top = 0; stack[top++] = start; component[start] = componentId; while (top &gt; 0) { int v = stack[--top]; for (int next : reverse[v]) { if (component[next] == 0) { component[next] = componentId; stack[top++] = next; } } } } for (int variable = 0; variable &lt; n; variable++) { if (component[variable] == component[variable + n]) { System.out.println(0); return; } } System.out.println(1); }}

title: BOJ. Domino (4196)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Strongly Connected Component, Tarjan's algorithm, SCC, Domino, 도미노, Review, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 4196 — Dominoes · 한국어 · 日本語Each test case gives a directed graph: pushing domino u makes every domino reachable by following outgoing edges fall. We need the smallest number of initial pushes that can make every vertex fall.First group vertices into strongly connected components (SCCs). Inside one SCC, every vertex can reach every other vertex, so one push anywhere in that component topples the entire component. If we collapse each SCC to one vertex and keep edges between different SCCs, the resulting condensation graph is a DAG.An SCC with no incoming edge in the condensation DAG must receive an initial push: no other component can make it fall. Conversely, pushing one vertex in every source SCC is sufficient. Every vertex in a finite DAG is reachable from some source (repeatedly follow incoming edges until none remain), so all components will fall. Thus the answer is exactly the number of source SCCs.The implementation uses iterative Kosaraju: an explicit DFS stack records vertices in finishing order, then a traversal of the reversed graph assigns SCC IDs in reverse finishing order. It uses no recursive calls, so a chain with 100,000 vertices cannot overflow the call stack. A final edge scan marks which SCCs have incoming edges from other SCCs. Each vertex and edge is processed a constant number of times, giving O(V + E) time and O(V + E) memory.Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.Arrays;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int limit; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } private int read() throws IOException { if (position == limit) { limit = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (limit == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int testCases = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); while (testCases-- &gt; 0) { int n = input.nextInt(); int m = input.nextInt(); int[] head = new int[n]; int[] reverseHead = new int[n]; Arrays.fill(head, -1); Arrays.fill(reverseHead, -1); int[] to = new int[m]; int[] next = new int[m]; int[] reverseTo = new int[m]; int[] reverseNext = new int[m]; for (int edge = 0; edge &lt; m; edge++) { int from = input.nextInt() - 1; int destination = input.nextInt() - 1; to[edge] = destination; next[edge] = head[from]; head[from] = edge; reverseTo[edge] = from; reverseNext[edge] = reverseHead[destination]; reverseHead[destination] = edge; } boolean[] visited = new boolean[n]; int[] order = new int[n]; int orderSize = 0; int[] nodeStack = new int[n]; int[] edgeStack = new int[n]; for (int start = 0; start &lt; n; start++) { if (visited[start]) { continue; } int top = 0; nodeStack[0] = start; edgeStack[0] = head[start]; visited[start] = true; while (top &gt;= 0) { int edge = edgeStack[top]; if (edge == -1) { order[orderSize++] = nodeStack[top--]; continue; } edgeStack[top] = next[edge]; int neighbor = to[edge]; if (!visited[neighbor]) { visited[neighbor] = true; nodeStack[++top] = neighbor; edgeStack[top] = head[neighbor]; } } } int[] component = new int[n]; Arrays.fill(component, -1); int[] stack = new int[n]; int componentCount = 0; for (int i = orderSize - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { int start = order[i]; if (component[start] != -1) { continue; } int size = 0; stack[size++] = start; component[start] = componentCount; while (size &gt; 0) { int node = stack[--size]; for (int edge = reverseHead[node]; edge != -1; edge = reverseNext[edge]) { int neighbor = reverseTo[edge]; if (component[neighbor] == -1) { component[neighbor] = componentCount; stack[size++] = neighbor; } } } componentCount++; } boolean[] hasIncoming = new boolean[componentCount]; for (int from = 0; from &lt; n; from++) { for (int edge = head[from]; edge != -1; edge = next[edge]) { int sourceComponent = component[from]; int destinationComponent = component[to[edge]]; if (sourceComponent != destinationComponent) { hasIncoming[destinationComponent] = true; } } } int pushes = 0; for (boolean incoming : hasIncoming) { if (!incoming) { pushes++; } } answer.append(pushes).append('\n'); } System.out.print(answer); }}

title: BOJ. Tree and Query 2 (13511)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Sparse table, Lowest Common Ancestor, LCA, Tree and Query 2, 트리와 쿼리 2, Review, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 13511 — Tree and Query 2 · 한국어 · 日本語Root the tree at vertex 1 and traverse it iteratively. For each vertex, record its depth and parent. The root is its own parent, so every ancestor-table entry remains valid. up[v][j] is the ancestor of v reached after 2^j edges, and weight[v][j] is the sum of those edge weights. Build both tables by doubling: the second half of a 2^j jump starts at up[v][j - 1].For a path query, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) by first lifting the deeper endpoint to the other endpoint’s depth, then lifting both from the largest jump down until their parents match. The path distance is the sum of the two weighted climbs from the endpoints to the LCA. The accumulator is long, since a path may contain many positive edge weights.For a type-2 query, let upEdges be the number of edges from a to the LCA and downEdges the number from the LCA to b. The path contains upEdges + downEdges + 1 vertices. If the 1-indexed k is at most upEdges + 1, the answer is a lifted by k - 1 edges. Otherwise, count backward from b: lift it by upEdges + downEdges + 1 - k edges. This handles the LCA and both endpoints without special path manipulation.The traversal and table construction are iterative, so a chain of 100,000 vertices cannot overflow the call stack. Preprocessing takes O(N log N) time and O(N log N) storage; each query takes O(log N) time.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;public class Main { static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int pointer = 0; private int length = 0; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = in.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[pointer++]; } } static class Edge { int to; int weight; Edge(int to, int weight) { this.to = to; this.weight = weight; } } static int[][] up; static long[][] weight; static int[] depth; static int lift(int vertex, int steps) { for (int j = 0; steps &gt; 0; j++, steps &gt;&gt;= 1) { if ((steps &amp; 1) != 0) vertex = up[vertex][j]; } return vertex; } static int lca(int a, int b) { if (depth[a] &lt; depth[b]) { int temp = a; a = b; b = temp; } a = lift(a, depth[a] - depth[b]); if (a == b) return a; for (int j = up[0].length - 1; j &gt;= 0; j--) { if (up[a][j] != up[b][j]) { a = up[a][j]; b = up[b][j]; } } return up[a][0]; } static long climbWeight(int vertex, int steps) { long total = 0; for (int j = 0; steps &gt; 0; j++, steps &gt;&gt;= 1) { if ((steps &amp; 1) != 0) { total += weight[vertex][j]; vertex = up[vertex][j]; } } return total; } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int levels = 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(n); ArrayList&lt;Edge&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) graph[i] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; i++) { int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; int w = input.nextInt(); graph[a].add(new Edge(b, w)); graph[b].add(new Edge(a, w)); } up = new int[n][levels]; weight = new long[n][levels]; depth = new int[n]; boolean[] visited = new boolean[n]; int[] stack = new int[n]; int top = 0; stack[top++] = 0; visited[0] = true; up[0][0] = 0; while (top &gt; 0) { int vertex = stack[--top]; for (Edge edge : graph[vertex]) { if (visited[edge.to]) continue; visited[edge.to] = true; up[edge.to][0] = vertex; weight[edge.to][0] = edge.weight; depth[edge.to] = depth[vertex] + 1; stack[top++] = edge.to; } } for (int j = 1; j &lt; levels; j++) { for (int vertex = 0; vertex &lt; n; vertex++) { int middle = up[vertex][j - 1]; up[vertex][j] = up[middle][j - 1]; weight[vertex][j] = weight[vertex][j - 1] + weight[middle][j - 1]; } } int queryCount = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; queryCount; i++) { int type = input.nextInt(); int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; int ancestor = lca(a, b); if (type == 1) { output.append(climbWeight(a, depth[a] - depth[ancestor]) + climbWeight(b, depth[b] - depth[ancestor])).append('\n'); } else { int k = input.nextInt(); int upEdges = depth[a] - depth[ancestor]; int downEdges = depth[b] - depth[ancestor]; int answer = k &lt;= upEdges + 1 ? lift(a, k - 1) : lift(b, upEdges + downEdges + 1 - k); output.append(answer + 1).append('\n'); } } System.out.print(output); }}

title: BOJ. Palindrome Devision (1509)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Sparse table, Lowest Common Ancestor, Palindrome Devision, 팰린드롬 분할, Review, Important, difficult
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1509 · 한국어 · 日本語Given a string s of length N, partition it into the fewest contiguous palindromic pieces. Precompute palindrome[l][r], true exactly when the inclusive substring s[l..r] is a palindrome. In increasing substring-length order, its ends must match, and either the substring has length at most two or its inner substring is already known to be a palindrome. This examines each of the O(N²) substrings once.Use prefix DP: dp[r] is the minimum number of palindromic pieces covering the half-open prefix s[0..r). Set dp[0] = 0; for every end boundary r from 1 through N, consider each earlier boundary l. If s[l..r) is palindromic, append it to an optimal partition of the preceding prefix: dp[r] = min(dp[r], dp[l] + 1). The first character is handled by l = 0; a palindrome spanning the entire input yields dp[N] = 1. Every partition has a final palindromic piece, so considering all such l finds the optimum. Repeated characters and mixed splits need no special cases.The palindrome table and prefix DP each use O(N²) time overall (the DP checks O(N²) possible intervals); space is O(N²) for the table and O(N) for dp. The algorithm is iterative and does not depend on recursion depth.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.Arrays;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String s = input.readLine(); int n = s.length(); boolean[][] palindrome = new boolean[n][n]; for (int length = 1; length &lt;= n; length++) { for (int left = 0; left + length &lt;= n; left++) { int right = left + length - 1; palindrome[left][right] = s.charAt(left) == s.charAt(right) &amp;&amp; (length &lt;= 2 || palindrome[left + 1][right - 1]); } } int[] dp = new int[n + 1]; Arrays.fill(dp, n + 1); dp[0] = 0; for (int right = 1; right &lt;= n; right++) { for (int left = 0; left &lt; right; left++) { if (palindrome[left][right - 1]) { dp[right] = Math.min(dp[right], dp[left] + 1); } } } System.out.println(dp[n]); }}

title: BOJ. Find Minimum (11003)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Sliding Window, Find Minimum, Deque
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/11003ApproachFor each position i, the required window is [max(0, i - L + 1), i]. In particular, the first L - 1 windows contain only the values seen so far; they are not padded with nonexistent elements.Keep candidate indices in increasing order in a deque, with their values in a parallel primitive array. Before inserting A[i], remove indices &lt;= i - L from the front because they are outside the current window. Then remove values greater than or equal to A[i] from the back: the new value is no larger and remains in the window at least as long, so those candidates can never be a future minimum. The front value is therefore the minimum for the current window. Removing equal values is safe and keeps only the newest copy.Each index is inserted once and removed at most once, so the total work is O(N) amortized. The input scanner reads bytes directly, and the deque uses two int[] arrays, avoiding per-number strings and per-element objects. The arrays and output buffer use O(N) memory.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int windowLength = input.nextInt(); int[] indices = new int[n]; int[] values = new int[n]; int front = 0; int back = 0; StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { int value = input.nextInt(); while (front &lt; back &amp;&amp; indices[front] &lt;= i - windowLength) { front++; } while (front &lt; back &amp;&amp; values[back - 1] &gt;= value) { back--; } indices[back] = i; values[back] = value; back++; if (i &gt; 0) { output.append(' '); } output.append(values[front]); } System.out.println(output); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int pointer; private int length; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' '); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = in.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[pointer++]; } }}

title: BOJ. Road Network (3176)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Sparse table, Lowest Common Ancestor, LCA, Road Network, 도로 네트워크, Review, Important, difficult
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/3176Root the tree at vertex 1 with an explicit stack, recording each vertex’s depth, immediate parent, and the minimum and maximum edge weight on its one-edge climb. For each higher power of two, combine two half-length climbs to build the ancestor, minimum-edge, and maximum-edge tables. The root is its own ancestor; sentinel extrema on its empty climb do not affect any real path.For a query, first lift the deeper endpoint until both endpoints have equal depth, folding the traversed edge extrema into the answer. Then lift both endpoints together from the largest jump down whenever their ancestors differ, folding both traversals. The remaining one-edge climbs meet at their lowest common ancestor. If both endpoints are the same vertex, the path has no edges; this implementation defines its neutral result as 0 0 (the original constraints generally use distinct endpoints).The iterative rooting avoids call-stack overflow on a chain of 100,000 vertices. Preprocessing time and storage are O(N log N); each path query takes O(log N) time.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;public class Main { static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int limit; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } private int read() throws IOException { if (position == limit) { limit = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (limit == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } } static class Edge { int to; int weight; Edge(int to, int weight) { this.to = to; this.weight = weight; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int levels = 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(n); ArrayList&lt;Edge&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n]; for (int vertex = 0; vertex &lt; n; vertex++) graph[vertex] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; i++) { int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; int weight = input.nextInt(); graph[a].add(new Edge(b, weight)); graph[b].add(new Edge(a, weight)); } int[][] up = new int[n][levels]; int[][] minEdge = new int[n][levels]; int[][] maxEdge = new int[n][levels]; int[] depth = new int[n]; boolean[] visited = new boolean[n]; int[] stack = new int[n]; int size = 0; stack[size++] = 0; visited[0] = true; up[0][0] = 0; minEdge[0][0] = Integer.MAX_VALUE; maxEdge[0][0] = Integer.MIN_VALUE; while (size &gt; 0) { int vertex = stack[--size]; for (Edge edge : graph[vertex]) { if (visited[edge.to]) continue; visited[edge.to] = true; up[edge.to][0] = vertex; minEdge[edge.to][0] = edge.weight; maxEdge[edge.to][0] = edge.weight; depth[edge.to] = depth[vertex] + 1; stack[size++] = edge.to; } } for (int j = 1; j &lt; levels; j++) { for (int vertex = 0; vertex &lt; n; vertex++) { int middle = up[vertex][j - 1]; up[vertex][j] = up[middle][j - 1]; minEdge[vertex][j] = Math.min(minEdge[vertex][j - 1], minEdge[middle][j - 1]); maxEdge[vertex][j] = Math.max(maxEdge[vertex][j - 1], maxEdge[middle][j - 1]); } } int queryCount = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int query = 0; query &lt; queryCount; query++) { int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; if (a == b) { output.append("0 0\n"); continue; } int min = Integer.MAX_VALUE; int max = Integer.MIN_VALUE; if (depth[a] &lt; depth[b]) { int temp = a; a = b; b = temp; } int difference = depth[a] - depth[b]; for (int j = levels - 1; j &gt;= 0; j--) { if ((difference &amp; (1 &lt;&lt; j)) != 0) { min = Math.min(min, minEdge[a][j]); max = Math.max(max, maxEdge[a][j]); a = up[a][j]; } } if (a != b) { for (int j = levels - 1; j &gt;= 0; j--) { if (up[a][j] != up[b][j]) { min = Math.min(min, Math.min(minEdge[a][j], minEdge[b][j])); max = Math.max(max, Math.max(maxEdge[a][j], maxEdge[b][j])); a = up[a][j]; b = up[b][j]; } } min = Math.min(min, Math.min(minEdge[a][0], minEdge[b][0])); max = Math.max(max, Math.max(maxEdge[a][0], maxEdge[b][0])); } output.append(min).append(' ').append(max).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); }}

title: BOJ. LCA 2 (11438)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Sparse table, Lowest Common Ancestor, LCA, LCA 2, Review, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 11438 — LCA 2 · 한국어 · 日本語Root the tree at vertex 1. For each vertex v, store its depth and up[v][j], the ancestor reached by moving 2^j edges upward. The root is its own ancestor at every level. This self-parent convention keeps every table entry valid and makes jumps at the root safe.The ancestor table is built from up[v][0] = parent[v] and up[v][j] = up[up[v][j - 1]][j - 1]. The number of columns is derived from n; 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(n) columns cover every possible depth for positive n.To find the LCA of a and b, first swap them if necessary so a is the deeper vertex. Lift a by the set bits of the depth difference, bringing both vertices to the same depth. If they now match, that vertex is the LCA. Otherwise, inspect jump sizes from largest to smallest and move both vertices upward whenever their 2^j ancestors differ. Each move keeps them below their common ancestor; after the final step, their immediate parent is the LCA.The initial traversal uses an explicit stack rather than recursion, so a chain of 100,000 vertices does not consume the Java call stack. Preprocessing takes O(N log N) time and space, and each query takes O(log N) time.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Arrays;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine()); ArrayList&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { graph[i] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; i++) { String[] edge = input.readLine().split(" "); int a = Integer.parseInt(edge[0]) - 1; int b = Integer.parseInt(edge[1]) - 1; graph[a].add(b); graph[b].add(a); } int levels = 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(n); int[][] up = new int[n][levels]; int[] depth = new int[n]; boolean[] visited = new boolean[n]; int[] stack = new int[n]; int top = 0; stack[top++] = 0; visited[0] = true; up[0][0] = 0; while (top &gt; 0) { int vertex = stack[--top]; for (int neighbor : graph[vertex]) { if (visited[neighbor]) { continue; } visited[neighbor] = true; up[neighbor][0] = vertex; depth[neighbor] = depth[vertex] + 1; stack[top++] = neighbor; } } for (int j = 1; j &lt; levels; j++) { for (int vertex = 0; vertex &lt; n; vertex++) { up[vertex][j] = up[up[vertex][j - 1]][j - 1]; } } int queryCount = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine()); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; queryCount; i++) { String[] query = input.readLine().split(" "); int a = Integer.parseInt(query[0]) - 1; int b = Integer.parseInt(query[1]) - 1; output.append(lca(a, b, depth, up)).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static int lca(int a, int b, int[] depth, int[][] up) { if (depth[a] &lt; depth[b]) { int temp = a; a = b; b = temp; } int difference = depth[a] - depth[b]; for (int j = 0; j &lt; up[0].length; j++) { if ((difference &amp; (1 &lt;&lt; j)) != 0) { a = up[a][j]; } } if (a == b) { return a + 1; } for (int j = up[0].length - 1; j &gt;= 0; j--) { if (up[a][j] != up[b][j]) { a = up[a][j]; b = up[b][j]; } } return up[a][0] + 1; }}

title: BOJ. Composite Function And Query (17435)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Sparse table, Composite Function And Query, 합성함수와 쿼리, Review, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 17435 — Composite Function And Query한국어 · 日本語ApproachThe input defines a function f on the integers 1..M. Each query asks for f applied K times to a starting value x, i.e. f^K(x). Applying the function one step at a time can take up to 500,000 operations per query, so precompute powers of the function with binary lifting.Let up[b][x] be the value reached after applying f exactly 2^b times to x. The base row is up[0][x] = f(x). Two consecutive jumps of length 2^(b-1) make a jump of length 2^b, so:up[b][x] = up[b - 1][up[b - 1][x]]For a query, inspect the set bits of K. Whenever bit b is set, replace the current value with up[b][current]. The selected jump lengths sum to K, so this computes exactly f^K(x). In particular, when K = 0 no bit is set and the answer remains x; K = 1 uses only the base row. The table has 20 rows, covering every bit of K &lt;= 500000 (the highest possible set bit is 18), so no query can index beyond it.Preprocessing takes O(M log Kmax) time and memory, where Kmax = 500000. Each query takes O(log Kmax) time.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { private static final int LEVELS = 20; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int m = input.nextInt(); int[][] up = new int[LEVELS][m + 1]; for (int x = 1; x &lt;= m; x++) { up[0][x] = input.nextInt(); } for (int bit = 1; bit &lt; LEVELS; bit++) { for (int x = 1; x &lt;= m; x++) { up[bit][x] = up[bit - 1][up[bit - 1][x]]; } } int queryCount = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); for (int query = 0; query &lt; queryCount; query++) { int k = input.nextInt(); int value = input.nextInt(); for (int bit = 0; bit &lt; LEVELS; bit++) { if ((k &amp; (1 &lt;&lt; bit)) != 0) { value = up[bit][value]; } } answer.append(value).append('\n'); } System.out.print(answer); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int pointer; private int length; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' '); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = in.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[pointer++]; } }}

title: BOJ. Lowest Common Ancestor (3584)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Tree, Lowest Common Ancestor, LCA, 가장 가까운 공통 조상
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/3584Each test case gives a rooted tree with N nodes and exactly one pair of nodes whose lowest common ancestor (LCA) must be found. The input edges are directed from parent to child, so store each child’s parent in a parent array. The one node with no parent is the root.For the query, mark the first node and each of its ancestors by repeatedly following parent links. Then start at the second node and climb toward the root until reaching a marked node. The first marked node encountered is the lowest common ancestor: every node on the second node’s upward path is an ancestor of it, and the first intersection with the first node’s ancestor chain is the deepest shared ancestor. This includes queries where one queried node is itself an ancestor of the other, including the root.Building parent takes O(N) time. Marking and climbing take at most O(N) time in total, using O(N) space. The algorithm is iterative, so a tree shaped as a chain of 100,000 nodes does not consume the call stack.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); int testCases = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); for (int test = 0; test &lt; testCases; test++) { int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); int[] parent = new int[n + 1]; for (int edge = 0; edge &lt; n - 1; edge++) { StringTokenizer tokens = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int from = Integer.parseInt(tokens.nextToken()); int to = Integer.parseInt(tokens.nextToken()); parent[to] = from; } int root = 1; while (parent[root] != 0) { root++; } StringTokenizer query = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int first = Integer.parseInt(query.nextToken()); int second = Integer.parseInt(query.nextToken()); boolean[] ancestors = new boolean[n + 1]; for (int node = first; ; node = parent[node]) { ancestors[node] = true; if (node == root) { break; } } while (!ancestors[second]) { second = parent[second]; } output.append(second).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); }}

title: BOJ. SeongYeon Park (1086)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Bitmask, SeongYeon Park, 박성원, Review, Important, difficult
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1086 — SeongYeon Park · 한국어 · 日本語Subset dynamic programmingThe input contains N strings. A permutation chooses an ordering of their positions; even when two strings have identical contents, their positions are distinct choices and contribute separate permutations. There are N! equally likely orderings.Let dp[mask][r] be the number of ways to concatenate exactly the strings selected by mask so that the resulting number has remainder r modulo K. The empty concatenation has remainder zero, so dp[0][0] = 1. For each string i, precompute its remainder value[i] modulo K, and precompute power[len] = 10^len mod K for lengths up to the total input length.Appending string i to a concatenation with remainder r and current length len gives remaindernextRemainder = (r * power[length[i]] + value[i]) mod K.Thus, for every unused index i, add dp[mask][r] to dp[mask | (1 &lt;&lt; i)][nextRemainder]. The transition iterates over indices, not distinct string values, which correctly counts repeated input strings as distinguishable positions. Once all positions are used, dp[(1 &lt;&lt; N) - 1][0] is the number of divisible permutations.The probability is that count divided by N!. Reduce the fraction by their greatest common divisor; when the count is zero, print 0/1 directly. N &lt;= 15, so every state count and 15! fit in a signed long. With 2^N masks, K remainders, and at most N transitions per state, the time complexity is O(N K 2^N) and the space complexity is O(K 2^N).Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); String[] numbers = new String[n]; int totalLength = 0; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { numbers[i] = input.next(); totalLength += numbers[i].length(); } int k = input.nextInt(); int[] value = new int[n]; int[] length = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { length[i] = numbers[i].length(); int remainder = 0; for (int j = 0; j &lt; length[i]; j++) { remainder = (remainder * 10 + numbers[i].charAt(j) - '0') % k; } value[i] = remainder; } int[] power = new int[totalLength + 1]; power[0] = 1 % k; for (int len = 1; len &lt;= totalLength; len++) { power[len] = (int) ((long) power[len - 1] * 10 % k); } int states = 1 &lt;&lt; n; long[][] dp = new long[states][k]; dp[0][0] = 1; for (int mask = 0; mask &lt; states; mask++) { for (int remainder = 0; remainder &lt; k; remainder++) { long ways = dp[mask][remainder]; if (ways == 0) { continue; } for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { if ((mask &amp; (1 &lt;&lt; i)) == 0) { int nextRemainder = (int) ( ((long) remainder * power[length[i]] + value[i]) % k ); dp[mask | (1 &lt;&lt; i)][nextRemainder] += ways; } } } } long numerator = dp[states - 1][0]; if (numerator == 0) { System.out.println("0/1"); return; } long denominator = 1; for (int i = 2; i &lt;= n; i++) { denominator *= i; } long divisor = gcd(numerator, denominator); System.out.println((numerator / divisor) + "/" + (denominator / divisor)); } private static long gcd(long a, long b) { while (b != 0) { long remainder = a % b; a = b; b = remainder; } return a; } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String next() throws IOException { StringBuilder token = new StringBuilder(); int c; do { c = reader.read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); while (c &gt; ' ') { token.append((char) c); c = reader.read(); } return token.toString(); } int nextInt() throws IOException { return Integer.parseInt(next()); } }}

title: BOJ. Traveling Salesman problem (2098)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Bitmask, Traveling Salesman problem, TSP, 외판원 순회
snippet: Problem: BOJ 2098 — Traveling Salesman Problem · 한국어 · 日本語Bitmask dynamic programmingFix city 0 as the starting city; every tour can be rotated to start there. Represent a state as (current, visited), where visited is a bitmask of the cities already visited and includes city 0. Let dp[current][visited] be the minimum additional cost needed to visit every remaining city exactly once and then return to city 0.If every city has been visited, the remaining cost is the edge from current back to 0. If that directed edge does not exist, the state is impossible. Otherwise, try each unvisited city next for which the edge current → next exists, and take the minimum of the edge cost plus the corresponding subproblem:dp[current][visited] = min(cost[current][next] + dp[next][visited | (1 &lt;&lt; next)]).The minimum is over valid next cities only. An input cost of zero means there is no edge, so such transitions must be skipped. If no complete tour exists, BOJ 2098 requires output 0; an impossible state is represented internally by INF and is never added to another cost.There are N · 2^N states and each examines at most N next cities, so the time complexity is O(N² 2^N) and the space complexity is O(N 2^N). long costs and Long.MAX_VALUE / 4 as INF leave ample room for adding any valid route cost without overflow.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.Arrays;public class Main { private static final long INF = Long.MAX_VALUE / 4; private static int n; private static int[][] cost; private static long[][] dp; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); cost = new int[n][n]; for (int from = 0; from &lt; n; from++) { String[] row = input.readLine().trim().split("\\s+"); for (int to = 0; to &lt; n; to++) { cost[from][to] = Integer.parseInt(row[to]); } } dp = new long[n][1 &lt;&lt; n]; for (long[] row : dp) { Arrays.fill(row, -1); } long answer = visit(0, 1); System.out.println(answer == INF ? 0 : answer); } private static long visit(int current, int visited) { if (visited == (1 &lt;&lt; n) - 1) { return cost[current][0] == 0 ? INF : cost[current][0]; } if (dp[current][visited] != -1) { return dp[current][visited]; } long best = INF; for (int next = 0; next &lt; n; next++) { int bit = 1 &lt;&lt; next; if ((visited &amp; bit) != 0 || cost[current][next] == 0) { continue; } long remaining = visit(next, visited | bit); if (remaining != INF) { best = Math.min(best, cost[current][next] + remaining); } } return dp[current][visited] = best; }}

title: BOJ. RGB Distance 2 (17404)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, RGB Distance 2, RGB거리 2
snippet: BOJ 17404: RGB Distance 2한국어 · 日本語ApproachEach house is painted red, green, or blue, and neighboring houses must have different colors. Because the houses form a circle, the first and last houses are neighbors too, so their colors must differ as well.Fix the first house’s color and run a linear dynamic program. Let dp[c] be the minimum cost through the current house when that house is painted color c. Initialize all three states to infinity except the fixed first color, whose state is its painting cost. For each later house and color c, the transition is the cost of c plus the smaller previous cost among the other two colors:next[c] = cost[i][c] + min(dp[(c + 1) % 3], dp[(c + 2) % 3]).After processing every house, consider only final colors different from the fixed first color. This enforces the circular edge. Repeat for each of the three possible first colors and take the minimum result. Every valid circular coloring has exactly one first color, so these three cases cover all possibilities without accepting an invalid one.The case N = 2 follows the same rule: the two houses are adjacent around the circle and must have different colors. The final-color check rejects the fixed starting color, leaving precisely those valid choices.The recurrence uses two rolling arrays of three long values. Costs are stored as input, while the DP state uses constant auxiliary space; the three runs take O(N) time in total. A wide long total and a safely bounded infinity value avoid overflow when costs are accumulated.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { private static final long INF = Long.MAX_VALUE / 4; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int[][] cost = new int[n][3]; for (int house = 0; house &lt; n; house++) { for (int color = 0; color &lt; 3; color++) { cost[house][color] = input.nextInt(); } } long answer = INF; for (int firstColor = 0; firstColor &lt; 3; firstColor++) { long[] previous = {INF, INF, INF}; long[] current = new long[3]; previous[firstColor] = cost[0][firstColor]; for (int house = 1; house &lt; n; house++) { for (int color = 0; color &lt; 3; color++) { current[color] = cost[house][color] + Math.min(previous[(color + 1) % 3], previous[(color + 2) % 3]); } long[] temp = previous; previous = current; current = temp; } for (int lastColor = 0; lastColor &lt; 3; lastColor++) { if (lastColor != firstColor) { answer = Math.min(answer, previous[lastColor]); } } } System.out.println(answer); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int pointer; private int length; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' '); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = in.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[pointer++]; } }}

title: BOJ. Workbook (1766)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Topological Sort, Workbook, 문제집
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1766 — Workbook · 한국어 · 日本語Each directed edge A -&gt; B means problem A must be solved before problem B. We need a topological ordering: every vertex appears exactly once, and every edge points from an earlier position to a later one. When several problems are available, the required ordering chooses the smallest-numbered one first.Kahn’s algorithm maintains the in-degree (the number of unfinished prerequisites) of each problem. Put every zero-in-degree problem in a min-priority queue. Repeatedly remove the smallest available problem, append it to the answer, and decrement the in-degree of each outgoing neighbor. A neighbor becomes available exactly when its in-degree reaches zero, so insert it then. The heap always chooses the smallest problem that can legally be next; a FIFO queue would not guarantee this. For example, with edges 1 -&gt; 4 and 2 -&gt; 3, after choosing 1, both 2 and 4 are available, and the heap chooses 2 first.The input may separate integers with any whitespace, so the scanner reads bytes and skips whitespace rather than assuming one record per line. Duplicate edges are retained in both the adjacency list and in-degree count; processing each copy subtracts one, leaving a vertex eligible only after all prerequisite edges have been removed. Isolated problems are in the initial heap, and this also handles N = 1 without special cases.Building the graph takes O(N + M). Every vertex is inserted into and removed from the heap once, while every edge is processed once, giving O((N + M) log N) time and O(N + M) space.Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.PriorityQueue;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position = 0; private int length = 0; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = in.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int m = input.nextInt(); @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") ArrayList&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) graph[i] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); int[] indegree = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; m; i++) { int from = input.nextInt() - 1; int to = input.nextInt() - 1; graph[from].add(to); indegree[to]++; } PriorityQueue&lt;Integer&gt; available = new PriorityQueue&lt;&gt;(); for (int problem = 0; problem &lt; n; problem++) { if (indegree[problem] == 0) available.add(problem); } StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); while (!available.isEmpty()) { int current = available.remove(); answer.append(current + 1).append(' '); for (int next : graph[current]) { if (--indegree[next] == 0) available.add(next); } } System.out.println(answer); }}

title: BOJ. Distributed Processing (1009)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Distributed Processing, 분산처리
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1009For each test case, compute the last digit of a^b by binary exponentiation modulo 10. This avoids trying to discover a repeating cycle and works for every base, including bases divisible by 10. The result identifies the computer numbered by that digit, except that a remainder of 0 means computer 10 (the computers are numbered 1 through 10).The program reads the test-case count and then processes each (a, b) pair independently. Its running time per case is O(log b).Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int testCases = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int test = 0; test &lt; testCases; test++) { String[] values = input.readLine().trim().split("\\s+"); int a = Integer.parseInt(values[0]); long b = Long.parseLong(values[1]); int lastDigit = (int) powerModuloTen(a, b); output.append(lastDigit == 0 ? 10 : lastDigit).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } static long powerModuloTen(int base, long exponent) { long result = 1; long factor = base % 10; while (exponent &gt; 0) { if ((exponent &amp; 1) != 0) result = (result * factor) % 10; factor = (factor * factor) % 10; exponent &gt;&gt;= 1; } return result; }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 238 C digitnum
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 238 C — digitnum · 한국어 · 日本語For every integer from 1 through N, add its number of decimal digits, then print the sum modulo 998244353.Group the integers by digit length. For a length d, the applicable range is [10^(d-1), min(N, 10^d - 1)]; add d times the number of integers in that range. The loop stops once its range reaches N.The number of digit lengths is O(log N), so the time complexity is O(log N) and the extra space complexity is O(1). All range endpoints are computed as long. To avoid overflowing when forming 10^d, the code checks whether the next power of ten is at most N before multiplying by ten.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { private static final long MOD = 998244353L; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); long n = Long.parseLong(input.readLine().trim()); long answer = 0; long start = 1; for (long digits = 1; start &lt;= n; digits++) { long end = n; if (start &lt;= n / 10) { end = start * 10 - 1; } long count = end - start + 1; answer = (answer + (digits % MOD) * (count % MOD)) % MOD; if (end == n) { break; } start *= 10; } System.out.println(answer); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 238 B Pizza
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 238 B — Pizza · 한국어 · 日本語Start with a cut at 0°. Each instruction rotates the knife clockwise by the given angle, so the new cut is the previous angle plus that rotation, modulo 360. Store all N resulting cut positions together with 0°. Repeated positions are valid: they mean that a cut falls on an existing cut and create a zero-width gap.Sort the positions. The gaps between consecutive positions are slice sizes, and the last slice wraps around from the final cut to 360° (the same point as 0°). The largest of these gaps is the largest possible slice. With N + 1 positions, sorting takes O(N log N) time and the array uses O(N) space.For example, with rotations 90, 180, 45, 195, the cut positions are 0, 90, 270, 315, 150. After sorting they are 0, 90, 150, 270, 315; the gaps are 90, 60, 120, 45, and the wraparound gap is 45, so the answer is 120.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.Arrays;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); StringTokenizer rotations = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int[] cuts = new int[n + 1]; int angle = 0; for (int i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) { angle = (angle + Integer.parseInt(rotations.nextToken())) % 360; cuts[i] = angle; } Arrays.sort(cuts); int largest = 0; for (int i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) { largest = Math.max(largest, cuts[i] - cuts[i - 1]); } largest = Math.max(largest, 360 - cuts[n] + cuts[0]); System.out.println(largest); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 238 A Exponential or Quadratic
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 238 A — Exponential or Quadratic[English] · 한국어 · 日本語We need to determine whether 2^N &gt; N^2. There is no need to calculate the power: for N = 1, the inequality holds; for N = 2, 3, 4, it does not (2^4 = 4^2). Starting at N = 5, it is always true. If 2^N &gt; N^2 for some N &gt;= 5, then 2^(N + 1) &gt; 2N^2 &gt;= (N + 1)^2, so the inequality continues to hold for every larger integer.Therefore, the answer is Yes exactly when N = 1 or N &gt;= 5; otherwise it is No. A pair of integer comparisons is enough, even for large permitted values of N.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); System.out.println(n == 1 || n &gt;= 5 ? "Yes" : "No"); }}

title: BOJ. Hue Circle (2482)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Hue Circle, 색상환
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2482 · 한국어 · 日本語We must choose K of the N positions on a circle so that no two selected positions are adjacent, including the first and last positions. Let line(L, k) count ways to choose k nonadjacent positions from a line of length L. The chosen positions need at least one unchosen position between consecutive choices, soline(L, k) = C(L - k + 1, k)when 0 &lt;= k &lt;= L - k + 1; otherwise it is zero.
