In particular, choosing zero positions has one way, and negative or impossible arguments contribute zero.Split the circular choices into two disjoint cases: If the first position is selected, its two neighbors cannot be selected. The remaining N - 3 positions form a line, from which we choose K - 1: line(N - 3, K - 1). If the first position is not selected, the other N - 1 positions form a line, from which we choose K: line(N - 1, K).Add these counts and take the result modulo 1,000,000,003. The cases cover every selection exactly once. The implementation builds Pascal’s triangle only through the required K columns, obtaining each needed binomial coefficient in O(NK) time and O(NK) space. This is small for N &lt;= 1000 and also avoids factorial division modulo a non-prime modulus.Handle boundaries before building the table: selecting zero positions has one way; N = 1 has one way for K = 1 and zero for other positive K; N = 2 has two ways for K = 1 and zero for larger K. Invalid N or K and any K &gt; floor(N / 2) for N &gt; 1 yield zero. The first two cycle sizes are explicit because the usual split assumes three distinct positions.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { private static final int MOD = 1_000_000_003; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); int k = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); if (n &lt; 1 || k &lt; 0 || k &gt; n) { System.out.println(0); return; } if (k == 0) { System.out.println(1); return; } if (n == 1) { System.out.println(k == 1 ? 1 : 0); return; } if (n == 2) { System.out.println(k == 1 ? 2 : 0); return; } if (k &gt; n / 2) { System.out.println(0); return; } int[][] binomial = new int[n + 1][k + 1]; for (int row = 0; row &lt;= n; row++) { binomial[row][0] = 1; for (int column = 1; column &lt;= Math.min(row, k); column++) { int value = binomial[row - 1][column] + binomial[row - 1][column - 1]; binomial[row][column] = value &gt;= MOD ? value - MOD : value; } } int answer = binomial[n - k - 1][k - 1] + binomial[n - k][k]; if (answer &gt;= MOD) { answer -= MOD; } System.out.println(answer); }}

title: BOJ. ACM Craft (1005)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Topological Sort, Graph, ACM Craft
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1005 — ACM Craft · 한국어 · 日本語Each rule A B means building A must be completed before building B can start. The rules form a directed acyclic graph. Process buildings in topological order so that every prerequisite has its completion time before its dependent building is handled.Let finish[v] be the earliest time building v can be completed. Its recurrence is finish[v] = duration[v] + max(finish[p]) over prerequisites p, with the maximum over an empty set defined as 0 for a source building. For each edge u -&gt; v, update finish[v] with finish[u] + duration[v], keeping the maximum over all prerequisites. This maximum matters when a building has multiple prerequisite paths: construction can start only after the slowest required predecessor is finished. Initially set finish[v] = duration[v]; this handles source buildings and a target that is itself a source, whose answer is simply its own duration.Kahn’s algorithm queues every vertex with indegree zero. When a building is removed from the queue, relax all outgoing edges and decrement their indegrees; a dependent building enters the queue only after all its prerequisites have been processed. The target’s accumulated finish value is then the answer for that test case.The adjacency lists, indegrees, and queue take O(N + K) time and space per test case, where N is the number of buildings and K is the number of rules. long stores completion times safely.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int testCases = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); while (testCases-- &gt; 0) { int n = input.nextInt(); int k = input.nextInt(); long[] duration = new long[n]; long[] finish = new long[n]; int[] indegree = new int[n]; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n]; for (int building = 0; building &lt; n; building++) { duration[building] = input.nextInt(); finish[building] = duration[building]; graph[building] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int rule = 0; rule &lt; k; rule++) { int prerequisite = input.nextInt() - 1; int building = input.nextInt() - 1; graph[prerequisite].add(building); indegree[building]++; } int target = input.nextInt() - 1; int[] queue = new int[n]; int front = 0; int back = 0; for (int building = 0; building &lt; n; building++) { if (indegree[building] == 0) { queue[back++] = building; } } while (front &lt; back) { int prerequisite = queue[front++]; for (int building : graph[prerequisite]) { finish[building] = Math.max( finish[building], finish[prerequisite] + duration[building] ); if (--indegree[building] == 0) { queue[back++] = building; } } } output.append(finish[target]).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); private StringTokenizer tokenizer; int nextInt() throws IOException { while (tokenizer == null || !tokenizer.hasMoreTokens()) { tokenizer = new StringTokenizer(reader.readLine()); } return Integer.parseInt(tokenizer.nextToken()); } }}

title: BOJ. Advertisement (1305)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, KMP, String, Advertisement, 광고
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1305 — Advertisement · 한국어 · 日本語Let the observed advertisement have length L. We need the shortest block whose infinite repetition begins with this entire observed string. Compute the KMP prefix function pi, where pi[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of s[0..i] that is also a suffix. At the end, pi[L - 1] is the largest border of the whole string.The border is exactly the portion that can overlap when one copy of the shortest block is followed by the next. Thus the shortest block length is L - pi[L - 1]. This is valid even when that length does not divide L: for example, ababa has a border of length 3, so repeating ab begins with ababa. With no nonempty border, the answer is L; if the string is a repetition of a smaller block, the formula returns that block’s length.The input guarantees 1 &lt;= L &lt;= 1,000,000 and that the string contains exactly L characters. The implementation checks this before indexing the prefix array. Prefix-function construction and the final calculation take O(L) time; the prefix array uses O(L) space.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int length = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine()); String advertisement = input.readLine(); if (length &lt;= 0 || advertisement == null || advertisement.length() != length) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid advertisement length"); } int[] pi = prefixFunction(advertisement); System.out.println(length - pi[length - 1]); } private static int[] prefixFunction(String s) { int[] pi = new int[s.length()]; int matched = 0; for (int i = 1; i &lt; s.length(); i++) { while (matched &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; s.charAt(i) != s.charAt(matched)) { matched = pi[matched - 1]; } if (s.charAt(i) == s.charAt(matched)) { pi[i] = ++matched; } } return pi; }}

title: BOJ. Independent Set of Tree. (2213)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Graph, Dynamic Programming, Independent Set of Tree., 트리의 독립집합
snippet: Problem: BOJ 2213 — Tree Independent Set · 한국어 · 日本語Root the tree at vertex 1. For each vertex v, let in[v] be the maximum weight of an independent set in the subtree of v that includes v, and out[v] the maximum when it excludes v. If w[v] is its positive weight, then in[v] = w[v] + sum(out[child]): choosing v rules out each child. out[v] = sum(max(in[child], out[child])): without v, each child may be chosen or omitted independently.The graph is a tree, so the child subtrees have no edges between them; these choices therefore combine to give an optimum. Build a parent array and a root-first vertex order iteratively, then process that order backwards so every child DP value is ready before its parent. This avoids recursion and remains safe for a chain of 100,000 vertices.Reconstruct by walking the rooted tree from the root. If the parent was chosen, the current vertex must be omitted. Otherwise, choose it only when in[v] &gt; out[v]; on a tie omit it. The root follows the same rule. Either choice on a tie is optimal, and this fixed rule simply makes the output deterministic. Finally sort the chosen vertex IDs before printing them. The total weight is the root’s larger DP value; the second output line is one corresponding independent set.Each vertex and edge is processed a constant number of times, so the time and space complexities are both O(N).Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Collections;import java.util.List;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); int[] weight = new int[n + 1]; StringTokenizer weights = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); for (int vertex = 1; vertex &lt;= n; vertex++) { weight[vertex] = Integer.parseInt(weights.nextToken()); } List&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n + 1]; for (int vertex = 1; vertex &lt;= n; vertex++) { graph[vertex] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int edge = 0; edge &lt; n - 1; edge++) { StringTokenizer tokens = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int a = Integer.parseInt(tokens.nextToken()); int b = Integer.parseInt(tokens.nextToken()); graph[a].add(b); graph[b].add(a); } int[] parent = new int[n + 1]; int[] order = new int[n]; int size = 0; order[size++] = 1; parent[1] = -1; for (int index = 0; index &lt; size; index++) { int vertex = order[index]; for (int next : graph[vertex]) { if (next == parent[vertex]) { continue; } parent[next] = vertex; order[size++] = next; } } long[] in = new long[n + 1]; long[] out = new long[n + 1]; for (int index = n - 1; index &gt;= 0; index--) { int vertex = order[index]; in[vertex] = weight[vertex]; for (int next : graph[vertex]) { if (parent[next] == vertex) { in[vertex] += out[next]; out[vertex] += Math.max(in[next], out[next]); } } } boolean[] selected = new boolean[n + 1]; int[] traversal = new int[n]; int top = 0; traversal[top++] = 1; long optimum = Math.max(in[1], out[1]); while (top &gt; 0) { int vertex = traversal[--top]; int p = parent[vertex]; selected[vertex] = p == -1 ? in[vertex] &gt; out[vertex] : !selected[p] &amp;&amp; in[vertex] &gt; out[vertex]; for (int next : graph[vertex]) { if (parent[next] == vertex) { traversal[top++] = next; } } } List&lt;Integer&gt; answer = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int vertex = 1; vertex &lt;= n; vertex++) { if (selected[vertex]) { answer.add(vertex); } } Collections.sort(answer); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); output.append(optimum).append('\n'); for (int vertex : answer) { output.append(vertex).append(' '); } System.out.println(output); }}

title: BOJ. excellence town (1949)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Graph, Dynamic Programming, excellence town, 우수 마을
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1949 · 한국어 · 日本語A tree has a population weight at each village. Choose villages with the maximum total population subject to the rule that no two adjacent villages are both chosen. The input contains N, then the N population values, followed by the N - 1 undirected roads.Root the tree at village 1 iteratively. Store the order in which vertices are visited; processing that order in reverse guarantees every child is handled before its parent without recursion (and therefore avoids stack overflow on a long path). For each village u, maintain two values: take[u]: the best total when u is selected. Its children cannot be selected, so take[u] = population[u] + sum(skip[child]). skip[u]: the best total when u is not selected. Each child may be selected or skipped, so skip[u] = sum(max(take[child], skip[child])).The answer is max(take[root], skip[root]). Since populations are positive, selecting the root alone is always a positive valid choice; the empty selection cannot improperly win. A single node therefore returns its population. In a path, neighboring choices compete through the two states, and in a star, selecting the center competes with selecting its leaves.The adjacency lists, traversal order, and DP arrays each use O(N) space. Every vertex and edge is processed a constant number of times, for O(N) time. Use long for the DP totals so summed populations do not overflow an int.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); long[] population = new long[n]; StringTokenizer values = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { population[i] = Long.parseLong(values.nextToken()); } ArrayList&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { graph[i] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; i++) { StringTokenizer edge = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int a = Integer.parseInt(edge.nextToken()) - 1; int b = Integer.parseInt(edge.nextToken()) - 1; graph[a].add(b); graph[b].add(a); } int[] parent = new int[n]; int[] order = new int[n]; int size = 0; order[size++] = 0; parent[0] = -1; for (int i = 0; i &lt; size; i++) { int node = order[i]; for (int neighbor : graph[node]) { if (neighbor == parent[node]) { continue; } parent[neighbor] = node; order[size++] = neighbor; } } long[] take = new long[n]; long[] skip = new long[n]; for (int i = n - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { int node = order[i]; take[node] = population[node]; for (int child : graph[node]) { if (parent[child] == node) { take[node] += skip[child]; skip[node] += Math.max(take[child], skip[child]); } } } System.out.println(Math.max(take[0], skip[0])); }}

title: BOJ. Phone Keyboard (5670)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Trie, Data Structure, Phone Keyboard, 휴대폰 자판
snippet: Problem: BOJ 5670 — Phone KeyboardFor each word, the first letter is always typed. After that, type the next letter only when the current trie node has more than one child, or the current prefix is itself a complete word. A complete word needs this extra keystroke to distinguish it from longer words with the same prefix.Insert all words before counting keystrokes. Each trie node records its number of distinct child nodes and whether it ends a word. Thus duplicate insertions do not create extra branches, while a prefix-word collision is counted through the end-of-word flag. Sum each word’s keystrokes and divide by the number of words in that dataset; print each average with exactly two decimal places.The trie construction and all word traversals take O(S) time, where S is the total number of characters across the input words. The trie uses O(S) nodes (with 26 child references per node), and the input words are retained for counting.Javaimport java.util.*;import java.io.*;public class Main { static BufferedReader br; static StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); Trie trie; ArrayList&lt;String&gt; al = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); while(true) { String ss = br.readLine(); if(ss == null || ss.length() == 0) break; int n = toi(ss); if(n == 0) break; trie = new Trie(); al.clear(); for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { String s = br.readLine(); trie.add(s); al.add(s); } int count = 0; for(String s: al) { count += trie.solve(s); } sb.append(String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.2f", (double)count / n)).append("\n"); } print(sb); } static class Trie { Trie[] arr = new Trie[26]; int num = 0; boolean tail; void add(String s) { int l = s.length(); Trie t = this; for(int i = 0; i &lt; l; i++) { int ch = s.charAt(i) - 'a'; if(t.arr[ch] == null) { t.arr[ch] = new Trie(); t.num++; } t = t.arr[ch]; } t.tail = true; } int solve(String s) { Trie t = arr[s.charAt(0) - 'a']; int cnt = 1; for(int i = 1; i &lt; s.length(); i++) { if(t.num + (t.tail ? 1 : 0) &gt; 1) cnt++; t = t.arr[s.charAt(i) - 'a']; } return cnt; } } static int toi(String s) { return Integer.parseInt(s); } static String[] getLine() throws IOException { return br.readLine().split(" "); } static int[] getArr() throws IOException { return Arrays.stream(br.readLine().split(" ")).mapToInt(Integer::parseInt).toArray(); } static &lt;T&gt; void print(T s) { System.out.print(s); } static &lt;T&gt; void println(T s) { System.out.println(s); }}

title: BOJ. Society Service(SNS) (2533)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Graph, Dynamic Programming, Society Service(SNS), 사회망 서비스(SNS)
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2533Root the tree at vertex 0 and build a root-first order iteratively. Processing that order in reverse guarantees that every child has already been processed, so the dynamic program needs no recursive calls and remains safe on a chain of up to 10^6 vertices.For each vertex u, notAdopter[u] is the minimum number of early adopters in its subtree when u is not one. In that case every child must be an early adopter, so this state is the sum of the children’s adopter states. adopter[u] is the minimum when u is an early adopter; each child can then use whichever state is cheaper, in addition to u itself. A leaf therefore has states (0, 1). This also handles the single-vertex tree: its answer is min(0, 1) = 0.The adjacency lists, traversal order, and two DP states use primitive arrays. Each vertex and edge is processed a constant number of times, giving O(N) time and O(N) space.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int[] head = new int[n]; int[] to = new int[2 * (n - 1)]; int[] next = new int[2 * (n - 1)]; java.util.Arrays.fill(head, -1); int edgeCount = 0; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; i++) { int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; to[edgeCount] = b; next[edgeCount] = head[a]; head[a] = edgeCount++; to[edgeCount] = a; next[edgeCount] = head[b]; head[b] = edgeCount++; } int[] parent = new int[n]; int[] order = new int[n]; int size = 1; order[0] = 0; parent[0] = -1; // Build a root-first order without recursion. for (int i = 0; i &lt; size; i++) { int node = order[i]; for (int edge = head[node]; edge != -1; edge = next[edge]) { int child = to[edge]; if (child == parent[node]) { continue; } parent[child] = node; order[size++] = child; } } int[] notAdopter = new int[n]; int[] adopter = new int[n]; for (int i = size - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { int node = order[i]; adopter[node] = 1; for (int edge = head[node]; edge != -1; edge = next[edge]) { int child = to[edge]; if (child == parent[node]) { continue; } notAdopter[node] += adopter[child]; adopter[node] += Math.min(notAdopter[child], adopter[child]); } } System.out.println(Math.min(notAdopter[0], adopter[0])); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int pointer; private int length; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' '); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = in.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[pointer++]; } }}

title: BOJ. Clock pictures (10266)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Clock pictures, KMP, String, 시계 사진들, Review
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/10266한국어 · 日本語A clock has 360,000 possible angular positions, one for each 1/1000-degree unit from 0 through 359999. Store each picture in a Boolean array of this length: an index is true exactly when a clock hand appears at that position. This representation also handles multiple hands at the same position without changing the matching logic.The pictures match when one can be rotated to coincide with the other. Equivalently, the clockwise gaps between consecutive hands must form the same cyclic sequence in both pictures: the starting hand may differ, but the gaps must match in order. Instead of comparing those gaps under every possible starting hand, treat the first Boolean pattern as circular: concatenate it with itself. Every rotation then appears as a length-360000 window in that doubled pattern. Scan only the first 2 * 360000 - 1 positions; these contain every possible window start exactly once without including a redundant start at the duplicated endpoint. KMP checks whether the second pattern occurs in that scan.The prefix table and scan both compare Boolean values directly, so occupied positions remain distinct from empty ones. For C = 360000 positions and N hands, building the arrays and running KMP take O(C + N) time. The position arrays and prefix table use O(C) space; the temporary input arrays use O(N), and the problem constraint N &lt;= 200000 &lt; C keeps the total auxiliary space at O(C).import java.util.*;import java.io.*;public class Main { static BufferedReader br; static int timeNum = 360000; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); br.readLine(); boolean[] clock1 = new boolean[2 * timeNum]; boolean[] clock2 = new boolean[timeNum]; int[] arr = getArr(); for (int e : arr) clock1[e] = clock1[e + timeNum] = true; arr = getArr(); for (int e : arr) clock2[e] = true; print(kmp(clock1, clock2) ? "possible" : "impossible"); } static int[] pi(boolean[] s) { int[] pi = new int[s.length]; int l = 0; for (int r = 1; r &lt; s.length; r++) { while (l &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; s[l] != s[r]) l = pi[l - 1]; if (s[l] == s[r]) { pi[r] = l + 1; l++; } } return pi; } static boolean kmp(boolean[] t, boolean[] s) { int[] pi = pi(s); int r = 0; for (int l = 0; l &lt; 2 * timeNum - 1; l++) { while (r &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; t[l] != s[r]) r = pi[r - 1]; if (t[l] == s[r]) { if (r == s.length - 1) return true; r++; } } return false; } static int toi(String s) { return Integer.parseInt(s); } static int[] getArr() throws IOException { return Arrays.stream(br.readLine().split(" ")).mapToInt(Integer::parseInt).toArray(); } static &lt;T&gt; void print(T s) { System.out.print(s); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 237 E Skiing
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, Graph, Dijkstra, Review, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 237 E — Skiing · 한국어 · 日本語For a route from vertex 1 to a vertex v, let U be the total amount climbed and D the total amount descended. The happiness change along the route is D - 2U: descending by a unit gains one, while climbing by a unit loses two. Since the net height change is H[v] - H[1] = U - D, we have D = U + H[1] - H[v], so the happiness is H[1] - H[v] - U. For a fixed destination, its height is fixed, so maximizing happiness is equivalent to minimizing the total climb U.Assign each undirected road u-v a directed cost in each direction: going from u to v costs max(0, H[v] - H[u]), the climb on that step. Going from v to u similarly costs max(0, H[u] - H[v]). Descending and equal-height steps cost zero. All costs are nonnegative, so Dijkstra’s algorithm finds the minimum accumulated climb from vertex 1 to every reachable vertex. The edge costs are directed even though the roads are undirected; in particular, an equal-height road has zero cost in both directions.For each reachable vertex v, compute H[1] - H[v] - dist[v], where dist[v] is the minimum climb. Unreachable vertices have no route from the start and must not be included. Initialize the answer to zero because vertex 1 is reachable from itself with happiness zero. Distances, height differences, and happiness are stored as long to avoid overflow when adding costs. The running time is O((N + M) log N) and the space usage is O(N + M).Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Arrays;import java.util.List;import java.util.PriorityQueue;public class Main { private static class Edge { int to; long climb; Edge(int to, long climb) { this.to = to; this.climb = climb; } } private static class State implements Comparable&lt;State&gt; { int vertex; long distance; State(int vertex, long distance) { this.vertex = vertex; this.distance = distance; } @Override public int compareTo(State other) { return Long.compare(distance, other.distance); } } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } long nextLong() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); long value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner scanner = new FastScanner(); int n = (int) scanner.nextLong(); int m = (int) scanner.nextLong(); long[] height = new long[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { height[i] = scanner.nextLong(); } List&lt;List&lt;Edge&gt;&gt; graph = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(n); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { graph.add(new ArrayList&lt;&gt;()); } for (int i = 0; i &lt; m; i++) { int u = (int) scanner.nextLong() - 1; int v = (int) scanner.nextLong() - 1; graph.get(u).add(new Edge(v, Math.max(0L, height[v] - height[u]))); graph.get(v).add(new Edge(u, Math.max(0L, height[u] - height[v]))); } long[] distance = new long[n]; Arrays.fill(distance, Long.MAX_VALUE); distance[0] = 0; PriorityQueue&lt;State&gt; queue = new PriorityQueue&lt;&gt;(); queue.add(new State(0, 0)); while (!queue.isEmpty()) { State current = queue.poll(); if (current.distance != distance[current.vertex]) { continue; } for (Edge edge : graph.get(current.vertex)) { long nextDistance = current.distance + edge.climb; if (nextDistance &lt; distance[edge.to]) { distance[edge.to] = nextDistance; queue.add(new State(edge.to, nextDistance)); } } } long answer = 0; for (int v = 0; v &lt; n; v++) { if (distance[v] != Long.MAX_VALUE) { answer = Math.max(answer, height[0] - height[v] - distance[v]); } } System.out.println(answer); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 237 D LR insertion
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 237 D — LR insertion · 한국어 · 日本語The recursive inorder traversal of a tree with up to 500,000 nodes can overflow the call stack. Instead, construct the answer directly with a deque. Start with N, then process S from right to left. For each index i, append i to the back if S[i] is L; otherwise prepend it to the front. The deque then contains the required order.This works because we undo the insertions in reverse order. The last value to be inserted is N, so it is the initial deque. For each earlier i, L means i + 1 was inserted immediately before i, so i belongs at the right end; R means i + 1 was inserted immediately after i, so i belongs at the left end. Each operation extends the corresponding end and preserves the required relative order. Each value is added once, so the time and space complexities are both O(N).Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayDeque;import java.util.Deque;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); String s = input.readLine().trim(); Deque&lt;Integer&gt; order = new ArrayDeque&lt;&gt;(); order.addLast(n); for (int i = n - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { if (s.charAt(i) == 'L') { order.addLast(i); } else { order.addFirst(i); } } StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); for (int value : order) { if (answer.length() &gt; 0) { answer.append(' '); } answer.append(value); } System.out.println(answer); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 237 C kasaka
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 237 C — kasaka · 한국어 · 日本語The only operation is prepending a, so the characters at the end cannot be changed. Let leadingA and trailingA be the lengths of the runs of a at the beginning and end of the string. If leadingA &gt; trailingA, the string cannot become a palindrome: the existing leading as would need more matching as at the end than are available.Otherwise, prepending trailingA - leadingA copies of a balances those runs. The remaining part between the leading and trailing runs must already be a palindrome. Skip both runs with two pointers and compare the characters that remain. If the pointers cross, that middle part is empty or has one character, so it is a palindrome.This also covers strings made entirely of a (the middle is empty) and strings with no a at either end (the entire string is checked). The scan takes O(|S|) time and uses O(1) extra space.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String s = input.readLine(); int left = 0; while (left &lt; s.length() &amp;&amp; s.charAt(left) == 'a') { left++; } int right = s.length() - 1; while (right &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; s.charAt(right) == 'a') { right--; } int leadingA = left; int trailingA = s.length() - 1 - right; if (leadingA &gt; trailingA) { System.out.println("No"); return; } while (left &lt; right) { if (s.charAt(left) != s.charAt(right)) { System.out.println("No"); return; } left++; right--; } System.out.println("Yes"); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 237 B Matrix Transposition
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 237 B — Matrix TranspositionGiven an H by W matrix A, output its transpose B, which has W rows and H columns. Transposition swaps each element’s row and column indices: for every 0 &lt;= i &lt; H and 0 &lt;= j &lt; W, set B[j][i] = A[i][j]. The dimensions need not be equal, so the output must be built with W rows of H values each; this also handles a single row or column naturally.The constraints are small (1 &lt;= H, W &lt;= 100), and every input value can be copied once into its transposed position. The time and storage required are both O(HW). The code reads the dimensions and matrix, then prints each output row with spaces between values and a newline after the row.import java.io.*;import java.util.*;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); StringTokenizer st = new StringTokenizer(br.readLine()); int h = Integer.parseInt(st.nextToken()); int w = Integer.parseInt(st.nextToken()); int[][] a = new int[h][w]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; h; i++) { st = new StringTokenizer(br.readLine()); for (int j = 0; j &lt; w; j++) { a[i][j] = Integer.parseInt(st.nextToken()); } } StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder(); for (int j = 0; j &lt; w; j++) { for (int i = 0; i &lt; h; i++) { if (i &gt; 0) out.append(' '); out.append(a[i][j]); } out.append('\n'); } System.out.print(out); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 237 A Not Overflow
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 237 A — Not Overflow[English] · 한국어 · 日本語The input value can be much larger than a 32-bit signed integer, so read it as a long. A signed 32-bit integer ranges from Integer.MIN_VALUE (-2^31) through Integer.MAX_VALUE (2^31 - 1), inclusive. Compare the long value against both endpoints; print Yes exactly when it lies within that range, and No otherwise. Using inclusive comparisons correctly accepts both boundary values and rejects values just below or above them.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); long value = Long.parseLong(input.readLine().trim()); System.out.println(Integer.MIN_VALUE &lt;= value &amp;&amp; value &lt;= Integer.MAX_VALUE ? "Yes" : "No"); }}

title: BOJ. Find (1786)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Find, String, KMP, KMP Algorithm, 찾기, Review
snippet: BOJ 1786: Find · 한국어 · 日本語Given a text T and a non-empty pattern P, find every occurrence of P in T. KMP avoids rescanning text characters after a mismatch. The problem guarantees that P is non-empty; the search function below also returns no matches for an empty pattern without indexing into it.Prefix function and searchpi[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of P[0..i] that is also a suffix. While building the prefix function, a mismatch shortens the candidate prefix with pi[j - 1]; a match extends it.During search, j is the number of pattern characters currently matched. On a mismatch, fall back to pi[j - 1] and continue matching. When j == P.length(), the match ends at text index i, so its starting position is i - P.length() + 2: this converts the zero-based index to the 1-based position required by the problem. Immediately fall back to j = pi[j - 1] after recording a match. That retains a possible overlap between the matched suffix and the next prefix, so overlapping occurrences are all reported in ascending order.The prefix-function construction and search together take O(|T| + |P|) time. Additional space is O(|P| + K) for the prefix array and the list of K matches.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String text = input.readLine(); String pattern = input.readLine(); List&lt;Integer&gt; positions = findMatches(text, pattern); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); output.append(positions.size()).append('\n'); for (int i = 0; i &lt; positions.size(); i++) { if (i &gt; 0) output.append(' '); output.append(positions.get(i)); } System.out.print(output); } private static List&lt;Integer&gt; findMatches(String text, String pattern) { List&lt;Integer&gt; positions = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); if (pattern.isEmpty()) return positions; int[] pi = prefixFunction(pattern); int matched = 0; for (int i = 0; i &lt; text.length(); i++) { while (matched &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; text.charAt(i) != pattern.charAt(matched)) { matched = pi[matched - 1]; } if (text.charAt(i) == pattern.charAt(matched)) { matched++; if (matched == pattern.length()) { positions.add(i - pattern.length() + 2); matched = pi[matched - 1]; } } } return positions; } private static int[] prefixFunction(String pattern) { int[] pi = new int[pattern.length()]; int matched = 0; for (int i = 1; i &lt; pattern.length(); i++) { while (matched &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; pattern.charAt(i) != pattern.charAt(matched)) { matched = pi[matched - 1]; } if (pattern.charAt(i) == pattern.charAt(matched)) { pi[i] = ++matched; } } return pi; }}

title: BOJ. String square (4354)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, String square, KMP, 문자열 제곱, Review, difficult, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 4354 — String PowerEnglish · 한국어 · 日本語Prefix function and the candidate periodFor each input string s of length L, compute its prefix function pi. At position i, pi[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of s[0..i] that is also a suffix. The last value pi[L - 1] gives the longest border of the whole string. Removing that border leaves a candidate period of length p = L - pi[L - 1].The candidate is a true repeating block only when L is divisible by p. In that case the string consists of exactly L / p copies of the block. Otherwise, no shorter block repeats evenly across the entire string, so the answer is 1. This also handles a one-character string: its prefix-function value is 0, so p = 1 and the answer is 1.Each input line is processed until the line containing only .. The null check also stops safely if input ends; valid problem input includes the terminator. Non-terminator strings are nonempty, so the prefix-function array and its final entry always exist.The prefix function takes O(L) time and O(L) space per string.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); String s; while ((s = input.readLine()) != null &amp;&amp; !s.equals(".")) { output.append(repetitionCount(s)).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static int repetitionCount(String s) { int length = s.length(); int[] prefix = new int[length]; for (int i = 1, matched = 0; i &lt; length; i++) { while (matched &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; s.charAt(i) != s.charAt(matched)) { matched = prefix[matched - 1]; } if (s.charAt(i) == s.charAt(matched)) { matched++; prefix[i] = matched; } } int period = length - prefix[length - 1]; return length % period == 0 ? length / period : 1; }}

title: BOJ. Ant tunnel (14725)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Ant tunnel, 개미굴, Review
snippet: [Link] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/14725Each input line is a path from the root of the ant tunnel. Inserting each token into a trie merges any prefix already present: a node’s children are the next foods that can follow that prefix. A TreeMap stores those children in lexicographic order, so a depth-first traversal visits siblings in the required order without sorting or copying them first.During traversal, append -- once for every edge from the root, followed by the current token and a newline. Thus the root’s children have no prefix dashes, and each deeper level gains exactly one --.If the total number of tokens is S and the trie contains V nodes, insertion takes O(S log V) time in the worst case with ordered maps, and traversal takes O(V) time. The trie uses O(V) space.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.Map;import java.util.TreeMap;public class Main { private static final StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine()); Trie root = new Trie(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { String[] foods = input.readLine().split(" "); Trie node = root; for (int j = 1; j &lt; foods.length; j++) { node = node.children.computeIfAbsent(foods[j], key -&gt; new Trie()); } } root.print(0); System.out.print(output); } private static class Trie { private final TreeMap&lt;String, Trie&gt; children = new TreeMap&lt;&gt;(); private void print(int depth) { for (Map.Entry&lt;String, Trie&gt; child : children.entrySet()) { for (int i = 0; i &lt; depth; i++) { output.append("--"); } output.append(child.getKey()).append('\n'); child.getValue().print(depth + 1); } } }}

title: BOJ. String set (14425)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, String set, 문자열 집합, Review
snippet: Problem: BOJ 14425 — String Set · 한국어 · 日本語The problem gives N strings to store and M strings to check. Count how many check strings are present among the stored strings. Every string contains only lowercase English letters.Hash setStore the input strings in a HashSet&lt;String&gt;. Inserting the same string more than once leaves the set unchanged, so duplicate stored strings do not affect the result. For each query, use contains to test exact whole-string membership and increment the count if it is present. Each query is processed once, so it contributes at most one to the answer.Hash-set insertion and membership checks take expected O(L) time for a string of length L, including hashing and comparing string contents. Across all inserted strings and queries, the expected total time is O(total characters). The set uses O(total characters) space for the distinct stored strings.Javaimport java.util.*;import java.io.*;public class Main { static BufferedReader br; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int[] arr = getArr(); int n = arr[0], m = arr[1]; Set&lt;String&gt; words = new HashSet&lt;&gt;(); for(int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) words.add(br.readLine()); int count = 0; for(int i = 0; i &lt; m; i++) { if(words.contains(br.readLine())) count++; } System.out.print(count); } static int[] getArr() throws IOException { return Arrays.stream(br.readLine().split(" ")).mapToInt(Integer::parseInt).toArray(); }}

title: BOJ. Two Liquid (2470)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Two Liquid, 두 용액, Review
snippet: BOJ 2470: Two Liquids · 한국어 · 日本語Given N distinct solutions, choose two different entries whose sum is closest to zero. Sort the values, then place one pointer at each end. At every step, the two pointed-to entries are a valid candidate; remember the pair whenever its absolute sum is smaller than the best seen. If the sum is negative, move the left pointer right to increase it. If it is positive, move the right pointer left to decrease it. Stop immediately when the sum is zero, since no absolute sum can be smaller.This also handles arrays whose values all have the same sign: the pointers still examine pairs, and the movement rule progresses until all viable improvements have been considered. The indices always satisfy left &lt; right, so the selected entries are distinct. Widen values to long before adding, and compare absolute magnitudes without narrowing or subtracting potentially large values. Sorting costs O(N log N) and the scan costs O(N), for O(N log N) time overall and O(N) space for the sorted copy.Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.Arrays;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int[] values = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { values[i] = input.nextInt(); } Arrays.sort(values); int left = 0; int right = n - 1; int bestLeft = left; int bestRight = right; long bestAbs = Long.MAX_VALUE; while (left &lt; right) { long sum = (long) values[left] + values[right]; long absSum = Math.abs(sum); if (absSum &lt; bestAbs) { bestAbs = absSum; bestLeft = left; bestRight = right; } if (sum == 0) { break; } else if (sum &lt; 0) { left++; } else { right--; } } System.out.println(values[bestLeft] + " " + values[bestRight]); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = input.read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = input.read(); } while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = input.read(); } return sign * value; } }}JavaScriptconst fs = require('fs');const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8').trim().split(/\s+/).map(BigInt);const n = Number(input[0]);const values = input.slice(1, n + 1).sort((a, b) =&gt; (a &lt; b ? -1 : a &gt; b ? 1 : 0));let left = 0;let right = n - 1;let bestLeft = left;let bestRight = right;let bestAbs = null;while (left &lt; right) { const sum = values[left] + values[right]; const absSum = sum &lt; 0n ? -sum : sum; if (bestAbs === null || absSum &lt; bestAbs) { bestAbs = absSum; bestLeft = left; bestRight = right; } if (sum === 0n) { break; } else if (sum &lt; 0n) { left++; } else { right--; }}console.log(`${values[bestLeft]} ${values[bestRight]}`);BigInt keeps both addition and absolute-value comparison exact. The selected indices remain ordered, so the output values are in sorted order and come from two distinct input entries.

title: BOJ. Knapsack problem (1450)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Knapsack problem, Two Pointer, Meet in middle, Binary Search, 냅색문제, Review, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1450 — Knapsack ProblemMeet in the middleEnumerating all subsets of N = 30 items takes O(2^N) time. Instead, split the items into two halves and enumerate each half’s subset sums. Each list has at most 2^(N/2) sums. Sort the right-half sums; for every left-half sum s, binary-search for the first right-half sum greater than C - s. The number of sums before that position is exactly the number of right-half choices that fit with s.Both enumerations start with the empty subset sum 0, so the empty subset is counted exactly once. Do not discard zero sums: every distinct subset is a choice, even if its sum is zero. All item weights are positive, so a half-sum greater than C can never be part of a valid combination; the implementation omits only those sums. Sums and the answer use long, because the answer can reach 2^30.The time complexity is O(2^(N/2) log 2^(N/2)) and the space complexity is O(2^(N/2)).import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Collections;import java.util.List;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); long capacity = input.nextLong(); int middle = n / 2; int[] weights = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { weights[i] = input.nextInt(); } List&lt;Long&gt; leftSums = subsetSums(weights, 0, middle, capacity); List&lt;Long&gt; rightSums = subsetSums(weights, middle, n, capacity); Collections.sort(rightSums); long count = 0; for (long leftSum : leftSums) { count += upperBound(rightSums, capacity - leftSum); } System.out.println(count); } private static List&lt;Long&gt; subsetSums(int[] weights, int from, int to, long capacity) { List&lt;Long&gt; sums = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); sums.add(0L); for (int i = from; i &lt; to; i++) { int currentSize = sums.size(); for (int j = 0; j &lt; currentSize; j++) { long nextSum = sums.get(j) + weights[i]; if (nextSum &lt;= capacity) { sums.add(nextSum); } } } return sums; } private static int upperBound(List&lt;Long&gt; sorted, long value) { int low = 0; int high = sorted.size(); while (low &lt; high) { int middle = low + (high - low) / 2; if (sorted.get(middle) &lt;= value) { low = middle + 1; } else { high = middle; } } return low; } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); int nextInt() throws IOException { return (int) nextLong(); } long nextLong() throws IOException { int c; do { c = input.read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); long value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = input.read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Sum of Two Numbers (3273)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Sum of two numbers, 두 수의 합, Review
snippet: The input contains N distinct positive integers and a target X (1 ≤ N ≤ 100,000, each value is at most 1,000,000). Count unordered pairs of different input elements whose sum is X.Sort the values, then keep two pointers at the smallest and largest remaining values. If their sum is too small, the left value cannot form a target pair with any remaining value, so move the left pointer right. If the sum is too large, the right value cannot pair with any remaining value, so move the right pointer left. On a match, count the pair and move both pointers: this consumes each endpoint, so the same pair cannot be counted again. The pointers meet after every candidate has been considered; if none matched, the count remains zero. This also works for the smallest valid input (N = 1), since the pointers start equal and no pair is counted.The sum is computed as long to avoid overflow. Sorting takes O(N log N) time; the pointer scan takes O(N), for O(N log N) overall and O(N) space for the input array.Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.Arrays;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int[] values = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { values[i] = input.nextInt(); } int target = input.nextInt(); Arrays.sort(values); int left = 0; int right = n - 1; int count = 0; while (left &lt; right) { long sum = (long) values[left] + values[right]; if (sum == target) { count++; left++; right--; } else if (sum &lt; target) { left++; } else { right--; } } System.out.println(count); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = input.read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = input.read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Subsequence sum (1806)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Two Pointer, BOJ, Subsequence sum, 부분합, Review
snippet: BOJ 1806: Subsequence SumAll values are positive, so extending the exclusive right boundary can onlyincrease the window sum, and moving the left boundary can only decrease it.For each right boundary, once the sum reaches S, record that window andadvance the left boundary while the sum remains at least S. Any longerwindow ending at the same position cannot improve the answer. The window is[left, right), so its length is exactly right - left; this also handlessingle-element and first/last windows without special cases. If no windowqualifies, the answer remains 0. The scan takes O(N) time because bothboundaries move only forward, and uses O(N) space for the input values.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); long target = input.nextLong(); int[] values = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { values[i] = input.nextInt(); } int minLength = n + 1; int left = 0; long sum = 0; int right = 0; while (right &lt; n) { sum += values[right++]; while (sum &gt;= target) { minLength = Math.min(minLength, right - left); sum -= values[left++]; } } System.out.println(minLength == n + 1 ? 0 : minLength); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int length; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } private int nextInt() throws IOException { return (int) nextLong(); } private long nextLong() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); long value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}const fs = require('fs');const input = fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8').trim().split(/\s+/).map(Number);const n = input[0];const target = input[1];const values = input.slice(2);let minLength = n + 1;let left = 0;let sum = 0;let right = 0;while (right &lt; n) { sum += values[right++]; while (sum &gt;= target) { minLength = Math.min(minLength, right - left); sum -= values[left++]; }}console.log(minLength === n + 1 ? 0 : minLength);

title: BOJ. Stick (1094)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Stick, 막대기
snippet: BOJ 1094: Stick한국어 · 日本語The target length is between 1 and 64. Since the original stick has length 64, every piece obtainable by repeatedly cutting it in half has a power-of-two length: 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.Write the target in binary. Its set bits express it as a sum of distinct powers of two; each selected piece size is needed exactly once. For example, 23 = 16 + 4 + 2 + 1, so four pieces are needed. Therefore, the answer is the number of set bits in the target. Java’s Integer.bitCount computes this directly without simulating any cuts.The time complexity is O(1), and the extra space complexity is O(1).Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int target = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine()); System.out.println(Integer.bitCount(target)); }}

title: BOJ. Line up (2252)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Topological Sort, Graph, BOJ, Line up, 줄 세우기, Review
snippet: [Problem] https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2252Each input pair A B means that student A must stand before student B. Model this rule as a directed edge A -&gt; B. A valid line is a topological ordering: every edge points from an earlier student to a later one. Students with no ordering relationship can appear in either order, so the result is one valid ordering, not necessarily a unique one.Kahn’s algorithm repeatedly selects a vertex with indegree zero (no remaining prerequisite), outputs it, and removes its outgoing edges. Removing an edge decreases the indegree of its destination; when that value reaches zero, the destination is ready to be output. The queue can contain any number of ready vertices, and every choice preserves the required partial order.Store every input edge in the adjacency list and increment its destination’s indegree for every occurrence. This keeps the two representations consistent even if a constraint is repeated. For a DAG, every vertex is eventually output exactly once. The algorithm takes O(N + M) time and O(N + M) space, where N is the number of students and M is the number of constraints.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayDeque;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;import java.util.Queue;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int studentCount = input.nextInt(); int constraintCount = input.nextInt(); List&lt;List&lt;Integer&gt;&gt; next = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(studentCount); for (int student = 0; student &lt; studentCount; student++) { next.add(new ArrayList&lt;&gt;()); } int[] indegree = new int[studentCount]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; constraintCount; i++) { int before = input.nextInt() - 1; int after = input.nextInt() - 1; next.get(before).add(after); indegree[after]++; } Queue&lt;Integer&gt; ready = new ArrayDeque&lt;&gt;(); for (int student = 0; student &lt; studentCount; student++) { if (indegree[student] == 0) { ready.offer(student); } } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); boolean first = true; while (!ready.isEmpty()) { int student = ready.poll(); if (!first) { output.append(' '); } output.append(student + 1); first = false; for (int after : next.get(student)) { indegree[after]--; if (indegree[after] == 0) { ready.offer(after); } } } System.out.println(output); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int length; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } private int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Determine task (1311)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Bitmask, BOJ, Determine task, 할 일 정하기 1, Review
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1311 — AssignmentThere are N people and N tasks. Assign each person exactly one task, with each task used once, so that the sum of the assignment costs is minimized.Bitmask dynamic programmingLet dp[mask] be the minimum cost after assigning the first Integer.bitCount(mask) people to exactly the tasks whose bits are set in mask. The next person is therefore Integer.bitCount(mask). For every task not yet assigned, set its bit and add that person’s cost:dp[mask | (1 &lt;&lt; task)] = min(dp[mask | (1 &lt;&lt; task)], dp[mask] + cost[person][task]).The empty mask starts with cost 0; all other states start at INF. The full mask contains all tasks, so its value is the answer. This bottom-up form naturally retains zero-cost states. With N &lt;= 20 and costs at most 1,000,000, any complete assignment costs at most 20,000,000, safely below INF = 1,000,000,000.There are 2^N masks and at most N transitions per mask, so the time complexity is O(N * 2^N) and the space complexity is O(2^N).Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { private static final int INF = 1_000_000_000; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int[][] cost = new int[n][n]; for (int person = 0; person &lt; n; person++) { for (int task = 0; task &lt; n; task++) { cost[person][task] = input.nextInt(); } } int stateCount = 1 &lt;&lt; n; int[] dp = new int[stateCount]; for (int mask = 1; mask &lt; stateCount; mask++) { dp[mask] = INF; } for (int mask = 0; mask &lt; stateCount; mask++) { int person = Integer.bitCount(mask); if (person == n) { continue; } for (int task = 0; task &lt; n; task++) { int taskBit = 1 &lt;&lt; task; if ((mask &amp; taskBit) == 0) { int nextMask = mask | taskBit; dp[nextMask] = Math.min( dp[nextMask], dp[mask] + cost[person][task] ); } } } System.out.println(dp[stateCount - 1]); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = input.read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = input.read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Matrix multiplication order (11049)
tags: JavaScript, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Dynamic Programming, BOJ, Matrix multiplication order, 행렬 곱셈 순서
snippet: Problem: BOJ 11049 — Matrix Chain Multiplication · 한국어 · 日本語Interval dynamic programmingLet dp[i][j] be the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed to multiply matrices i through j in order. One matrix needs no multiplication, so dp[i][i] = 0. For an interval containing more than one matrix, choose the final split after matrix k: first compute the left chain i..k, then the right chain k+1..j, and multiply the two resulting matrices.If matrix i has dimensions r_i × c_i, the problem guarantees compatible neighbors: c_i = r_(i+1). Therefore the left result has dimensions r_i × c_(k), the right result has dimensions r_(k+1) × c_j, and compatibility makes their shared dimension c_k = r_(k+1). The final multiplication costs r_i * c_k * c_j. Thus:dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + r_i * c_k * c_j) for i &lt;= k &lt; j.Evaluate intervals from shorter to longer so both subinterval costs are already known. The sentinel is Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, rather than a smaller arbitrary constant that can be less than a valid answer. Under the problem’s bounds the actual costs are below this sentinel and integer arithmetic remains exact. The algorithm takes O(N^3) time and O(N^2) space. When N = 1, the initialized diagonal is the answer, 0.const stream = require('fs').readFileSync(0, 'utf-8').trim().split(/\n/);const n = Number(stream[0]);const dimensions = stream.slice(1).map((line) =&gt; line.split(' ').map(Number));const dp = Array.from({ length: n }, () =&gt; new Array(n).fill(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER),);for (let i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) dp[i][i] = 0;for (let length = 2; length &lt;= n; length++) { for (let start = 0; start + length &lt;= n; start++) { const end = start + length - 1; for (let split = start; split &lt; end; split++) { const cost = dp[start][split] + dp[split + 1][end] + dimensions[start][0] * dimensions[split][1] * dimensions[end][1]; dp[start][end] = Math.min(dp[start][end], cost); } }}console.log(dp[0][n - 1]);

title: BOJ. Consecutive prime sum (1644)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Consecutive prime sum, 소수의 연속합, Review
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1644 — Sum of Consecutive PrimesSieve and sliding windowFirst generate every prime not greater than N with the Sieve of Eratosthenes. Then keep a window of consecutive primes with indices from left through right and its sum. Extend the right end while the sum is less than N; once it reaches or exceeds N, count it if equal and remove the leftmost prime. Because all primes are positive, extending the window can only increase its sum and removing its first element can only decrease it. Thus each pointer only moves forward, and every consecutive-prime range is considered once.If N = 1, there are no primes at most N, so the answer is zero; the same empty-prime-list behavior handles any input with no primes. The input bound is at most 4,000,000, so int safely stores each prime and the count, while long safely stores the running sum.The sieve takes O(N log log N) time and O(N) space. The window scan takes O(P) time for P primes, which is O(N) in the upper bound.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); boolean[] composite = new boolean[n + 1]; for (int p = 2; p &lt;= n / p; p++) { if (!composite[p]) { for (int multiple = p * p; multiple &lt;= n; multiple += p) { composite[multiple] = true; } } } List&lt;Integer&gt; primes = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int value = 2; value &lt;= n; value++) { if (!composite[value]) { primes.add(value); } } int left = 0; long sum = 0; int count = 0; for (int right = 0; right &lt; primes.size(); right++) { sum += primes.get(right); while (sum &gt;= n) { if (sum == n) { count++; } sum -= primes.get(left++); } } System.out.println(count); }}

title: BOJ. Set (11723)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Bitmask, BOJ, Set, 집합
snippet: BitmaskThe set contains only the integers 1 through 20, so store membership in one int. Map value x to bit position x - 1: 1 &lt;&lt; (x - 1) creates a mask with exactly that bit set. Shifts are zero-based, which is why the value must be decremented. The full-set mask is (1 &lt;&lt; 20) - 1, whose low 20 bits are all 1; 0 represents the empty set.For add, OR the mask into the set; for remove, AND with its complement; for check, AND and test for a nonzero result; and for toggle, XOR. all assigns the full mask, while empty clears it. The input guarantees each value command uses 1 &lt;= x &lt;= 20; add and remove are safe even when membership is already in the requested state. Each command takes O(1) time and the set uses O(1) space.Problem linkJavaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { private static final int FULL_SET = (1 &lt;&lt; 20) - 1; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int commandCount = input.nextInt(); int set = 0; StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; commandCount; i++) { String command = input.next(); if (command.equals("all")) { set = FULL_SET; } else if (command.equals("empty")) { set = 0; } else { int x = input.nextInt(); int mask = 1 &lt;&lt; (x - 1); switch (command) { case "add": set |= mask; break; case "remove": set &amp;= ~mask; break; case "check": output.append((set &amp; mask) != 0 ? 1 : 0).append('\n'); break; case "toggle": set ^= mask; break; } } } System.out.print(output); } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } String next() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); StringBuilder token = new StringBuilder(); while (c &gt; ' ') { token.append((char) c); c = read(); } return token.toString(); } int nextInt() throws IOException { return Integer.parseInt(next()); } }}

title: BOJ. Strongly Connected Component (2150)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, SCC, Graph, BOJ, Strongly Connected Component, 트리와 쿼리
snippet: Problem 2150: Strongly Connected ComponentIterative KosarajuKosaraju’s algorithm finds strongly connected components in two depth-first passes. This implementation uses explicit integer stacks rather than recursive calls, so a path of 10,000 vertices cannot exhaust Java’s call stack.The first pass traverses the original graph. Each stack frame stores a vertex and the index of its next outgoing edge; when all outgoing edges have been examined, the vertex is appended to finishOrder. This is the same postorder as recursive DFS. The second pass visits vertices in reverse finishing order in the reversed graph. Each such traversal collects exactly one SCC: the finishing order ensures that no uncollected component reachable in the reversed graph can absorb it, while reverse reachability groups all vertices mutually reachable with its start vertex.Vertices are sorted within each component, then components are sorted by their smallest vertex. The output begins with the component count; each component is printed on one line with its vertices followed by -1, as required by BOJ 2150.Both traversals inspect every vertex and edge a constant number of times. Sorting costs at most O(V log V) across the components; since components partition the vertices, this is bounded by O(V log V). Total time is O(V + E + V log V) and space is O(V + E).import java.io.*;import java.util.*;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int vertexCount = input.nextInt(); int edgeCount = input.nextInt(); List&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new List[vertexCount + 1]; List&lt;Integer&gt;[] reversed = new List[vertexCount + 1]; for (int vertex = 1; vertex &lt;= vertexCount; vertex++) { graph[vertex] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); reversed[vertex] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int i = 0; i &lt; edgeCount; i++) { int from = input.nextInt(); int to = input.nextInt(); graph[from].add(to); reversed[to].add(from); } boolean[] visited = new boolean[vertexCount + 1]; int[] stack = new int[vertexCount]; int[] nextEdge = new int[vertexCount]; int[] finishOrder = new int[vertexCount]; int finishCount = 0; for (int start = 1; start &lt;= vertexCount; start++) { if (visited[start]) { continue; } int top = 0; stack[0] = start; nextEdge[0] = 0; visited[start] = true; while (top &gt;= 0) { int vertex = stack[top]; if (nextEdge[top] &lt; graph[vertex].size()) { int neighbor = graph[vertex].get(nextEdge[top]++); if (!visited[neighbor]) { visited[neighbor] = true; stack[++top] = neighbor; nextEdge[top] = 0; } } else { finishOrder[finishCount++] = vertex; top--; } } } Arrays.fill(visited, false); List&lt;List&lt;Integer&gt;&gt; components = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int i = finishCount - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { int start = finishOrder[i]; if (visited[start]) { continue; } List&lt;Integer&gt; component = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); int top = 0; stack[0] = start; visited[start] = true; while (top &gt;= 0) { int vertex = stack[top--]; component.add(vertex); for (int neighbor : reversed[vertex]) { if (!visited[neighbor]) { visited[neighbor] = true; stack[++top] = neighbor; } } } Collections.sort(component); components.add(component); } components.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(component -&gt; component.get(0))); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder().append(components.size()).append('\n'); for (List&lt;Integer&gt; component : components) { for (int vertex : component) { output.append(vertex).append(' '); } output.append(-1).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int length; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } private int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Tree And Query (15681)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Binary Tree, Dynamic Programming, BOJ, Tree And Query, 트리와 쿼리
snippet: Problem: BOJ 15681 — Tree and Query · 한국어 · 日本語Iterative rooting and reverse-order accumulationRoot the undirected tree at R. During a stack-based traversal, record each node’s parent and append the node to an order array. A node is added to the stack only from its parent, so every node is pushed and recorded exactly once; when an edge leads back to the current node’s parent, skip it. Because a parent is processed before its children are discovered, every parent appears before its children in order.Initialize every subtree size to one, counting the node itself. Then scan order backward and add each node’s accumulated size to its parent. Reversing the parent-before-child order guarantees that all children have contributed before their parent is propagated upward. Thus, when preprocessing finishes, subtreeSize[u] is exactly the number of nodes in the subtree rooted at u. A query is answered directly from this array in O(1) time; this includes the root query (which returns N) and a leaf query (which returns 1).The traversal and accumulation each visit every node once, and reading the N - 1 edges takes O(N) time. Total preprocessing is O(N), followed by O(Q) time for queries. The adjacency lists, parent/order arrays, stack, and subtree-size array use O(N) memory. No recursive calls are used, so a chain of 100,000 nodes does not consume the Java call stack.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int nodeCount = input.nextInt(); int root = input.nextInt(); int queryCount = input.nextInt(); List&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new List[nodeCount + 1]; for (int node = 1; node &lt;= nodeCount; node++) { graph[node] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int i = 0; i &lt; nodeCount - 1; i++) { int u = input.nextInt(); int v = input.nextInt(); graph[u].add(v); graph[v].add(u); } int[] parent = new int[nodeCount + 1]; int[] order = new int[nodeCount]; int[] stack = new int[nodeCount]; int orderSize = 0; int top = 0; stack[top] = root; parent[root] = -1; while (top &gt;= 0) { int node = stack[top--]; order[orderSize++] = node; for (int neighbor : graph[node]) { if (neighbor == parent[node]) { continue; } parent[neighbor] = node; stack[++top] = neighbor; } } int[] subtreeSize = new int[nodeCount + 1]; for (int node = 1; node &lt;= nodeCount; node++) { subtreeSize[node] = 1; } for (int i = orderSize - 1; i &gt; 0; i--) { int node = order[i]; subtreeSize[parent[node]] += subtreeSize[node]; } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; queryCount; i++) { output.append(subtreeSize[input.nextInt()]).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int length; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } private int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Make Bridge(2) (17472)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Graph, Union Find, BOJ, Make Bridge(2), 다리 만들기 2
snippet: BOJ 17472: Make Bridge 2Translations: 한국어 · 日本語ApproachTreat every connected land mass as a vertex of a graph. First label islands with a flood fill. Then inspect every row and every column: from each island cell, continue in that direction across water until the next land cell or the edge of the map. A bridge is a candidate only when it reaches a different island after crossing at least two water cells. This naturally checks horizontal and vertical bridges in both directions. Keep only the shortest candidate for each unordered island pair; longer bridges between the same pair can never help a minimum spanning tree.The candidate bridges form a weighted undirected graph. Kruskal’s algorithm selects the shortest edges that join different components. If it cannot select exactly islandCount - 1 bridges, the islands cannot all be connected and the answer is -1. A single island needs no bridge, so its answer is 0.The grid dimensions are at most 10 × 10, and the number of islands is at most six. Flood fill and the two directional scans take O(NM) time. Sorting at most I(I - 1) / 2 candidate edges takes O(I² log I), for total time O(NM + I² log I) and space O(NM + I²), where I is the number of islands.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayDeque;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Comparator;import java.util.List;import java.util.Queue;public class Main { private static final int[] DR = {-1, 1, 0, 0}; private static final int[] DC = {0, 0, -1, 1}; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int rows = input.nextInt(); int columns = input.nextInt(); int[][] map = new int[rows][columns]; for (int r = 0; r &lt; rows; r++) { for (int c = 0; c &lt; columns; c++) { map[r][c] = input.nextInt(); } } int islandCount = labelIslands(map, rows, columns); if (islandCount == 1) { System.out.println(0); return; } if (islandCount == 0) { System.out.println(-1); return; } int[][] shortest = new int[islandCount][islandCount]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; islandCount; i++) { for (int j = 0; j &lt; islandCount; j++) { shortest[i][j] = Integer.MAX_VALUE; } } for (int r = 0; r &lt; rows; r++) { for (int c = 0; c &lt; columns; c++) { if (map[r][c] == 0) { continue; } for (int direction = 0; direction &lt; 4; direction++) { int nextRow = r + DR[direction]; int nextColumn = c + DC[direction]; int length = 0; while (inside(nextRow, nextColumn, rows, columns) &amp;&amp; map[nextRow][nextColumn] == 0) { length++; nextRow += DR[direction]; nextColumn += DC[direction]; } if (length &gt;= 2 &amp;&amp; inside(nextRow, nextColumn, rows, columns) &amp;&amp; map[nextRow][nextColumn] != map[r][c]) { int from = map[r][c] - 2; int to = map[nextRow][nextColumn] - 2; shortest[from][to] = Math.min(shortest[from][to], length); shortest[to][from] = Math.min(shortest[to][from], length); } } } } List&lt;Edge&gt; edges = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int a = 0; a &lt; islandCount; a++) { for (int b = a + 1; b &lt; islandCount; b++) { if (shortest[a][b] != Integer.MAX_VALUE) { edges.add(new Edge(a, b, shortest[a][b])); } } } edges.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(edge -&gt; edge.length)); DisjointSet sets = new DisjointSet(islandCount); int totalLength = 0; int bridgesUsed = 0; for (Edge edge : edges) { if (sets.union(edge.from, edge.to)) { totalLength += edge.length; bridgesUsed++; if (bridgesUsed == islandCount - 1) { break; } } } System.out.println(bridgesUsed == islandCount - 1 ? totalLength : -1); } private static int labelIslands(int[][] map, int rows, int columns) { int islandCount = 0; Queue&lt;Integer&gt; queue = new ArrayDeque&lt;&gt;(); for (int r = 0; r &lt; rows; r++) { for (int c = 0; c &lt; columns; c++) { if (map[r][c] != 1) { continue; } int label = ++islandCount + 1; map[r][c] = label; queue.offer(r * columns + c); while (!queue.isEmpty()) { int cell = queue.poll(); int currentRow = cell / columns; int currentColumn = cell % columns; for (int direction = 0; direction &lt; 4; direction++) { int nextRow = currentRow + DR[direction]; int nextColumn = currentColumn + DC[direction]; if (inside(nextRow, nextColumn, rows, columns) &amp;&amp; map[nextRow][nextColumn] == 1) { map[nextRow][nextColumn] = label; queue.offer(nextRow * columns + nextColumn); } } } } } return islandCount; } private static boolean inside(int row, int column, int rows, int columns) { return row &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; row &lt; rows &amp;&amp; column &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; column &lt; columns; } private static class Edge { final int from; final int to; final int length; Edge(int from, int to, int length) { this.from = from; this.to = to; this.length = length; } } private static class DisjointSet { private final int[] parent; private final int[] size; DisjointSet(int count) { parent = new int[count]; size = new int[count]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; count; i++) { parent[i] = i; size[i] = 1; } } private int find(int value) { if (parent[value] != value) { parent[value] = find(parent[value]); } return parent[value]; } boolean union(int a, int b) { int rootA = find(a); int rootB = find(b); if (rootA == rootB) { return false; } if (size[rootA] &lt; size[rootB]) { int temp = rootA; rootA = rootB; rootB = temp; } parent[rootB] = rootA; size[rootA] += size[rootB]; return true; } } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int position; private int length; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Planet Tunnel (2887)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Graph, Kruskal, BOJ, Planet Tunnel, explanation, 행성 터널
snippet: Problem: BOJ 2887 — Planet TunnelSparse candidate edges for KruskalFor planets u and v, the tunnel cost is min(|x[u] - x[v]|, |y[u] - y[v]|, |z[u] - z[v]|). Building all N(N - 1) / 2 edges is too expensive when N is large. Instead, sort the planets separately by each coordinate and keep only the edges between consecutive planets in each ordering. This produces at most 3(N - 1) candidates.Why are these candidates enough?
