Consider any edge in a minimum spanning tree, and choose a coordinate whose absolute difference equals that edge’s cost; call that difference d. If another planet lies between its endpoints in this coordinate ordering, the endpoints are not consecutive. Along the ordered sequence between them, every consecutive coordinate gap is strictly less than d. The actual tunnel cost of each such consecutive pair is at most its gap, because the tunnel cost is the minimum of the three coordinate differences. Thus those consecutive edges form a path of edges each strictly cheaper than the chosen MST edge. Removing that edge from the tree creates a cut; the path crosses that cut, so one of its cheaper edges can reconnect the two sides. That contradicts minimality. Therefore each MST edge is consecutive in at least one coordinate ordering and is included among the candidates.For each candidate pair, use its actual tunnel cost (the minimum across all three axes), not necessarily the difference in the axis used to discover the pair. Kruskal’s algorithm sorts these edges and uses a disjoint-set union structure to add an edge only when it joins two components. N = 1 yields no candidates and a total cost of zero. Coordinate differences are computed as long before taking the absolute value, and the accumulated MST cost is also long.Each of the three coordinate sorts takes O(N log N) time and creates O(N) candidates. Sorting the O(N) candidates and running Kruskal take O(N log N) and O(N α(N)), respectively, so the total time is O(N log N) and space is O(N).import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Arrays;import java.util.List;public class Main { static class Planet { int x; int y; int z; int id; Planet(int x, int y, int z, int id) { this.x = x; this.y = y; this.z = z; this.id = id; } } static class Edge implements Comparable&lt;Edge&gt; { int from; int to; long cost; Edge(int from, int to, long cost) { this.from = from; this.to = to; this.cost = cost; } @Override public int compareTo(Edge other) { return Long.compare(cost, other.cost); } } static class DisjointSet { int[] parent; int[] rank; DisjointSet(int size) { parent = new int[size]; rank = new int[size]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; size; i++) { parent[i] = i; } } int find(int value) { if (parent[value] != value) { parent[value] = find(parent[value]); } return parent[value]; } boolean union(int a, int b) { int rootA = find(a); int rootB = find(b); if (rootA == rootB) { return false; } if (rank[rootA] &lt; rank[rootB]) { parent[rootA] = rootB; } else if (rank[rootA] &gt; rank[rootB]) { parent[rootB] = rootA; } else { parent[rootB] = rootA; rank[rootA]++; } return true; } } static long difference(int a, int b) { return Math.abs((long) a - b); } static long tunnelCost(Planet a, Planet b) { return Math.min(difference(a.x, b.x), Math.min(difference(a.y, b.y), difference(a.z, b.z))); } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); Planet[] planets = new Planet[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { planets[i] = new Planet(input.nextInt(), input.nextInt(), input.nextInt(), i); } List&lt;Edge&gt; candidates = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(Math.max(0, 3 * (n - 1))); Planet[] ordered = planets.clone(); for (int axis = 0; axis &lt; 3; axis++) { final int coordinate = axis; Arrays.sort(ordered, (a, b) -&gt; Integer.compare( coordinate(a, coordinate), coordinate(b, coordinate))); for (int i = 0; i + 1 &lt; n; i++) { Planet a = ordered[i]; Planet b = ordered[i + 1]; candidates.add(new Edge(a.id, b.id, tunnelCost(a, b))); } } candidates.sort(null); DisjointSet sets = new DisjointSet(n); long total = 0; int used = 0; for (Edge edge : candidates) { if (sets.union(edge.from, edge.to)) { total += edge.cost; if (++used == n - 1) { break; } } } System.out.println(total); } static int coordinate(Planet planet, int axis) { if (axis == 0) return planet.x; if (axis == 1) return planet.y; return planet.z; } static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream in = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int ptr; private int len; int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } private int read() throws IOException { if (ptr == len) { len = in.read(buffer); ptr = 0; if (len == -1) return -1; } return buffer[ptr++]; } }}한국어 버전 · 日本語版

title: BOJ. MST (Minimum Spanning Tree) (1197)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Graph, BOJ, MST (Minimum Spanning Tree), 최소 스패닝 트리
snippet: Problem · 한국어 · 日本語Kruskal’s algorithmA spanning tree connects every vertex without cycles. A minimum spanning tree (MST) is a spanning tree with the smallest possible total edge weight. Kruskal’s algorithm sorts edges in nondecreasing weight order and accepts an edge exactly when its endpoints are in different components. A disjoint-set union (DSU) structure detects that condition and merges the components.The greedy choice is safe: among the edges joining distinct current components, the lightest can be included in some MST (the cut property). Repeating this choice builds a forest without cycles; once it has V - 1 edges, it is a spanning tree and therefore an MST. Edge weights may be negative: sorting and the cut-property argument still apply, and negative edges should be included whenever they connect separate components.The endpoints are treated symmetrically. Keep both original endpoint values when reading an edge; there is no need to reorder them for Kruskal. Compare weights with Integer.compare rather than subtraction, which can overflow. The total is stored in long, since adding as many as V - 1 int-weight edges may exceed the int range. With E edges and V vertices, sorting dominates at O(E log E) time; DSU operations take amortized O(α(V)) each. Space usage is O(V + E).import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Comparator;import java.util.List;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int vertexCount = input.nextInt(); int edgeCount = input.nextInt(); List&lt;Edge&gt; edges = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(edgeCount); for (int i = 0; i &lt; edgeCount; i++) { int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; int weight = input.nextInt(); edges.add(new Edge(a, b, weight)); } edges.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(edge -&gt; edge.weight)); DisjointSet sets = new DisjointSet(vertexCount); long totalWeight = 0; int acceptedEdges = 0; for (Edge edge : edges) { if (!sets.union(edge.a, edge.b)) { continue; } totalWeight += edge.weight; acceptedEdges++; if (acceptedEdges == vertexCount - 1) { break; } } System.out.println(totalWeight); } private static final class Edge { final int a; final int b; final int weight; Edge(int a, int b, int weight) { this.a = a; this.b = b; this.weight = weight; } } private static final class DisjointSet { private final int[] parent; private final int[] size; DisjointSet(int n) { parent = new int[n]; size = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { parent[i] = i; size[i] = 1; } } private int find(int x) { if (parent[x] != x) { parent[x] = find(parent[x]); } return parent[x]; } boolean union(int a, int b) { int rootA = find(a); int rootB = find(b); if (rootA == rootB) { return false; } if (size[rootA] &lt; size[rootB]) { int temp = rootA; rootA = rootB; rootB = temp; } parent[rootB] = rootA; size[rootA] += size[rootB]; return true; } } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return sign * value; } }}

title: BOJ. Digital Video Disk (9345)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Segment Tree, Data Structure, Digital Video Disk, 디지털 비디오 디스크(DVDs), Review
snippet: Problem link · 한국어 · 日本語Iterative segment tree for DVD permutationsThe array starts as the permutation 0, 1, ..., N - 1. A type-0 operation swaps the values at two positions, and a type-1 operation asks whether the interval [A, B] currently contains exactly the DVDs numbered A through B.For a permutation, that condition is equivalent to min(A..B) == A and max(A..B) == B: the interval has B - A + 1 distinct values, all within [A, B], so if both endpoints occur as its minimum and maximum, every value in between must occur as well. Conversely, if the interval contains exactly the required DVDs, its minimum and maximum are those endpoints.The iterative segment tree stores the minimum and maximum for each segment. Leaves at indices size + i represent array position i, where size is the smallest power of two at least N. Each internal node stores the minimum and maximum of its two children. A point update replaces one leaf and recomputes every ancestor, so after swapping two positions we update both leaves. A range query walks upward over the half-open leaf interval [A, B + 1), combining only the covered nodes. The empty padding leaves are initialized to Integer.MAX_VALUE for minimum and Integer.MIN_VALUE for maximum, so they do not affect a query.Both point updates and range queries take O(log N) time; the tree and permutation use O(N) space. This also handles N = 1: the single leaf answers the interval [0, 0] correctly.Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int testCases = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); while (testCases-- &gt; 0) { int n = input.nextInt(); int operations = input.nextInt(); int[] dvdAt = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { dvdAt[i] = i; } int size = 1; while (size &lt; n) { size &lt;&lt;= 1; } int[] minTree = new int[size &lt;&lt; 1]; int[] maxTree = new int[size &lt;&lt; 1]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; size; i++) { int value = i &lt; n ? dvdAt[i] : Integer.MAX_VALUE; minTree[size + i] = value; maxTree[size + i] = i &lt; n ? dvdAt[i] : Integer.MIN_VALUE; } for (int node = size - 1; node &gt; 0; node--) { minTree[node] = Math.min(minTree[node &lt;&lt; 1], minTree[node &lt;&lt; 1 | 1]); maxTree[node] = Math.max(maxTree[node &lt;&lt; 1], maxTree[node &lt;&lt; 1 | 1]); } for (int operation = 0; operation &lt; operations; operation++) { int type = input.nextInt(); int a = input.nextInt(); int b = input.nextInt(); if (type == 0) { int valueA = dvdAt[a]; int valueB = dvdAt[b]; dvdAt[a] = valueB; dvdAt[b] = valueA; update(minTree, maxTree, size, a, valueB); update(minTree, maxTree, size, b, valueA); } else { int minimum = Integer.MAX_VALUE; int maximum = Integer.MIN_VALUE; int left = size + a; int right = size + b + 1; while (left &lt; right) { if ((left &amp; 1) != 0) { minimum = Math.min(minimum, minTree[left]); maximum = Math.max(maximum, maxTree[left]); left++; } if ((right &amp; 1) != 0) { --right; minimum = Math.min(minimum, minTree[right]); maximum = Math.max(maximum, maxTree[right]); } left &gt;&gt;= 1; right &gt;&gt;= 1; } output.append(minimum == a &amp;&amp; maximum == b ? "YES\n" : "NO\n"); } } } System.out.print(output); } private static void update(int[] minTree, int[] maxTree, int size, int position, int value) { int node = size + position; minTree[node] = value; maxTree[node] = value; for (node &gt;&gt;= 1; node &gt; 0; node &gt;&gt;= 1) { minTree[node] = Math.min(minTree[node &lt;&lt; 1], minTree[node &lt;&lt; 1 | 1]); maxTree[node] = Math.max(maxTree[node &lt;&lt; 1], maxTree[node &lt;&lt; 1 | 1]); } } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } private int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Josephus problem(2) (1168)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Segment Tree, BOJ, Josephus problem(2), 요세푸스 문제 2, Important
snippet: Problem: BOJ 1168 — Josephus Problem 2There are N people in a circle, numbered from 1 to N. Repeatedly remove every K-th person, starting the count at the next person after the previous removal, and print the removal order in the form &lt;a, b, ...&gt;.Fenwick tree of live peopleKeep a Fenwick tree whose value at each position is 1 while that numbered person is still in the circle, and 0 after removal. A prefix sum therefore tells how many live people occur up to a position. The tree supports both removing a person and selecting the person with a given live-person rank in O(log N).Let rank be the zero-based rank of the next person to count among the remaining live people. The person removed in this round has rank (rank + K - 1) % remaining. Find the original number at one-based order rank + 1 using Fenwick binary lifting, then decrement its count. The next count starts at the slot immediately after that removal, which now has zero-based rank rank % (remaining - 1); this is exactly the selected rank modulo the new circle size. Updating that rank only when people remain also handles the final removal without a modulo by zero. For N = 1, the only rank is 0, so the sole output is &lt;1&gt;.Each of the N removals performs one order-statistic search and one update, giving O(N log N) time and O(N) space.Javaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int k = input.nextInt(); FenwickTree live = new FenwickTree(n); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder("&lt;"); int rank = 0; for (int remaining = n; remaining &gt; 0; remaining--) { rank = (int) ((rank + (long) k - 1) % remaining); int person = live.findByOrder(rank + 1); live.add(person, -1); if (remaining &gt; 1) { rank %= remaining - 1; } if (output.length() &gt; 1) { output.append(", "); } output.append(person); } output.append('&gt;'); System.out.print(output); } private static class FenwickTree { private final int size; private final int[] tree; private final int highestPowerOfTwo; FenwickTree(int size) { this.size = size; this.tree = new int[size + 1]; for (int i = 1; i &lt;= size; i++) { tree[i] = i &amp; -i; } int power = 1; while (power &lt;= size / 2) { power &lt;&lt;= 1; } highestPowerOfTwo = power; } void add(int index, int delta) { for (int i = index; i &lt;= size; i += i &amp; -i) { tree[i] += delta; } } int findByOrder(int order) { int index = 0; for (int step = highestPowerOfTwo; step &gt; 0; step &gt;&gt;= 1) { int next = index + step; if (next &lt;= size &amp;&amp; tree[next] &lt; order) { index = next; order -= tree[next]; } } return index + 1; } } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = input.read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = input.read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Data Structure (12899)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Segment Tree, BOJ, Data Structure, 데이터 구조
snippet: Maintain the multiset of inserted values with a Fenwick tree over the fixed value domain [1, 2_000_000]. tree[i] stores the frequency sum for the range ending at i determined by the low bit i &amp; -i. Inserting a value adds one to its frequency; removing a rank first finds the corresponding value and then subtracts one, so equal values remain separate occurrences.To select the k-th smallest value, Fenwick binary lifting builds the answer from the largest power of two downward. At each step it skips a candidate prefix only when its frequency is less than the remaining rank, subtracting that prefix count from k. The final index is the value whose cumulative frequency first reaches the original rank. This works for the first and last valid ranks, including when frequencies are duplicated. Each insertion, selection, and removal takes O(log V) time, where V = 2_000_000; the tree uses O(V) space. Counts fit in int because the number of operations is bounded by the problem input.Problem linkJavaimport java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { private static final int MAX_VALUE = 2_000_000; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int operationCount = input.nextInt(); FenwickTree frequencies = new FenwickTree(MAX_VALUE); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; operationCount; i++) { int operation = input.nextInt(); int valueOrRank = input.nextInt(); if (operation == 1) { frequencies.add(valueOrRank, 1); } else { int value = frequencies.kth(valueOrRank); output.append(value).append('\n'); frequencies.add(value, -1); } } System.out.print(output); } private static final class FenwickTree { private final int[] tree; FenwickTree(int size) { tree = new int[size + 1]; } void add(int index, int delta) { for (int i = index; i &lt; tree.length; i += i &amp; -i) { tree[i] += delta; } } int kth(int rank) { int index = 0; for (int step = Integer.highestOneBit(tree.length - 1); step != 0; step &gt;&gt;= 1) { int next = index + step; if (next &lt; tree.length &amp;&amp; tree[next] &lt; rank) { index = next; rank -= tree[next]; } } return index + 1; } } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) { return -1; } } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Array and Query (16975)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Segment Tree, BOJ, Array and Query, 수열과 쿼리 21
snippet: BOJ 16975: Array and QueryRange addition with a Fenwick difference treeKeep the original values in a base array and represent later additions with a difference array. Adding x to every position in the 1-based inclusive range [left, right] changes only two difference entries: add x at left and -x at right + 1. Therefore, the prefix sum of the difference array at index i is exactly the total added to position i; its current value is base[i] + prefix(i).A Fenwick tree stores those difference values. Each range update performs two Fenwick point updates, and each point query takes one prefix sum, so both operations take O(log N) time. The base array and Fenwick tree use O(N) space. The tree has an extra slot so an update ending at N can safely write the cancellation at N + 1; queries only sum through their requested index. Store values and additions as long so repeated accumulated additions do not overflow int.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); long[] base = new long[n + 1]; for (int i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) { base[i] = input.nextLong(); } Fenwick difference = new Fenwick(n + 1); int queryCount = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; queryCount; i++) { int type = input.nextInt(); if (type == 1) { int left = input.nextInt(); int right = input.nextInt(); long amount = input.nextLong(); difference.add(left, amount); difference.add(right + 1, -amount); } else { int index = input.nextInt(); output.append(base[index] + difference.prefixSum(index)).append('\n'); } } System.out.print(output); } private static final class Fenwick { private final long[] tree; Fenwick(int maximumIndex) { tree = new long[maximumIndex + 1]; } void add(int index, long value) { for (int i = index; i &lt; tree.length; i += i &amp; -i) { tree[i] += value; } } long prefixSum(int index) { long sum = 0; for (int i = index; i &gt; 0; i -= i &amp; -i) { sum += tree[i]; } return sum; } } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { return (int) nextLong(); } long nextLong() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } long value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 235 D - Multiply and Rotate
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 235 D — Multiply and Rotate · 한국어 · 日本語Starting from 1, apply either operation: multiply the current integer by A, or move its last decimal digit to the front. Rotation is allowed only when the number has at least two digits and does not end in 0. Find the minimum number of operations needed to reach N; if it is impossible, print -1. In particular, 120 cannot be rotated: although moving its final 0 to the front and reading the result as an integer would give 12, that operation is forbidden by the problem statement.Treat each integer as a vertex in an unweighted directed graph, with an edge for each valid operation. Breadth-first search from 1 visits states in nondecreasing order of operation count, so the first distance assigned to N is the minimum. A dist array both records that distance and prevents revisiting states. Under the constraints A, N ≤ 10^6, it is sufficient to search states from 1 through 10^6: products are enqueued only when they are at most 10^6, and a rotation of a searched state is also at most 10^6. Thus the array and queue each need 10^6 + 1 entries. Each state has at most two outgoing operations, giving O(10^6) time and space in the bounded state graph.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.Arrays;public class Main { private static final int LIMIT = 1_000_000; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String[] values = input.readLine().split(" "); int a = Integer.parseInt(values[0]); int target = Integer.parseInt(values[1]); int[] distance = new int[LIMIT + 1]; Arrays.fill(distance, -1); int[] queue = new int[LIMIT + 1]; int head = 0; int tail = 0; distance[1] = 0; queue[tail++] = 1; while (head &lt; tail) { int current = queue[head++]; if (current == target) { System.out.println(distance[current]); return; } long product = (long) current * a; if (product &lt;= LIMIT &amp;&amp; distance[(int) product] == -1) { distance[(int) product] = distance[current] + 1; queue[tail++] = (int) product; } if (current &gt;= 10 &amp;&amp; current % 10 != 0) { int place = 1; while (place &lt;= current / 10) { place *= 10; } int rotated = current % 10 * place + current / 10; if (distance[rotated] == -1) { distance[rotated] = distance[current] + 1; queue[tail++] = rotated; } } } System.out.println(-1); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 235 C The Kth Time Query
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 235 C — The Kth Time QueryFor each query (x, k), find the 1-indexed position of the kth occurrence of x in the array. If x occurs fewer than k times, return -1.Build a map from each value to the list of its positions. Scan the array from left to right and append i + 1 to that value’s list. Because positions are appended in increasing order, the list is already ordered, and the answer is the element at index k - 1. If the value is absent or its list has fewer than k entries, output -1.This handles repeated values naturally: the first and last entries answer k = 1 and k equal to the total number of occurrences, respectively. A missing value and any k larger than the occurrence count both produce -1.With expected constant-time hash-map access, constructing the position lists and answering all queries takes expected O(N + Q) time. The position lists store N indices; the map has at most N keys. The output buffer uses O(Q) space, so total auxiliary space is O(N + Q).import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.HashMap;import java.util.Map;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); private StringTokenizer tokens; int nextInt() throws IOException { while (tokens == null || !tokens.hasMoreTokens()) { tokens = new StringTokenizer(reader.readLine()); } return Integer.parseInt(tokens.nextToken()); } } public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int q = input.nextInt(); Map&lt;Integer, ArrayList&lt;Integer&gt;&gt; positions = new HashMap&lt;&gt;(); for (int i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) { int value = input.nextInt(); positions.computeIfAbsent(value, ignored -&gt; new ArrayList&lt;&gt;()).add(i); } StringBuilder answer = new StringBuilder(); for (int query = 0; query &lt; q; query++) { int value = input.nextInt(); int k = input.nextInt(); ArrayList&lt;Integer&gt; occurrences = positions.get(value); if (occurrences == null || occurrences.size() &lt; k) { answer.append(-1).append('\n'); } else { answer.append(occurrences.get(k - 1)).append('\n'); } } System.out.print(answer); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 235 B Climbing Takahashi
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 235 B — Climbing Takahashi한국어 · 日本語The heights form a sequence along the route. Takahashi starts at the first point and continues only while each next height is strictly greater than the current height. At the first equal or lower height, he stops before reaching that point. The answer is the height of the last point he reached.Initialize the answer with the first height, then scan from the second height onward. Update the answer for each increase and stop at the first non-increase. This also handles both edge cases: if every height increases, the answer becomes the final height; if the second height is already equal or lower, the answer remains the first height.The scan takes O(N) time and O(N) extra space for the heights.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); int[] heights = new int[n]; StringTokenizer tokens = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { heights[i] = Integer.parseInt(tokens.nextToken()); } int answer = heights[0]; for (int i = 1; i &lt; n; i++) { if (heights[i] &lt;= heights[i - 1]) { break; } answer = heights[i]; } System.out.println(answer); }}

title: AtCoder. ABC 235 A - Rotate
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, AtCoder, ABC contest
snippet: Problem: AtCoder ABC 235 A — Rotate · 한국어 · 日本語Given a three-digit decimal number, let its hundreds, tens, and ones digits be A, B, and C. The three left cyclic rotations are ABC, BCA, and CAB; output their sum. These are permutations of the three input digits, so repeated digits and zero are handled without any special cases. For example, input 123 produces 123, 231, and 312, whose sum is 666.Read the input as a string to retain the three digit positions even when B or C is 0. Convert each character to a digit and evaluate the place values directly: 100A + 10B + C, 100B + 10C + A, and 100C + 10A + B. Their sum is at most 2997, so an int is sufficient. The time and additional space complexities are both O(1).Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String digits = input.readLine(); int a = digits.charAt(0) - '0'; int b = digits.charAt(1) - '0'; int c = digits.charAt(2) - '0'; int answer = (100 * a + 10 * b + c) + (100 * b + 10 * c + a) + (100 * c + 10 * a + b); System.out.println(answer); }}

title: BOJ. DSLR (9019)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Dynamic Programming, BOJ, DSLR
snippet: ApproachTreat each integer from 0 through 9999 as a vertex in a directed graph. Each of the four DSLR commands is an edge from the current value to the value produced by that command. Since every command costs one step, breadth-first search (BFS) explores states in nondecreasing order of the number of commands from the start.Visit outgoing edges in D, S, L, R order. BFS then discovers shortest paths first and orders equal-length paths by that required command priority. Mark a state visited when it is enqueued; its first parent and command therefore record the highest-priority shortest path to it. Each of the 10,000 states is enqueued at most once. Store only integer states in the queue, and reconstruct the answer by following parent links backward. If the start already equals the target, the reconstructed path has length zero, so the output is an empty line.Each state has four outgoing transitions, giving O(10,000) time and O(10,000) auxiliary space per test case.Problem linkJavaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.Arrays;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { private static final int STATE_COUNT = 10000; public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int testCases = Integer.parseInt(reader.readLine()); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int testCase = 0; testCase &lt; testCases; testCase++) { StringTokenizer input = new StringTokenizer(reader.readLine()); int start = Integer.parseInt(input.nextToken()); int target = Integer.parseInt(input.nextToken()); int[] parent = new int[STATE_COUNT]; Arrays.fill(parent, -1); char[] commandUsed = new char[STATE_COUNT]; int[] queue = new int[STATE_COUNT]; int head = 0; int tail = 0; parent[start] = start; queue[tail++] = start; while (head &lt; tail &amp;&amp; parent[target] == -1) { int current = queue[head++]; int next = current * 2 % STATE_COUNT; if (parent[next] == -1) { parent[next] = current; commandUsed[next] = 'D'; queue[tail++] = next; } next = current == 0 ? 9999 : current - 1; if (parent[next] == -1) { parent[next] = current; commandUsed[next] = 'S'; queue[tail++] = next; } next = current % 1000 * 10 + current / 1000; if (parent[next] == -1) { parent[next] = current; commandUsed[next] = 'L'; queue[tail++] = next; } next = current % 10 * 1000 + current / 10; if (parent[next] == -1) { parent[next] = current; commandUsed[next] = 'R'; queue[tail++] = next; } } char[] reversedPath = new char[STATE_COUNT]; int pathLength = 0; for (int state = target; state != start; state = parent[state]) { reversedPath[pathLength++] = commandUsed[state]; } for (int i = pathLength - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { output.append(reversedPath[i]); } output.append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); }}

title: BOJ. Hide And Sick(4) (13913)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Dynamic Programming, BOJ, Hide And Sick(4), 숨바꼭질 4
snippet: Problem linkFor each position x in the inclusive range [0, 100000], the allowed moves are x - 1, x + 1, and 2 * x, provided the result remains in the range. Every move costs one second, so breadth-first search visits positions in nondecreasing order of the number of moves from the start. The first time a position is discovered, its distance is therefore minimal; recording the position that discovered it as its parent also records a shortest path.The start is enqueued once with distance zero. Each newly discovered in-range position is marked immediately before enqueueing, which prevents duplicate queue entries and cycles (including the self-transition 0 -&gt; 0). When the target is reached, follow parent links from target back to start and reverse that chain. This gives the exact shortest-path length and lists positions in travel order. The search and reconstruction take O(R) time and space, where R = 100001 is the number of positions.import java.io.*;import java.util.*;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); StringTokenizer values = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int start = Integer.parseInt(values.nextToken()); int target = Integer.parseInt(values.nextToken()); int range = 100001; int[] distance = new int[range]; int[] parent = new int[range]; int[] queue = new int[range]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; range; i++) { distance[i] = -1; parent[i] = -1; } int front = 0; int back = 0; queue[back++] = start; distance[start] = 0; while (front &lt; back &amp;&amp; distance[target] == -1) { int current = queue[front++]; int nextDistance = distance[current] + 1; if (current &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; distance[current - 1] == -1) { distance[current - 1] = nextDistance; parent[current - 1] = current; queue[back++] = current - 1; } if (current &lt; 100000 &amp;&amp; distance[current + 1] == -1) { distance[current + 1] = nextDistance; parent[current + 1] = current; queue[back++] = current + 1; } int doubled = current * 2; if (doubled &lt;= 100000 &amp;&amp; distance[doubled] == -1) { distance[doubled] = nextDistance; parent[doubled] = current; queue[back++] = doubled; } } int[] path = new int[distance[target] + 1]; int length = path.length; int position = target; for (int i = length - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { path[i] = position; if (i &gt; 0) { position = parent[position]; } } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); output.append(distance[target]).append('\n'); for (int value : path) { output.append(value).append(' '); } System.out.println(output); }}

title: BOJ. LCS 2 (9252)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, Dynamic Programming, BOJ, LCS 2
snippet: ProblemLet dp[i][j] be the length of the longest common subsequence of the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b. An empty prefix has LCS length zero. If the last characters match, they can extend an LCS of the two preceding prefixes; otherwise an LCS must omit at least one of those last characters:dp[0][j] = dp[i][0] = 0dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1 if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]) otherwiseFill the table from smaller prefixes to larger ones. To recover one LCS, walk backward from (n, m): on a matching pair, record that character and move diagonally; otherwise move to a neighboring cell with the same LCS length. The table invariant guarantees that each diagonal match contributes one character and each non-diagonal move preserves the best attainable length. Reversing the recorded characters gives an LCS of length dp[n][m]. When lengths tie either neighbor is valid, so repeated characters are handled without requiring a unique answer. The algorithm takes O(NM) time and O(NM) space. It prints the length followed by one LCS line; if the length is zero, that second line is blank.import java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String a = input.readLine(); String b = input.readLine(); int n = a.length(); int m = b.length(); int[][] dp = new int[n + 1][m + 1]; for (int i = 1; i &lt;= n; i++) { for (int j = 1; j &lt;= m; j++) { if (a.charAt(i - 1) == b.charAt(j - 1)) { dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1; } else { dp[i][j] = Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]); } } } StringBuilder reversed = new StringBuilder(); int i = n; int j = m; while (i &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; j &gt; 0) { if (a.charAt(i - 1) == b.charAt(j - 1)) { reversed.append(a.charAt(i - 1)); i--; j--; } else if (dp[i - 1][j] &gt;= dp[i][j - 1]) { i--; } else { j--; } } System.out.println(dp[n][m]); System.out.println(reversed.reverse()); }}

title: BOJ. Longest Increasing Subsequence(5) (14003)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Binary Search, Longest Increasing Subsequence(5), 가장 긴 증가하는 부분 수열 5
snippet: Problem linkFor each input value, maintain tails[length], the smallest possible ending value of an increasing subsequence of that length, and tailIndices[length], the input index that supplies that tail. Binary-search for the first tail greater than or equal to the current value (lower_bound) and replace it. Tails are minimal endpoints, not necessarily a subsequence themselves; their indices let us recover a real subsequence.Using the first tail &gt;= value makes the subsequence strictly increasing: an equal value replaces the existing tail instead of extending the sequence. Before changing the tails, set the current element’s predecessor to the index stored for the preceding length. This predecessor is earlier in the input and has a smaller value, because that earlier tail was strictly smaller than the current value. When the search reaches position zero, the element starts a subsequence and has no predecessor. Following predecessor links from the index for the final tail reconstructs one longest subsequence in reverse order.The invariant is that after processing each prefix, tails[k] is the smallest ending value among all increasing subsequences of length k + 1 in that prefix, and tailIndices[k] is an input position having that value. Lower-bound replacement preserves this invariant: a smaller endpoint is at least as extendable, and only a search result at length can increase the best length. The predecessor link captures a valid chain before an endpoint is replaced, so later replacements cannot break reconstruction. Since the input contains at least one value, length is at least one and tailIndices[length - 1] is valid; this also handles N = 1.Each value uses one binary search and constant-time updates, giving O(N log N) time. The input, tails, tail indices, predecessor indices, and reconstructed answer each use O(N) memory.import java.io.*;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final InputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int[] values = new int[n]; int[] tails = new int[n]; int[] tailIndices = new int[n]; int[] predecessor = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { values[i] = input.nextInt(); predecessor[i] = -1; } int length = 0; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { int value = values[i]; int left = 0; int right = length; while (left &lt; right) { int middle = left + (right - left) / 2; if (tails[middle] &gt;= value) { right = middle; } else { left = middle + 1; } } int position = left; if (position &gt; 0) predecessor[i] = tailIndices[position - 1]; tails[position] = value; tailIndices[position] = i; if (position == length) length++; } int[] answer = new int[length]; int index = tailIndices[length - 1]; for (int i = length - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { answer[i] = values[index]; index = predecessor[index]; } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); output.append(length).append('\n'); for (int value : answer) output.append(value).append(' '); System.out.println(output); }}

title: BOJ. Longest Increasing Subsequence(4) (14002)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, LIS Longest Increasing Subsequence(4), 가장 긴 증가하는 부분 수열 4
snippet: Problem linkFor each input value, maintain tails[length], the smallest possible ending value of an increasing subsequence of that length, along with the input index that supplies that tail. Binary-search for the first tail greater than or equal to the current value (lower_bound) and replace it. Tails are minimal endpoints, not necessarily a subsequence themselves; their indices are kept so we can recover a real subsequence.Using the first tail &gt;= value is what makes the subsequence strictly increasing: a value equal to an existing tail replaces it instead of extending the sequence. The predecessor of the current index is the index stored for the preceding length before updating the tails. Following those predecessor links from the final longest tail yields the chosen subsequence in reverse; reversing it gives the answer.The binary search and update take O(log N) per value, so the total time complexity is O(N log N). The input, tails, tail indices, predecessor links, and reconstructed answer each use O(N) space. A singleton produces a sequence of length one; repeated or decreasing values never incorrectly extend the subsequence.import java.io.*;public class Main { private static final class FastScanner { private final InputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int[] values = new int[n]; int[] tails = new int[n]; int[] tailIndices = new int[n]; int[] predecessor = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { values[i] = input.nextInt(); predecessor[i] = -1; } int length = 0; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { int value = values[i]; int left = 0; int right = length; while (left &lt; right) { int middle = left + (right - left) / 2; if (tails[middle] &gt;= value) { right = middle; } else { left = middle + 1; } } int position = left; if (position &gt; 0) predecessor[i] = tailIndices[position - 1]; tails[position] = value; tailIndices[position] = i; if (position == length) length++; } int[] answer = new int[length]; int index = tailIndices[length - 1]; for (int i = length - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { answer[i] = values[index]; index = predecessor[index]; } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); output.append(length).append('\n'); for (int value : answer) output.append(value).append(' '); System.out.println(output); }}

title: BOJ. Make into 1(2) (12852)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Dynamic Programming, Make into 1(2), 1로 만들기 2
snippet: ApproachLet dp[x] be the minimum number of operations needed to reduce x to 1. The final operation from x must be one of subtracting one, dividing by two when divisible, or dividing by three when divisible. Therefore, for each x from 2 through N, compute dp[x] as one plus the minimum dp among those valid predecessors. Every predecessor is smaller than x, so its answer has already been computed.Store the predecessor that produced the minimum alongside each dp[x]. Starting at N, repeatedly follow that predecessor until reaching 1; this reconstructs an optimal path in the required descending order. If multiple candidates have the same minimum, keeping any of them is valid and still yields an optimal path. For N = 1, dp[1] is zero and reconstruction prints just 1.The invariant is that after processing x, dp[x] is the minimum operation count from x to 1, and its recorded predecessor is a valid next value on a path attaining that count. The recurrence checks every possible final operation, and all smaller states are already optimal, so it preserves this invariant. The dynamic-programming table and predecessor array each contain N + 1 entries; filling them and reconstructing the path take O(N) time overall and O(N) space.Problem linkJavaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); int[] dp = new int[n + 1]; int[] predecessor = new int[n + 1]; for (int value = 2; value &lt;= n; value++) { int bestPrevious = value - 1; int bestSteps = dp[bestPrevious]; if (value % 2 == 0 &amp;&amp; dp[value / 2] &lt; bestSteps) { bestPrevious = value / 2; bestSteps = dp[bestPrevious]; } if (value % 3 == 0 &amp;&amp; dp[value / 3] &lt; bestSteps) { bestPrevious = value / 3; bestSteps = dp[bestPrevious]; } dp[value] = bestSteps + 1; predecessor[value] = bestPrevious; } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); output.append(dp[n]).append('\n'); for (int value = n; ; value = predecessor[value]) { output.append(value).append(' '); if (value == 1) { break; } } System.out.print(output); }}

title: BOJ. Iterate Tree (2263)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Segment Tree, Data Structure, Iterate Tree, 트리의 순회, Review
snippet: Problem linkInorder traversal places a node between its left and right subtrees, while postorder traversal ends each subtree with its root. For a current pair of ranges, the last postorder value is therefore the subtree root. A value-to-inorder-index table finds the split in constant time: the number of values to the left of that index determines the left subtree’s postorder range; the remaining preceding values belong to the right subtree.Process these ranges with an explicit stack rather than recursive calls. Each frame stores inclusive inorder and postorder bounds. Emit its root when removing the frame, then push the right frame followed by the left frame so the left subtree is processed next and output is preorder. Every node is indexed and processed once, so time and auxiliary space are both O(N). The explicit stack uses O(N) space in the worst case and avoids overflowing the call stack on a skewed tree.import java.io.*;import java.util.*;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); int[] inorder = new int[n]; int[] postorder = new int[n]; int[] inorderIndex = new int[n + 1]; StringTokenizer values = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { inorder[i] = Integer.parseInt(values.nextToken()); inorderIndex[inorder[i]] = i; } values = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { postorder[i] = Integer.parseInt(values.nextToken()); } int[] inLeftStack = new int[n]; int[] inRightStack = new int[n]; int[] postLeftStack = new int[n]; int[] postRightStack = new int[n]; int top = 0; inLeftStack[top] = 0; inRightStack[top] = n - 1; postLeftStack[top] = 0; postRightStack[top] = n - 1; StringBuilder preorder = new StringBuilder(); while (top &gt;= 0) { int inLeft = inLeftStack[top]; int inRight = inRightStack[top]; int postLeft = postLeftStack[top]; int postRight = postRightStack[top--]; int root = postorder[postRight]; preorder.append(root).append(' '); int rootIndex = inorderIndex[root]; int leftSize = rootIndex - inLeft; if (rootIndex &lt; inRight) { top++; inLeftStack[top] = rootIndex + 1; inRightStack[top] = inRight; postLeftStack[top] = postLeft + leftSize; postRightStack[top] = postRight - 1; } if (inLeft &lt; rootIndex) { top++; inLeftStack[top] = inLeft; inRightStack[top] = rootIndex - 1; postLeftStack[top] = postLeft; postRightStack[top] = postLeft + leftSize - 1; } } System.out.println(preorder); }}

title: BOJ. Bubble Sort (1517)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Segment Tree, Data Structure, Bubble Sort, 버블 소트, Review, difficult
snippet: ProblemA pair of indices (i, j) with i &lt; j and A[i] &gt; A[j] is an inversion. In bubble sort, each adjacent swap exchanges an out-of-order pair; that pair is then in sorted order and is never swapped again. The process removes every inversion, one per swap, so the total number of swaps is exactly the inversion count.Merge sort counts those pairs without simulating swaps. Once the two halves are sorted, if the current right value is smaller than the current left value, it is smaller than every remaining value in the left half. Add the number of remaining left values to the answer before copying that right value. On equality, take the left value first: equal values do not form an inversion. Recursive calls count inversions within each half, while this merge counts only cross-half inversions.The runtime is O(N log N) and the input plus merge buffer use O(N) space. The result uses long, since the maximum inversion count is N(N - 1) / 2.import java.io.*;public class Main { static class FastScanner { private final InputStream input; private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length = 0; private int pointer = 0; FastScanner(InputStream input) { this.input = input; } private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = input.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[pointer++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } } static int[] values; static int[] buffer; static long sortAndCount(int left, int right) { if (right - left &lt;= 1) return 0; int middle = left + (right - left) / 2; long count = sortAndCount(left, middle) + sortAndCount(middle, right); int i = left; int j = middle; int out = left; while (i &lt; middle &amp;&amp; j &lt; right) { if (values[i] &lt;= values[j]) { buffer[out++] = values[i++]; } else { buffer[out++] = values[j++]; count += middle - i; } } while (i &lt; middle) buffer[out++] = values[i++]; while (j &lt; right) buffer[out++] = values[j++]; System.arraycopy(buffer, left, values, left, right - left); return count; } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(System.in); int n = input.nextInt(); values = new int[n]; buffer = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) values[i] = input.nextInt(); System.out.println(sortAndCount(0, n)); }}

title: BOJ. Tree Iteration (1991)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Tree, Data Structure, Tree Iteration, 트리 순회
snippet: Problem linkEach input row gives a node and its left and right child. Labels are single uppercase letters, so an array indexed by label - 'A' stores both children. A missing child is written as . and remains a sentinel in the array; traversal checks for that sentinel before visiting, so absent branches are skipped safely. Starting at A, preorder visits node-left-right, inorder visits left-node-right, and postorder visits left-right-node. The three traversals are appended to separate strings and printed on three lines, in that order.Every node is visited once by each traversal. Since there are three traversals, the total running time is O(N) and the stored child links and output are O(N); the recursive call stack is O(H), where H is the tree height.import java.io.*;import java.util.*;public class Main { static char[][] children = new char[26][2]; static StringBuilder preorder = new StringBuilder(); static StringBuilder inorder = new StringBuilder(); static StringBuilder postorder = new StringBuilder(); static void traverse(int node) { if (node &lt; 0) return; preorder.append((char) ('A' + node)); traverse(children[node][0] == '.' ? -1 : children[node][0] - 'A'); inorder.append((char) ('A' + node)); traverse(children[node][1] == '.' ? -1 : children[node][1] - 'A'); postorder.append((char) ('A' + node)); } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader input = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); int n = Integer.parseInt(input.readLine().trim()); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { StringTokenizer row = new StringTokenizer(input.readLine()); int node = row.nextToken().charAt(0) - 'A'; children[node][0] = row.nextToken().charAt(0); children[node][1] = row.nextToken().charAt(0); } traverse('A' - 'A'); System.out.println(preorder); System.out.println(inorder); System.out.println(postorder); }}

title: BOJ. Diameter of Tree (1967)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Tree, Data Structure, Diameter of Tree, 트리의 지름
snippet: BOJ 1967: Diameter of TreeThe input lists each undirected edge only once. Store it in both endpoints’ adjacency lists, so a traversal can move in either direction; do not add either direction a second time.In a tree, the unique simple path between any two vertices is their distance. Start at any vertex s and traverse the whole tree, recording each vertex’s distance from s. Let a be a farthest vertex. A farthest endpoint of a diameter can be found this way: take a diameter path and consider where the path from s meets it. If s lies on the path, one of its endpoints is at least as far from s as that meeting point, and a farthest vertex is a diameter endpoint. If s lies off the path, the unique path from s joins the diameter at a vertex; by the tree’s unique paths, one of the two diameter endpoints is farthest (ties are harmless). Thus a is an endpoint of some diameter. A second traversal from a finds the greatest distance from that endpoint, which is the diameter length.Both traversals use explicit stacks rather than recursion, so a chain cannot overflow the call stack. The distances and answer use long. The n = 1 case has no edges: both traversals stay at vertex 0 and the answer is 0. Each traversal takes O(n) time, and the adjacency lists and traversal arrays use O(n) space.import java.io.*;import java.util.*;public class Main { static class Edge { final int to; final int weight; Edge(int to, int weight) { this.to = to; this.weight = weight; } } static class Farthest { final int vertex; final long distance; Farthest(int vertex, long distance) { this.vertex = vertex; this.distance = distance; } } static class FastScanner { private final InputStream input = System.in; private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length = 0; private int pointer = 0; private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = input.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[pointer++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } } static Farthest farthest(ArrayList&lt;Edge&gt;[] graph, int start) { int n = graph.length; int[] parent = new int[n]; Arrays.fill(parent, -2); int[] stack = new int[n]; long[] distance = new long[n]; int size = 0; stack[size++] = start; parent[start] = -1; int bestVertex = start; long bestDistance = 0; while (size &gt; 0) { int vertex = stack[--size]; if (distance[vertex] &gt; bestDistance) { bestDistance = distance[vertex]; bestVertex = vertex; } for (Edge edge : graph[vertex]) { if (edge.to == parent[vertex]) continue; parent[edge.to] = vertex; distance[edge.to] = distance[vertex] + edge.weight; stack[size++] = edge.to; } } return new Farthest(bestVertex, bestDistance); } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); ArrayList&lt;Edge&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) graph[i] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; n - 1; i++) { int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; int weight = input.nextInt(); graph[a].add(new Edge(b, weight)); graph[b].add(new Edge(a, weight)); } int endpoint = farthest(graph, 0).vertex; System.out.println(farthest(graph, endpoint).distance); }}

title: BOJ. Diameter of Tree (1167)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Tree, Data Structure, Diameter of Tree, 트리의 지름
snippet: ProblemIn a tree with nonnegative edge weights, start from any vertex and find a farthest vertex a; then find a farthest vertex from a. The distance found in the second traversal is the tree diameter. A farthest vertex from an arbitrary start is a diameter endpoint: if a diameter path is considered alongside the paths from the start, the tree’s unique paths and nonnegative weights imply that one of the diameter endpoints is at least as far from the start, and extending from that farthest vertex reaches a diameter endpoint. This is the standard two-sweep property for weighted trees.The input gives every vertex’s adjacency list, so each undirected edge already appears once from each endpoint. Add only the listed directed adjacency entries; inserting a reverse entry as well would duplicate edges. Each list ends with the vertex number -1, which must be recognized before attempting to read an edge weight. Both traversals use an explicit stack, avoiding recursion depth limits on a long chain. A long distance safely accumulates the path lengths. One vertex has no edges, so both sweeps simply return that vertex with diameter zero.The two traversals and graph construction take O(V) time for V vertices (E = V - 1), and the adjacency lists, stack, and visited/distance arrays use O(V) space.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int vertexCount = input.nextInt(); List&lt;Edge&gt;[] graph = new List[vertexCount]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; vertexCount; i++) { graph[i] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int i = 0; i &lt; vertexCount; i++) { int vertex = input.nextInt() - 1; while (true) { int neighbor = input.nextInt(); if (neighbor == -1) break; long weight = input.nextInt(); graph[vertex].add(new Edge(neighbor - 1, weight)); } } int endpoint = farthestVertex(graph, 0).vertex; long diameter = farthestVertex(graph, endpoint).distance; System.out.println(diameter); } private static Result farthestVertex(List&lt;Edge&gt;[] graph, int start) { int[] stack = new int[graph.length]; boolean[] visited = new boolean[graph.length]; long[] distance = new long[graph.length]; int size = 0; stack[size++] = start; visited[start] = true; int farthest = start; while (size &gt; 0) { int vertex = stack[--size]; if (distance[vertex] &gt; distance[farthest]) { farthest = vertex; } for (Edge edge : graph[vertex]) { if (visited[edge.to]) continue; visited[edge.to] = true; distance[edge.to] = distance[vertex] + edge.weight; stack[size++] = edge.to; } } return new Result(farthest, distance[farthest]); } private static final class Edge { final int to; final long weight; Edge(int to, long weight) { this.to = to; this.weight = weight; } } private static final class Result { final int vertex; final long distance; Result(int vertex, long distance) { this.vertex = vertex; this.distance = distance; } } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } }}

title: BOJ. Binary Search Tree (5639)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Tree, Data Structure, Binary Search Tree, 이진 검색 트리
snippet: BOJ 5639: Binary Search TreeBuild the BST from preorderThe input is the preorder traversal of a binary search tree with distinct keys. In preorder, a node appears before all of its descendants. Keep the path from the root to the most recently visited node in a stack. Its top is the current insertion point. If the next key is smaller than the top key, it is the left child of the top. Otherwise, pop ancestors while their keys are smaller than the new key. The last popped node is the new key’s parent, and the new node is its right child. The remaining stack top, if any, is an ancestor whose right subtree has not yet been left.This stack invariant makes each node enter and leave the stack at most once, so construction takes O(N) time. It also handles either chain without recursion or a sentinel that could be popped past the stack boundary.To produce postorder iteratively, traverse in root-right-left order by pushing the left child before the right child, then write the collected values in reverse. This yields left-right-root. Every node is visited once, so output takes O(N) time and O(N) additional space. Input is read until EOF.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); Node[] ancestors = new Node[100_000]; Node[] traversal = new Node[100_000]; int[] postorder = new int[100_000]; int size = 0; int first = input.nextInt(); if (first == -1) return; Node root = new Node(first); ancestors[size++] = root; int value; while ((value = input.nextInt()) != -1) { Node node = new Node(value); Node parent = null; while (size &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; ancestors[size - 1].value &lt; value) { parent = ancestors[--size]; } if (parent == null) { ancestors[size - 1].left = node; } else { parent.right = node; } ancestors[size++] = node; } int traversalSize = 0; int postorderSize = 0; traversal[traversalSize++] = root; while (traversalSize &gt; 0) { Node node = traversal[--traversalSize]; postorder[postorderSize++] = node.value; if (node.left != null) traversal[traversalSize++] = node.left; if (node.right != null) traversal[traversalSize++] = node.right; } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = postorderSize - 1; i &gt;= 0; i--) { output.append(postorder[i]).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static final class Node { final int value; Node left; Node right; Node(int value) { this.value = value; } } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); if (c == -1) return -1; int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Maximum and Minimum Values (2357)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Segment Tree, Data Structure, Maximum and Minimum Values, 최솟값과 최댓값
snippet: BOJ 2357: Maximum and Minimum ValuesIterative segment treeStore each input value at leaf n + i in two flat arrays. Every internal node combines its children: the minimum tree stores min(left, right), while the maximum tree stores max(left, right). This merge operation is associative, so a range can be split into disjoint tree segments and their results combined in any order.For an inclusive 1-based query [a, b], convert it to the half-open 0-based interval [a - 1, b), represented by tree indices a - 1 + n and b + n. Move the left and right endpoints upward together. Whenever the left endpoint is a right child, include it and advance; whenever the right endpoint is a right boundary, move it left and include it. The sentinels Integer.MAX_VALUE for the minimum and Integer.MIN_VALUE for the maximum are identity values, so they do not affect any real result, including queries containing only negative or only positive values.Building the two trees takes O(N) time and O(N) storage. Each query visits at most O(log N) levels and combines its selected segments in constant time per level, for O(log N) query time.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); int queryCount = input.nextInt(); int[] minTree = new int[2 * n]; int[] maxTree = new int[2 * n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) { int value = input.nextInt(); minTree[n + i] = value; maxTree[n + i] = value; } for (int i = n - 1; i &gt; 0; i--) { minTree[i] = Math.min(minTree[2 * i], minTree[2 * i + 1]); maxTree[i] = Math.max(maxTree[2 * i], maxTree[2 * i + 1]); } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; queryCount; i++) { int left = input.nextInt() - 1 + n; int right = input.nextInt() + n; int minimum = Integer.MAX_VALUE; int maximum = Integer.MIN_VALUE; while (left &lt; right) { if ((left &amp; 1) == 1) { minimum = Math.min(minimum, minTree[left]); maximum = Math.max(maximum, maxTree[left]); left++; } if ((right &amp; 1) == 1) { --right; minimum = Math.min(minimum, minTree[right]); maximum = Math.max(maximum, maxTree[right]); } left &gt;&gt;= 1; right &gt;&gt;= 1; } output.append(minimum).append(' ').append(maximum).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int sign = 1; if (c == '-') { sign = -1; c = read(); } int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value * sign; } }}

title: BOJ. Find Parent In Tree (11725)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Tree, Data Structure, Find Parent In Tree, 트리의 부모 찾기
snippet: BOJ 11725: Find the ParentsRoot the tree with a traversalTreat the undirected input edges as an adjacency list and root the tree at node 1. Starting with 1 in a breadth-first search queue, each newly reached neighbor is a child of the current node. Record that relationship when the neighbor is enqueued, not when it is later removed from the queue. This marks the node as discovered immediately, so no other edge can assign it a second parent. The root is marked before traversal and has no parent to print.A tree has exactly one path from the root to any node, so the first edge that reaches a node is its unique parent edge. After the traversal, print parent[2] through parent[N] in node order. The queue is an integer array, so the traversal uses no recursion and remains safe for a path-shaped tree with maximum depth.There are N - 1 edges. Building the undirected adjacency lists and visiting each vertex and edge takes O(N) time. The adjacency lists, parent array, and queue take O(N) extra space.import java.io.BufferedInputStream;import java.io.IOException;import java.util.ArrayList;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int n = input.nextInt(); @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") ArrayList&lt;Integer&gt;[] graph = new ArrayList[n + 1]; for (int node = 1; node &lt;= n; node++) { graph[node] = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); } for (int edge = 0; edge &lt; n - 1; edge++) { int a = input.nextInt(); int b = input.nextInt(); graph[a].add(b); graph[b].add(a); } int[] parent = new int[n + 1]; int[] queue = new int[n]; int head = 0; int tail = 0; parent[1] = 1; queue[tail++] = 1; while (head &lt; tail) { int current = queue[head++]; for (int neighbor : graph[current]) { if (parent[neighbor] != 0) continue; parent[neighbor] = current; queue[tail++] = neighbor; } } StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int node = 2; node &lt;= n; node++) { output.append(parent[node]).append('\n'); } System.out.print(output); } private static final class FastScanner { private final BufferedInputStream input = new BufferedInputStream(System.in); private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length; private int position; private int read() throws IOException { if (position == length) { length = input.read(buffer); position = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[position++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } }}

title: BOJ. Cycle game (20040)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Union Find, Cycle game, 사이클 게임
snippet: Problem linkProcess the edges in their input order. Before adding an edge (a, b), find the representative of each endpoint’s connected component in the graph formed by earlier edges. If the representatives are equal, a path already connects a and b, so adding this edge creates a cycle; report its one-based turn immediately. Otherwise, merge the two components. This detects the first cycle because a cycle is created exactly when an edge joins vertices already connected by a path. It also correctly detects a self-loop on its own turn and treats the second copy of a parallel edge as cycle-forming.The disjoint-set union structure stores each root’s component size as a negative value. find applies path compression, and union attaches the smaller component below the larger one. Together they give amortized O(α(N)) time per operation, so processing M edges takes O(M α(N)) time and the structure uses O(N) space. The program prints 0 if no edge creates a cycle.import java.io.*;public class Main { static class FastScanner { private final InputStream input; private final byte[] buffer = new byte[1 &lt;&lt; 16]; private int length = 0; private int pointer = 0; FastScanner(InputStream input) { this.input = input; } private int read() throws IOException { if (pointer == length) { length = input.read(buffer); pointer = 0; if (length == -1) return -1; } return buffer[pointer++]; } int nextInt() throws IOException { int c; do { c = read(); } while (c &lt;= ' ' &amp;&amp; c != -1); int value = 0; while (c &gt; ' ') { value = value * 10 + c - '0'; c = read(); } return value; } } static class DisjointSet { private final int[] parentOrSize; DisjointSet(int n) { parentOrSize = new int[n]; for (int i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) parentOrSize[i] = -1; } int find(int node) { if (parentOrSize[node] &lt; 0) return node; return parentOrSize[node] = find(parentOrSize[node]); } boolean union(int a, int b) { int rootA = find(a); int rootB = find(b); if (rootA == rootB) return false; if (parentOrSize[rootA] &gt; parentOrSize[rootB]) { int temp = rootA; rootA = rootB; rootB = temp; } parentOrSize[rootA] += parentOrSize[rootB]; parentOrSize[rootB] = rootA; return true; } } public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(System.in); int n = input.nextInt(); int m = input.nextInt(); DisjointSet dsu = new DisjointSet(n); for (int turn = 1; turn &lt;= m; turn++) { int a = input.nextInt() - 1; int b = input.nextInt() - 1; if (!dsu.union(a, b)) { System.out.println(turn); return; } } System.out.println(0); }}

title: LeetCode. 131. Palindrome Partitioning
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Palindrome Partitioning
snippet: Problem linkPrecompute palindromic substrings, then backtrackLet palindrome[left][right] indicate whether the inclusive substring s[left..right] is a palindrome. A substring is palindromic exactly when its endpoint characters match and either it has at most two characters or its inner substring is also palindromic:palindrome[left][right] = (s.charAt(left) == s.charAt(right)) &amp;&amp; (right - left &lt; 2 || palindrome[left + 1][right - 1])Fill the table with left moving from right to left. This ensures the shorter inner interval has already been computed. The table takes O(n^2) time and space.Backtracking builds one partition from left to right. At each starting index, try every ending index whose substring is marked palindromic, append that substring, and recurse from the next index. When the start reaches n, copy the current path as one complete partition. The base case also handles an empty input: it adds the empty path, so partition("") returns one empty partition. The search has at most 2^(n-1) complete partitions for nonempty input; excluding the result strings and their construction, DFS uses O(n) path/stack space. Overall time is O(n^2 + n * 2^n) in the worst case including the output strings, and auxiliary space is O(n^2).import java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.List;class Solution { public List&lt;List&lt;String&gt;&gt; partition(String s) { int n = s.length(); boolean[][] palindrome = new boolean[n][n]; for (int left = n - 1; left &gt;= 0; left--) { for (int right = left; right &lt; n; right++) { palindrome[left][right] = s.charAt(left) == s.charAt(right) &amp;&amp; (right - left &lt; 2 || palindrome[left + 1][right - 1]); } } List&lt;List&lt;String&gt;&gt; result = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); backtrack(s, 0, palindrome, new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(), result); return result; } private void backtrack( String s, int start, boolean[][] palindrome, List&lt;String&gt; path, List&lt;List&lt;String&gt;&gt; result) { if (start == s.length()) { result.add(new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(path)); return; } for (int end = start; end &lt; s.length(); end++) { if (!palindrome[start][end]) { continue; } path.add(s.substring(start, end + 1)); backtrack(s, end + 1, palindrome, path, result); path.remove(path.size() - 1); } }}

title: BOJ. Friend Network (4195)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Union Find, Friend Network, 친구 네트워크, Review
snippet: Problem linkApproachMap each person’s name to a parent name, and keep a component size for each root. Initially, every newly encountered name is its own root with size one. For a friendship, find both roots and link the smaller component under the larger one, adding their sizes at the surviving root. If the roots are already equal, nothing changes; print that root’s existing size regardless. A fresh disjoint-set structure is created for each test case.The invariant is that every name in a connected friendship group reaches the same root, and the size stored at that root equals the number of people in the group. Path compression preserves the root while shortening future searches; union by size prevents tall trees. Both operations together take amortized O(α(V)) time per friendship, where V is the number of distinct names in the case; including expected constant-time hash-map access, all F friendships take expected O(F α(V)) time. The maps use O(V) space. find is iterative, so even an unusually deep parent chain cannot exhaust the call stack.Javaimport java.io.BufferedReader;import java.io.IOException;import java.io.InputStreamReader;import java.util.HashMap;import java.util.Map;import java.util.StringTokenizer;public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { FastScanner input = new FastScanner(); int testCases = input.nextInt(); StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder(); for (int testCase = 0; testCase &lt; testCases; testCase++) { int friendshipCount = input.nextInt(); DisjointSet friends = new DisjointSet(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; friendshipCount; i++) { String first = input.next(); String second = input.next(); output.append(friends.union(first, second)).append('\n'); } } System.out.print(output); } private static class DisjointSet { private final Map&lt;String, String&gt; parent = new HashMap&lt;&gt;(); private final Map&lt;String, Integer&gt; size = new HashMap&lt;&gt;(); private void add(String name) { if (!parent.containsKey(name)) { parent.put(name, name); size.put(name, 1); } } private String find(String name) { String root = name; while (!parent.get(root).equals(root)) { root = parent.get(root); } while (!name.equals(root)) { String next = parent.get(name); parent.put(name, root); name = next; } return root; } int union(String first, String second) { add(first); add(second); String firstRoot = find(first); String secondRoot = find(second); if (firstRoot.equals(secondRoot)) { return size.get(firstRoot); } if (size.get(firstRoot) &lt; size.get(secondRoot)) { String temporary = firstRoot; firstRoot = secondRoot; secondRoot = temporary; } parent.put(secondRoot, firstRoot); int combinedSize = size.get(firstRoot) + size.get(secondRoot); size.put(firstRoot, combinedSize); size.remove(secondRoot); return combinedSize; } } private static class FastScanner { private final BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader( new InputStreamReader(System.in)); private StringTokenizer tokenizer; String next() throws IOException { while (tokenizer == null || !tokenizer.hasMoreTokens()) { tokenizer = new StringTokenizer(reader.readLine()); } return tokenizer.nextToken(); } int nextInt() throws IOException { return Integer.parseInt(next()); } }}

title: BOJ. Let's go on a trip (1976)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, Union Find, Let's go on a trip, 여행 가자, Review
snippet: Problem linkTreat the cities as vertices and the roads as undirected edges. An itinerary is possible exactly when every city listed in it belongs to the same connected component: then a path exists between each consecutive pair of planned cities, and those paths can be concatenated. A one-city itinerary is therefore always possible.Use a disjoint-set union (DSU) structure. Initially each city is its own set. For every 1 in the adjacency matrix, union the corresponding cities; processing both directions of the undirected matrix is harmless because unioning a pair already in one set does nothing. Then read the itinerary and compare every city’s representative with the first one’s representative.
