title: LeetCode. 9. Palindrome Number
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Palindrome Number
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/palindrome-number/ApproachA negative integer cannot be a palindrome because its minus sign appears only on the left. Any nonzero integer ending in zero also cannot be a palindrome: its reverse would begin with zero, which is not represented in the original integer.Instead of converting the number to a string or reversing all its digits, reverse only the last half of the digits. Each loop iteration removes one digit from x and appends it to reversedHalf. The loop stops when reversedHalf has at least as many digits as the remaining x.At that point, the original number is a palindrome exactly when the two halves match. For an even number of digits, compare x with reversedHalf. For an odd number of digits, the middle digit belongs to reversedHalf but has no counterpart, so discard it with integer division by 10 before comparing.Only half the digits are reversed, so the intermediate value remains within the range of an int, including for Integer.MAX_VALUE. The algorithm takes O(log10 N) time and O(1) extra space.Javaclass Solution { public boolean isPalindrome(int x) { if (x &lt; 0 || (x != 0 &amp;&amp; x % 10 == 0)) { return false; } int reversedHalf = 0; while (x &gt; reversedHalf) { reversedHalf = reversedHalf * 10 + x % 10; x /= 10; } return x == reversedHalf || x == reversedHalf / 10; }}

title: LeetCode. 7. Reverse Integer
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Reverse Integer
snippet: Reverse Integer[Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/reverse-integer/We consume the input one digit at a time, appending each signed digit to thereversed value. Java integer division truncates toward zero, and % keeps thedividend’s sign, so x % 10 is the signed last digit for both positive andnegative inputs. Repeated division removes that digit; zero therefore alsohandles trailing zeroes without special cases.Before multiplying the accumulated value by 10, compare it with the integerbounds divided by 10. At the positive boundary, the last digit may be at most7; at the negative boundary it may be at least -8. These are the finaldigits of Integer.MAX_VALUE and Integer.MIN_VALUE. Rejecting a digit thatwould cross either bound before multiplication prevents overflow. The invariantis that reversed is exactly the reverse of the input digits consumed so far;each iteration preserves it, and the checks ensure every intermediate valuefits in an int.class Solution { public int reverse(int x) { int reversed = 0; while (x != 0) { int digit = x % 10; x /= 10; if (reversed &gt; Integer.MAX_VALUE / 10 || (reversed == Integer.MAX_VALUE / 10 &amp;&amp; digit &gt; 7) || reversed &lt; Integer.MIN_VALUE / 10 || (reversed == Integer.MIN_VALUE / 10 &amp;&amp; digit &lt; -8)) { return 0; } reversed = reversed * 10 + digit; } return reversed; }}Each iteration consumes one decimal digit, so the time complexity isO(log |x|). Only a fixed number of integer variables are used, giving O(1)extra space.

title: LeetCode. 6. ZigZag Conversion
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, ZigZag Conversion
snippet: ZigZag ConversionTraverse the string one character at a time, appending each character to the builderfor its current row. The row index moves down or up by one; reverse the direction whenit reaches the first or last row. Reading the row builders from top to bottom producesthe converted string. If there is only one row, or at least as many rows as characters,the zigzag has no diagonal movement and the input is already the result.This simulates the zigzag directly: each character is assigned to the row it occupiesin the traversal, and appending rows in order is exactly the required readout.For N characters, each character is appended and read once, so time is O(N).The row builders and result use O(N) space.[Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/zigzag-conversion/import java.util.ArrayList;class Solution { public String convert(String s, int numRows) { if (numRows == 1 || numRows &gt;= s.length()) { return s; } ArrayList&lt;StringBuilder&gt; rows = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(numRows); for (int row = 0; row &lt; numRows; row++) { rows.add(new StringBuilder()); } int currentRow = 0; int direction = 1; for (int i = 0; i &lt; s.length(); i++) { rows.get(currentRow).append(s.charAt(i)); if (currentRow == 0) { direction = 1; } else if (currentRow == numRows - 1) { direction = -1; } currentRow += direction; } StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder(s.length()); for (StringBuilder row : rows) { result.append(row); } return result.toString(); }}

title: LeetCode. 5. Longest Palindromic Substring
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Longest Palindromic Substring
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-palindromic-substring/ApproachEvery palindrome has either a character at its center (an odd-length palindrome) or agap between two characters at its center (an even-length palindrome). For each index,expand outward from both kinds of centers while the characters match. Each expansionchecks all palindromes with that center.Keep the best answer as a half-open interval [bestStart, bestEnd). When a longerpalindrome is found, replace the interval; otherwise leave it unchanged so an existingmaximum-length answer is preserved. An empty string has no centers and returns theempty substring.Javaclass Solution { public String longestPalindrome(String s) { int bestStart = 0; int bestEnd = 0; for (int center = 0; center &lt; s.length(); center++) { int left = center; int right = center; while (left &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; right &lt; s.length() &amp;&amp; s.charAt(left) == s.charAt(right)) { left--; right++; } if (right - left - 1 &gt; bestEnd - bestStart) { bestStart = left + 1; bestEnd = right; } left = center; right = center + 1; while (left &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; right &lt; s.length() &amp;&amp; s.charAt(left) == s.charAt(right)) { left--; right++; } if (right - left - 1 &gt; bestEnd - bestStart) { bestStart = left + 1; bestEnd = right; } } return s.substring(bestStart, bestEnd); }}For each of the N positions, two expansions can each inspect up to N characters, sothe time complexity is O(N²). The indices use only constant extra space, giving O(1)extra space.

title: LeetCode. 4 Median of Two Sorted Arrays
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Median of Two Sorted Arrays
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/median-of-two-sorted-arrays/Binary-search partitionBecause both arrays are sorted, we can divide them into left and right halves without merging them. The left half must contain exactly half of the elements (rounded up), and every value on the left must be less than or equal to every value on the right.Binary-search a partition in the shorter array, nums1. If i elements of nums1 belong to the left half, then j = (m + n + 1) / 2 - i elements of nums2 must belong there, where m and n are their lengths. Adjust i until the two boundary comparisons establish the invariant: left1 &lt;= right2 left2 &lt;= right1Here, left1 and left2 are the greatest values on each array’s left side, and right1 and right2 are the least values on each right side. Once both comparisons hold, the combined left side contains the smaller half of the values. For an odd total length, its greatest value is the median. For an even total length, the median is the average of that value and the least value on the combined right side.When a partition leaves one side of an array empty, use Integer.MIN_VALUE or Integer.MAX_VALUE as the corresponding boundary. These sentinels let the same comparisons handle partitions at either end without special cases. At least one input array is non-empty, as required by the problem.Each binary-search step halves the search interval in the shorter array, so the time complexity is O(log(min(m, n))); only a constant number of values are stored, giving O(1) extra space.class Solution { public double findMedianSortedArrays(int[] nums1, int[] nums2) { if (nums1.length &gt; nums2.length) { int[] temp = nums1; nums1 = nums2; nums2 = temp; } int m = nums1.length; int n = nums2.length; int half = (m + n + 1) / 2; int low = 0; int high = m; while (low &lt;= high) { int i = low + (high - low) / 2; int j = half - i; int left1 = i == 0 ? Integer.MIN_VALUE : nums1[i - 1]; int right1 = i == m ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : nums1[i]; int left2 = j == 0 ? Integer.MIN_VALUE : nums2[j - 1]; int right2 = j == n ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : nums2[j]; if (left1 &lt;= right2 &amp;&amp; left2 &lt;= right1) { if ((m + n) % 2 == 1) { return Math.max(left1, left2); } long middleValues = (long) Math.max(left1, left2) + Math.min(right1, right2); return middleValues / 2.0; } else if (left1 &gt; right2) { high = i - 1; } else { low = i + 1; } } throw new IllegalArgumentException("Input arrays must be sorted."); }}

title: LeetCode. 3. Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-substring-without-repeating-characters/Sliding windowMaintain a window s[left..right] and a set containing its characters. The invariant is that the active window contains no repeated UTF-16 char. When the character at right is already in the set, remove characters from the left (advancing left) until that duplicate is gone. Then add the new character, and update the longest valid window length.The window is always unique after each iteration. Any longest substring ending at the current position must start at or after left, because earlier starts would include a repeated character. Recording the current window length therefore considers the best valid substring ending there.Java implementationimport java.util.HashSet;import java.util.Set;class Solution { public int lengthOfLongestSubstring(String s) { Set&lt;Character&gt; window = new HashSet&lt;&gt;(); int left = 0; int best = 0; for (int right = 0; right &lt; s.length(); right++) { char current = s.charAt(right); while (window.contains(current)) { window.remove(s.charAt(left)); left++; } window.add(current); best = Math.max(best, right - left + 1); } return best; }}Each character enters and leaves the window at most once, so the time complexity is O(N). The set stores at most the distinct characters in the input, giving O(min(N, alphabet)) auxiliary space under LeetCode’s character set.

title: LeetCode. 16. 3Sum Closest
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, JavaScript, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, 3Sum Closest
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/3sum-closest/Given an integer array nums and an integer target, return the sum of three distinct elements that is closest to target. If multiple sums are equally close, any of them may be returned.Sort the array in ascending order, then fix each element in turn as the first of the three. Search for the other two with pointers starting at opposite ends of the remaining range. If their sum is below the target, move the left pointer right to increase it; if it is above, move the right pointer left to decrease it. At each step, keep whichever of the current sum and the best sum so far is closer to the target. Return immediately on an exact match, since no closer result is possible.Skipping duplicate fixed values and pointer values avoids repeating equivalent cases without changing the possible closest result; it is an optimization, not a correctness requirement.Sorting takes O(N log N), and the two-pointer scan takes O(N) for each fixed element, for O(N²) total time. The search uses O(1) extra space apart from sorting. JavaScript’s Array.prototype.sort may use engine-dependent auxiliary memory, so the total auxiliary-space bound including the sort depends on the runtime implementation rather than being universally O(1)./** * @param {number[]} nums * @param {number} target * @return {number} */function threeSumClosest(nums, target) { nums.sort((a, b) =&gt; a - b); let closest = nums[0] + nums[1] + nums[2]; for (let i = 0; i &lt; nums.length - 2; i++) { if (i &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; nums[i] === nums[i - 1]) continue; let left = i + 1; let right = nums.length - 1; while (left &lt; right) { const sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]; if (Math.abs(sum - target) &lt; Math.abs(closest - target)) { closest = sum; } if (sum === target) return sum; if (sum &lt; target) { const leftValue = nums[left]; while (left &lt; right &amp;&amp; nums[left] === leftValue) left++; } else { const rightValue = nums[right]; while (left &lt; right &amp;&amp; nums[right] === rightValue) right--; } } } return closest;}

title: LeetCode. 15. 3Sum
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, 3Sum
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/3sum/ApproachSort the array, then fix each index i in turn and search the suffix with twopointers, left = i + 1 and right = nums.length - 1. The sorted order letsthe pointers move monotonically: if the three-value sum is below zero, everypair using the current left and a smaller right endpoint is also too small,so advancing left is safe. If the sum is above zero, every pair using thecurrent right and a larger left endpoint is also too large, so decrementingright is safe. On a zero sum, record the triplet and move both pointers.Skip an index when its value matches the previous fixed value, so the samefirst value is not searched again. After recording a triplet, skip repeatedvalues at both pointers before continuing; this prevents producing the samevalue triplet more than once. Since the array is sorted, once nums[i] &gt; 0,all later values are positive too and the search can stop.Javaimport java.util.ArrayList;import java.util.Arrays;import java.util.List;class Solution { public List&lt;List&lt;Integer&gt;&gt; threeSum(int[] nums) { Arrays.sort(nums); List&lt;List&lt;Integer&gt;&gt; result = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; nums.length - 2; i++) { if (nums[i] &gt; 0) { break; } if (i &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) { continue; } int left = i + 1; int right = nums.length - 1; while (left &lt; right) { long sum = (long) nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]; if (sum &lt; 0) { left++; } else if (sum &gt; 0) { right--; } else { result.add(Arrays.asList(nums[i], nums[left], nums[right])); while (left &lt; right &amp;&amp; nums[left] == nums[left + 1]) { left++; } while (left &lt; right &amp;&amp; nums[right] == nums[right - 1]) { right--; } left++; right--; } } } return result; }}Sorting takes O(N log N) time and the fixed-index two-pointer searches takeO(N²) time overall. Sorting is in place; its implementation uses O(log N)workspace. The returned triplets require O(K) output space, where K is thenumber of triplets.

title: LeetCode. 12.Integer to Roman
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Integer to Roman
snippet: [Link] https://leetcode.com/problems/integer-to-roman/Greedy denomination selectionRoman numerals use descending place-value symbols, with six subtractive forms: IV and IX represent 4 and 9, XL and XC represent 40 and 90, and CD and CM represent 400 and 900. At each step, take the largest denomination no greater than the remaining value, append its symbol, and subtract that denomination. Repeat until nothing remains. The table includes the subtractive forms as single denominations, so the greedy choices directly produce the standard notation.This representation is canonical for the problem’s range, 1 through 3999. For values below 4000, the thousands digit is represented by zero to three Ms. Each remaining decimal digit is independent: hundreds use C, D, CD, CM; tens use X, L, XL, XC; and ones use I, V, IV, IX. For any such digit, greedily choosing its largest applicable form yields exactly its conventional single Roman digit representation. Since the place values do not overlap and each digit has a unique such form, concatenating them from largest to smallest gives the unique canonical numeral. The descending table performs precisely this decomposition.Javaclass Solution { public String intToRoman(int num) { int[] values = { 1000, 900, 500, 400, 100, 90, 50, 40, 10, 9, 5, 4, 1 }; String[] symbols = { "M", "CM", "D", "CD", "C", "XC", "L", "XL", "X", "IX", "V", "IV", "I" }; StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i &lt; values.length; i++) { while (num &gt;= values[i]) { result.append(symbols[i]); num -= values[i]; } } return result.toString(); }}Let $L$ be the output length. The loop appends each output symbol once, so the time complexity is $O(L)$ and the result storage is $O(L)$. Under the problem constraint $1 \le num \le 3999$, the output length is bounded by a constant.

title: LeetCode. 11. Container With Most Water
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, LeetCode, Container With Most Water
snippet: Problem: Container With Most WaterTwo pointersFor indices l &lt; r, the two vertical lines hold water up to the shorter line. Their container has width r - l, height min(height[l], height[r]), and area\[(r-l)\times\min(\text{height}[l],\text{height}[r]).\]Start with the widest possible pair, the two ends of the array. Record its area, then move the pointer at the shorter line inward. If both heights are equal, move either one; this implementation moves the right pointer.Why discarding the shorter side is safeSuppose height[l] &lt;= height[r]. The current area is bounded by height[l]. If we keep l and choose any narrower container with a right endpoint r' &lt; r, its width is smaller than r-l, and its height is at most height[l] because the left wall is still height[l]. Thus its area cannot exceed the current area. No better answer can use l with a right endpoint inside r, so we can discard l and advance it. The symmetric argument applies when the right side is shorter. Repeating this leaves no potentially better pair unexamined.Java implementationThe constraints are 2 &lt;= height.length &lt;= 10^5 and 0 &lt;= height[i] &lt;= 10^4. Therefore the largest possible area is at most (10^5 - 1) * 10^4 = 999,990,000, which fits in a signed 32-bit int; both the multiplication and the result can use int.class Solution { public int maxArea(int[] height) { int left = 0; int right = height.length - 1; int best = 0; while (left &lt; right) { int area = (right - left) * Math.min(height[left], height[right]); best = Math.max(best, area); if (height[left] &lt; height[right]) { left++; } else { right--; } } return best; }}Each pointer moves inward at most N times, so the algorithm takes O(N) time and uses O(1) extra space.

title: Sort. Radix Sort
tags: Code Block, Code Snippet, JavaScript, Radix, Code, Radix, Sort, Coding Interview
snippet: Radix SortTime Complexity: O(nw) (n: number of items, w: length of item) Space Complexity: O(n+w)function radixSort(array) { let max; let digitArr = new Array(10); for (let i = 0; i &lt; digitArr.length; i++) { digitArr[i] = []; } for (let i = 0; i &lt; array.length; i++) { if (i === 0 || max &lt; array[i]) { max = array[i]; } } let maxLog = Math.log10(max) + 1; for (let digit = 1; digit &lt;= maxLog; digit++) { let digit10 = Math.pow(10, digit); let tempArr = []; for (let i = 0; i &lt; array.length; i++) { if (digit === 1) { digitArr[array[i] % digit10].push(array[i]); } else { tempDigit = Math.floor(((array[i] % digit10) * 10) / digit10); digitArr[tempDigit].push(array[i]); } } for (let i = 0; i &lt; digitArr.length; i++) { while (digitArr[i].length !== 0) { tempArr.push(digitArr[i][0]); digitArr[i].shift(); } } array = [...tempArr]; } return array;}

title: BOJ. Tree (4803)
tags: Java, Algorithm, Coding Interview, BOJ, DFS, Tree, Data Structure
snippet:
ApproachA tree is a connected, acyclic undirected graph. For each unvisited vertex, run a breadth-first traversal to visit its entire connected component. Mark each vertex visited when it is enqueued so that no vertex is queued more than once. While traversing an edge, the neighbor is a cycle witness if it has already been visited and is not the current vertex’s parent; the parent edge itself is the one edge that must be ignored in an undirected graph. Count the component only if no cycle was found.
